statement: In the stated Deligne indexing, the codimension-one Gysin differential enters E_1^{0,24}=H^{24}(X), making the relevant graded piece a cokernel; the attempt instead reverses the arrow and calls it a kernel.

For a smooth complex stack of dimension 20, the dual compact-support degree corresponding to H^{24}(U) is 16, not 24; therefore Gr^W_{24}H_c^{24}(U) is not an equivalent reformulation of the stated Borel-Moore target.

The asserted decorated graph spectral sequence, its degree formula, edge twists, automorphism action including orientation signs, and its relation to the Deligne spectral sequence are not constructed; consequently the claim that every positive-edge contribution is Tate is not established by the supplied range discussion.

For the forgetful Leray analysis of ordinary weight-28 degree-28 cohomology on M_{g,n}, a pure summand of V^{\otimes n} has coefficient weight n; base cohomology H^p(M_g, L) then has weights at least p+n. Labeling a candidate source as W_p H^p(M_g,V^{\otimes n}) while also adding fiber weight n is an inconsistent weight convention and, under the standard VHS convention, the piece W_p vanishes.

Kunneth summands of H^*(C^n), including H^1(C)^{\otimes n}, are not automatically direct summands of R^*f_*Q for f:M_{g,n}->M_g. Pairwise diagonals have complex codimension 1, so passage to the ordered configuration space requires explicit Gysin/restriction sequences; without them, V^{\otimes n} is only a candidate before diagonal relations, not a coefficient system on M_g.

The ordered configuration fiber F(C,n) is nonproper, so R^q f_*Q carries mixed Hodge modules/variations. Non-Tate contributions to gr^W_{2d-16} H^{2d-16}(M_{g,n}) may sit in any Leray bidegree (p,q) with p+q=2d-16 compatible with the weight filtration; isolating a single slot such as (2d-16-n,n) does not exhaust possible non-Tate sources.

For the forgetful map of smooth DM stacks M_{g,n}->M_g, geometric fibers over curves with nontrivial automorphisms are configuration stacks rather than the scheme F(C,n). Claims that identify R^q f_*Q with the monodromy representation on H^q(F(C,n)) must either restrict to the automorphism-free locus and control the complement, or work entirely with stacky direct images.

A disproof of the degree-16 pure-Tate reduction for a listed open pair requires an exhibited nonzero non-Tate summand in the exact group W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{g,n}) (equivalently its ordinary realization after the dimension-dependent Poincare twist). A Leray-source heuristic with unproved survival, nonvanishing, and differentials does not meet that bar.

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction. contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001-THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0005: the SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 excerpt packaged in C66-001-v4 gives vanishing of H^0(C, omega_C tensor W_{f_i}|_C^vee(Gamma)) whenever 0 > 4 f_i + n - 2g - 14, which for g=6, f_2=5 reads n < 6; hence n <= 5 is automatic and n = 6 is exactly the degree-zero boundary, reproducing c(6) = 5. The finding therefore sits exactly at the campaign case and nowhere else. INSTANTIATION VERIFIED FROM SUPPLIED PRIMARY EXCERPT: deg(W_5|_C) = 4g + 12 - 4f = 16, deg(W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}) = 16 - (2g-2) = 6 = n, and deg(omega_C tensor W_5|_C^vee(Gamma)) = 2g - 2 - 16 + 6 = 0, so the packet's own C66-GEO-Z instruction ('Six-point failure locus: O_C(Gamma) isomorphic to W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}') is precisely the geometric-point form of a degree-zero triviality condition. The finding is thus about the packet's own construction, not about a misreading of SRC-0004. LIVE PRIMARY VERIFICATION OF THE MATHEMATICAL POINT. (1) Pagani-Ricolfi-van Zelm, 'Pullbacks of universal Brill-Noether classes via Abel-Jacobi morphisms' (arXiv:1809.10668), Section 3.2: the universal Brill-Noether locus is given set-theoretically as {(C,P,L) : L in Pic^d C, h^0(C,L) > r} and then 'can be endowed with the scheme structure of the (g-d+r)-th Fitting ideal of R^1 pi_* L'. The scheme structure is IMPOSED by a separate definition, not read off from the set-theoretic description; and the paper's entire subject is the comparison of such universal classes with their pullbacks along Abel-Jacobi morphisms, treated as a substantive computation (Thom-Porteous class w^r_d = Delta^{(r+1)}_{g-d+r} c(-R pi_* L)). This is direct primary support for the finding's core assertion. (2) arXiv:2405.17689 constructs Brill-Noether ideals BN^k(F) = I_{r_0-k}(delta^0), the ideal of (r_0-k)x(r_0-k) minors of delta^0 for a base-change complex (a bounded complex of locally free sheaves with R^i (f_T)_* F_T iso h^i(E_T^.) for any T -> Y), i.e. exactly the determinantal/Fitting structure the finding names. Its Lemma 3.5 records that Fitting ideals commute with FLAT base change. IMPORTANTLY, on direct retrieval of the paper text I could NOT verify any statement that these ideals or loci commute with ARBITRARY base change; a search-engine summary asserted this, and I am recording that assertion as UNVERIFIED and not relying on it. The flat-versus-arbitrary distinction is exactly where 'over an arbitrary base' in the finding bites, so this failure to verify strengthens rather than weakens the finding. (3) Expected-codimension arithmetic (reviewer-computed, elementary): chi(N) = 1 - g = -5 forces complex ranks e and e+5, so the rank-drop locus has expected codimension g = 6, matching the codimension of the identity section in the relative Picard. The two structures therefore agree in expected codimension while remaining a priori distinct as schemes - necessary but not sufficient, which is the finding's precise content. DISCHARGE ROUTE AND ITS CURRENT STATUS. The natural discharge is: (a) base-change stability of the Brill-Noether/Fitting degeneracy structure, so that the relative locus is the pullback of a universal determinantal locus in Pic^0; plus (b) reducedness of that universal degree-zero locus, which for a single smooth curve follows from the Riemann-Kempf/Petri tangent-space formula T_L W^r_d = (Im mu_0)^perp, since for L = O_C the map mu_0 : H^0(O_C) tensor H^0(K) -> H^0(K) is an isomorphism and the tangent space is zero. Step (b) is reviewer-supplied: every PDF retrieval attempted in this session (ACGH-derived lecture notes, arXiv:1809.10668 PDF) returned undecodable binary and could not be text-verified, so no primary citation for the tangent-space computation is recorded here. Step (a) is likewise not verified beyond the flat case. Consequently the finding names a genuinely OPEN obligation on C66-GEO-Z, not a formality already settled in the cited literature. NON-DUPLICATION. Distinct from FND-0005 (Z nonempty by Riemann-Roch): FND-0005 establishes that the underlying point set is nonempty, which is the complementary statement and is exactly what does NOT determine scheme structure - the two findings compose rather than merge. Distinct from FND-0022 (localization spectral sequence codimension shifts and Tate twists for gonality/Brill-Noether stratification of M_{g,n-1}), FND-0020 and FND-0037 (mixed weights and non-split extension of R^1 pi_* Q), FND-0031/FND-0032/FND-0033/FND-0034 (weight spectral sequence corner, CGP top weight, pure-row semisimplicity, non-separating divisor Mbar_{5,8}), and FND-0003 (genus-7 unbalanced residual pencil breaking a finite-etale model). None concerns scheme structure of a relative degeneracy locus. Merge target: none. AUDIT LIMITATIONS DISCLOSED. (i) The supplied proof/findings.jsonl snapshot contains only FND-0001 through FND-0034; FND-0035, FND-0036 and FND-0037 appear only as packet entries and as duplicate_of targets, and FND-0038 through FND-0046 are absent entirely. Non-duplication is therefore certified against FND-0001..FND-0034 plus the ten adjudicated findings listed in packet C66-001-v4, and NOT against any finding in the FND-0038..FND-0045 range, which I could not inspect. (ii) The section-10 text of SRC-0004 could not be retrieved (ar5iv returned only through Section 1.4; PDF and abs retrievals gave no section content), so whether Canning-Larson themselves treat the failure locus scheme-theoretically is UNRESOLVED; this does not affect the adjudication, because the finding targets the campaign's C66-GEO-Z construction, whose fibrewise phrasing is verified directly from the supplied packet. (iii) Two Grok 4.5 helper workers (W-8dd9b4cf42bf, W-09149da767e3) were dispatched and both returned only a single preamble sentence with no substantive content; they contributed nothing to this audit and no claim here rests on them. Remaining worker budget was not spent. VERDICT. Promote from candidate to corroborated on independent verification by a second engine (claude; codex was the sole prior reviewer and is excluded for this task) of the degree-zero instantiation at (6,6), of the imposed-rather-than-derived nature of the Fitting scheme structure on Brill-Noether/Abel-Jacobi loci, and of the flat-versus-arbitrary base-change gap. Evidence class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source. Recommended kind refinement: the finding functions as a rigor obligation on C66-GEO-Z rather than an approach-killing obstruction, and any attempt claiming to have 'constructed Z' must exhibit the scheme structure it is using and the comparison, plus an integrality hypothesis on the fibres.

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001-THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It constrains the C66-GEO-Z construction, not any recorded claim, and is compatible with corroborated FND-0005 (for L = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} on a genus-6 tetragonal curve, deg L = 6 and chi(L) = 6-6+1 = 1, so h^0(L) = 1 + h^1(L) >= 1 fibrewise) and with the packet's own directives at C66-GEO-H0 ('Stratify by h^0(W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1})') and the S_6-cover directive ('Model ordered distinct reduced divisors as a finite etale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in the relative linear system'), both of which presuppose a well-defined relative linear system over strata on which h^0 varies. PRIMARY VERIFICATION. (1) Semicontinuity: Stacks Project Lemma 36.32.1 (tag 0BDN) states that for f: X -> S proper of finite presentation and F of finite presentation and flat over S, the function s -> dim_{kappa(s)} H^i(X_s, F_s) commutes with arbitrary base change, is upper semi-continuous, and has locally constructible level sets; jumping loci are therefore genuine closed conditions, not artifacts removable by shrinking. (2) The only unconditional positive criterion in that section is Lemma 36.32.4 (tag 0D4E): if R^i f_* F = 0 for i > 0, then f_* F is locally free and its formation commutes with arbitrary base change - for a relative curve and a line bundle this is exactly the h^1 = 0 hypothesis. The two classical licenses are Grauert (h^i constant on a reduced base implies R^i locally free with base change; Hartshorne, Algebraic Geometry, GTM 52, III.12.9) and Grothendieck's cohomology-and-base-change theorem (Hartshorne III.12.11; Mumford, Abelian Varieties, II.5; EGA III 7.7.5). (3) Mechanism: formation of Proj(Sym F) commutes with base change for any quasi-coherent F, so the fibre of P(pi_* L) = Proj(Sym pi_* L) at s is P((pi_* L) tensor kappa(s)), which is the intended |L_s| = P(H^0(X_s, L_s)) if and only if the comparison map (pi_* L) tensor kappa(s) -> H^0(X_s, L_s) is an isomorphism. At a jumping point neither Grauert nor the R^1 = 0 criterion applies, so that isomorphism is unlicensed; the finding is correct as stated and is standard relative algebraic geometry, not a novel obstruction. (4) Repair: the relative divisor/Hilbert scheme Div^d_{C/S} (the relative symmetric product for a smooth relative curve) with the Abel-Jacobi map to Pic^d_{C/S} has fibre over [L_s] the complete linear system |L_s| by construction and needs no base-change hypothesis (Kleiman, 'The Picard scheme', arXiv:math/0504020; ACGH, Geometry of Algebraic Curves I, Ch. IV, where W^r_d and G^r_d are constructed determinantally precisely because h^0 jumps, and C_d -> Pic^d is a projective bundle only in the non-jumping range d >= 2g-1). BITE IN THE CAMPAIGN CASE. deg L = 6 < 2g-1 = 11, so the projective-bundle range does not apply; with chi(L) = 1 from FND-0005 one has h^1(L_s) = h^0(L_s) - 1, so jumping is equivalent to effectivity of the degree-4 bundle omega_C tensor L^{-1} = omega_C^2 tensor W_5^{-1}, a live condition on genus-6 tetragonal curves (effective degree-4 classes form W_4 of dimension 4 inside the 6-dimensional Pic^4, and 4 is the gonality). Where h^0 jumps to 2 the true fibre |L_s| is a P^1 while pi_* L has generic rank 1, so a naive P(pi_* L) records at most a point over that stratum; the ordered-divisor S_6 etale cover would then be formed over the wrong space exactly along the stratum the packet asks to isolate, and component/dimension/stabilizer counts for Z (C66-GEO-Z, C66-GEO-COMP) inherited from it would be wrong there. This audit does not decide whether that stratum is nonempty - that is subproblem C66-GEO-H0 - and the finding is correctly phrased conditionally ('when h^0(L) jumps'). SCOPE SHARPENINGS (no weakening of the finding): the obstruction binds over arbitrary, including non-reduced, bases and on any non-constant-h^0 stratum; it does not bind on the h^0 = 1, h^1 = 0 open, where tag 0D4E licenses the naive construction; and it is a construction-validity obstruction only, not a refutation of the existence or nonemptiness of Z (FND-0005 stands). RELATION TO SIBLINGS. Distinct from corroborated FND-0046, which concerns whether a fibrewise equivalence upgrades to a scheme-theoretic identification of the relative evaluation-failure locus with an Abel-Jacobi incidence locus and demands comparison of determinantal/Fitting scheme structures; FND-0047 concerns the prior step, namely whether the ambient relative linear system is the correct object at all when h^0 jumps. The two compose rather than duplicate: adopting the Div/Abel-Jacobi repair urged by FND-0047 still leaves the Fitting-structure comparison demanded by FND-0046. Also distinct from FND-0022 (localization/Gysin bookkeeping for stratifications) and FND-0033 (pure-corner semisimplicity). Merge target: none. VERDICT: promote from candidate to corroborated on independent verification; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source; reviewer engines become codex plus claude, independently. PROVENANCE CAVEATS: the read-only workspace provides no shell, so SHA-256 digests of the retrieved pages could not be computed; content_sha256 is reported as null rather than filled with an unverified value. Retrieval of the two arXiv records covers the abstract pages (title, authors, version, DOI) and not internal section content; the Div/Abel-Jacobi and textbook citations (Kleiman, ACGH, Hartshorne, Mumford, EGA III) are bibliographic pointers to standard results, while the two Stacks Project lemma statements were verified verbatim. ATT-0019 and REV-0024 are absent from the workspace and were not re-audited; the promotion rests on the mathematical statement, not on attempt-local provenance.

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001-THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. PRIMARY VERIFICATION OF CLAUSE 1 (the identification of the group). SRC-0001 (Payne, arXiv:2605.20453v1, retrieved live) states verbatim that 'the subspace W_k H^k(M_{g,n}) is the image of H^k(Mbar_{g,n}) under restriction to the open subspace parameterizing smooth curves. It carries a pure Hodge structure of weight k' — this is Deligne (Hodge II) lowest-weight theory and confirms the finding's opening equation exactly. SRC-0002 (CLP, arXiv:2307.08830v3, retrieved live) supplies the same content in right-exact form, H^{k-2}(bd~M_{g,n}) -> H^k(Mbar_{g,n}) -> W_k H^k(M_{g,n}) -> 0, i.e. THM-0003. Arithmetic checks for (6,6): d=3*6-3+6=21; ordinary degree 2d-16=26 with weight 26, so weight=degree and the piece is pure and lowest in its degree; Chow codimension 26/2=13; Poincare duality on the smooth proper stack gives 2*21-26=16, so H^{26}(Mbar_{6,6}) is dual to the CONJ-0001 group H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6}) up to Q(-21). All agree with the TASK target block. VERIFICATION OF CLAUSE 2 (no supplied identification; assuming one is not independent). (i) The relevant implication runs one way only: SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3 — the paper's own 'key new technical statement' — is 'if X is smooth and has the CKgP, then W_k H^k(X) is algebraic', and algebraic generation of a pure weight-2p piece forces Tate type ⊕Q(-p). So an identification of W_26 H^26(M_{6,6}) with a complex generated by algebraic cotangent/gluing classes would immediately discharge the (6,6) case. An input that yields the conclusion in one step is not an independent input, which is precisely the finding's point. (ii) That input is unavailable at (6,6): THM-0005's CKgP marking bound for g=6 is n<=c(6)=5 < 6 (SRC-0002 Thm 1.10 independently confirms the analogous genus-7 bound, 'For n<=3, the moduli space M_{7,n} has the CKgP and R*(M_{7,n})=A*(M_{7,n})'). (iii) Tautological generation of H^{2p}(Mbar_{g,n}) for ALL (g,n) is known per SRC-0001 only for p<=2, and for p=3 only when g not in {7,8,9}; codimension p=13 is far outside every published range. (iv) Decisively, SRC-0001 records that non-tautological classes occur in even degree and that 'all known examples occur in codimension 11 and higher' — codimension 13 lies inside the regime where decorated-strata generation is known to fail in general, so it cannot be assumed for free at (6,6). (v) Current state of the art confirms the finding rather than refuting it: Bergstrom-Wennink (arXiv:2603.26962v1, 27 Mar 2026), the closest published attempt to run exactly this program, computes weight-graded pieces of H^*(M_{g,n}) from Deligne's weight spectral sequence only under the explicit ASSUMPTIONS that Pixton's relations are complete and that 'the E_1-page consists only of tautological cohomology', verified case-by-case and not proved; and its range 2g+n<=12 excludes (6,6) (2*6+6=18). SCOPE SHARPENINGS (mild, non-defeating, recorded for the record). (a) 'Circular' is best read as 'requires an input at least as strong as the conclusion': algebraic/tautological generation implies Tate type but is strictly stronger (a non-tautological ALGEBRAIC class is still Tate), so the defect is petitio principii in the practical sense unless the attempt's only warrant for the generation claim is the target itself. (b) One inclusion is genuinely available and should not be denied by future reviewers: the codimension-13 tautological/strata classes do push into W_26 H^26(M_{6,6}) and their span is Tate; what no supplied argument provides is SURJECTIVITY onto the pure piece. (c) The closing clause is correctly framed as a statement about the supplied argument — it does not, and must not be read to, provide positive evidence that a non-Tate weight-26 summand exists. MERGE ANALYSIS — do not merge. Against FND-0031 (corroborated, group 'pure-corner-depth-one-only'): that finding blocks the Deligne weight SS / Getzler-Kapranov complex at the m=0 corner on the ground that its E_1 terms are cohomology of boundary strata and the m=0 term is the still-unknown compactified group, i.e. unknown-input circularity. FND-0048 blocks a different object — the ALGEBRAIC decorated strata complex, all of whose terms are Tate by construction — on the ground of an unproven generation hypothesis. Different mechanism, different attempt (ATT-0020/REV-0025 vs ATT-0014/REV-0021), and the two are complementary rather than redundant. Against FND-0032: its own adjudication (FAUD-0008) explicitly carved out the decorated case, 'the obstruction is to the undecorated top-weight regime; decorated/lower-weight graph-complex methods are outside this finding and not ruled out here'; FND-0048 fills exactly that flagged gap. Against FND-0033 (semisimplicity/extensions) and FND-0034 (nonseparating divisor Mbar_{5,8}): unrelated content. Against retired FND-0021/FND-0028: those were retired for misdescribing CKgP as a property of the compactification, contradicting THM-0005's open-M_{g,n} scope; FND-0048 makes no such claim and is the correct-scope statement of the residual gap, so it is not a revival of a retired item. Merge target: none. LIMITATIONS DECLARED. (1) ATT-0020 and REV-0025 are absent from this read-only workspace, so the audit verifies the mathematical content and the packet-level absence of any such identification in C66-001-v4; it does not re-audit ATT-0020's section-level provenance, which is not required for the mathematical promotion. (2) Independent extraction of SRC-0002 Table 1 was unreliable (one retrieval reported g=6 bound n<=3, a follow-up reported no Table 1 in the introduction); this is non-load-bearing because n=6 exceeds the bound under either the packet value c(6)=5 or the lower reading, so the compatibility argument with THM-0005 holds regardless. The packet value c(6)=5 is retained. (3) No SHA-256 digests are recorded: this workspace exposes no shell or hashing tool, so content_sha256 is set to null rather than fabricated; URLs, arXiv ids/versions and retrieval date are accurate. (4) Grok 4.5 helper workers were deliberately NOT dispatched: TASK.json sets excluded_engines=['grok'] and the finding's originating reviewer_engines=['grok'], so any grok assistance would void independence. CONCLUSION: promote FND-0048 from candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source on independent live verification of the lowest-weight identification (SRC-0001), the CKgP-to-algebraicity implication and boundary sequence (SRC-0002), the codimension-11-and-higher non-tautological regime (SRC-0001), and the assumption-laden, out-of-range state of the art for decorated weight-spectral-sequence computations (arXiv:2603.26962v1).

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty and the statement opposes none of CONJ-0001, THM-0001-THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. Primary verification of the surviving core. (1) SRC-0001 (Payne, arXiv:2605.20453v1) section 5 records verbatim that 'The prediction that H^k(Mbar_{g,n}) is pure Tate for even k <= 20 is confirmed for k <= 14, but the cases 16, 18, and 20 remain open', confirming OBS-0001 and hence that any Q(-13) assertion at the (6,6) open input is CONJ-0001, not a theorem. (2) The implication actually available in the corpus runs one way only: SRC-0002 (Canning-Larson-Payne, arXiv:2307.08830v3) Lemma 4.3 states that if X is smooth and has the CKgP then W_k H^k(X) is algebraic, i.e. algebraicity implies Tate type, never the converse. The converse is the Hodge conjecture: SRC-0001 section 2.1 states the rational cycle class map cyc^k: Z^k(X) tensor Q -> H^{2k}(X) intersect H^{k,k}(X) is (conjecturally) surjective, and section 3.1 records that tautological generation of H^{2k}(Mbar_{g,n}) is what yields the Hodge conjecture in codimension k. (3) The algebraicity input is genuinely unavailable at (6,6): THM-0005 gives c(6)=5 < 6, so M_{6,6} lies outside published CKgP coverage (spot-checked against SRC-0002, which cites M_{3,n} CKgP for n <= 11 and proves M_{7,n} CKgP for n <= 3, matching c(3)=11 and c(7)=3). The surviving core of FND-0049 -- that a degree-26 class need not be an algebraic codimension-13 cycle, so concluding type Q(-13) without controlling h^{p,26-p} for p != 13 upgrades a prediction to a theorem -- is therefore correct and non-vacuous. Two clauses do NOT survive audit. (a) 'Equating ordinary degree 26 with Chow codimension 13' is not itself an error: the cycle class map CH^13 -> H^{26} doubles degree, so 26 <-> 13 is the standard and correct dictionary, and RED-0001's arithmetic is internally consistent (d = 3g-3+n = 21, ordinary degree 2d-16 = 26 = 2(d-8), codimension d-8 = 13). SRC-0001 (Payne, arXiv:2605.20453, Section 2.4) states verbatim: 'For odd k<11, we have H^k(Mbar_{g,n})=0 for all g and n. Given this vanishing, the generalized Hodge and Tate conjectures hold vacuously in these cases.' The same survey (Section 5) records 'The prediction that H^k(Mbar_{g,n}) is pure Tate for even k<=20 is confirmed for k<=14, but the cases 16, 18, and 20 remain open,' consistent with OBS-0001 and CONJ-0001; SRC-0002 Theorem 1.5(3) ('R H^*(Mbar_{g,n}) contains H^k(Mbar_{g,n}), for even k<=14, for all g and n') matches THM-0002 with no separate vanishing caveat, i.e. vacuity is treated as automatic, not as a defect. G is a polarizable pure Q-Hodge structure of weight -16, and polarizable pure Q-HS of fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category; the only Tate object of weight -16 is Q(8), so G is a direct sum of Q(8) if and only if G has no simple summand other than Q(8). SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6, quoted verbatim in the packet, gives deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f and deg(omega_C tensor W_f|_C^vee(Gamma)) = 2g-2-(4g+12-4f)+n = 4f+n-2g-14. F's rank and degree were re-derived here independently as ker(Sym^2 E -> phi_*L^2) with L = omega_C tensor phi^*O(2): rank 6-4 = 2 and degree 36-27 = 9. Hence f_1+f_2 = 9, 'balanced' is exactly (4,5) as the packet states, the first unbalanced type is (3,6), and its expected codimension is h^1(P^1, End F) = h^1(O(-3)) = 2. (a) Smooth plane quintics with the g^1_4 = |O(1)-p| given by projection from a point p on C. Using phi_*O_C = O + sum_i O(-e_i) with sum e_i = g+d-1 = 9 and h^0(kD) = (k+1) + sum_i max(0, k-e_i+1): h^0(D) = 2 forces all e_i >= 2, and h^0(2D) = h^0(O_C(2H)) - 2 = 6-2 = 4 forces exactly one e_i = 2, hence E = (2,3,4). The relative quadric containing C is then Bl_p P^2 = F_1 inside P(E^vee): for E = (2,3,4) and f = 6 the symmetric matrix has entry degrees 2e_i-f giving determinant a nonzero constant (fibrewise smooth conic bundle), and P(G) with Sym^2 G ~ E forces G = O(a)+O(a+1), i.e. F_1; blowing down recovers the plane quintic and the projection pencil. So F = (3,6), unbalanced. This locus has dimension 12+1 = 13 in the 15-dimensional degree-4 Hurwitz space (dim = b-3 = 18-3, the packet's own count), i.e. codimension 2, matching h^1(End F) = 2; Riemann-Hurwitz gives deg R = 18, so these covers are generically simply branched and genuinely lie in that Hurwitz space. Plane quintics have gonality exactly 4 -- consistent with corroborated FND-0022, which already records that the genus-6 gonality-4 open contains the Brill-Noether-special plane quintic locus -- so this witness is in scope under every reading of the campaign's tetragonal setting. (b) Secondary witness: genus-6 trigonal curves as (4,3) curves on P^1 x P^1, where h^0(2D) = 3 forces E = (3,3,3) and the constant conic is a relative quadric with f = 6, again F = (3,6), on a 13-dimensional locus (the trigonal locus), codimension 2. The genus-6 special-loci picture used here (trigonal, plane quintic, hyperelliptic as the non-general strata) matches the Penev-Vakil genus-6 stratification returned by live search and the in-packet corroborated FND-0022. (3) THE UNBALANCED FAILURE LOCUS IS NONEMPTY AND NOT LOWER-DIMENSIONAL. On F = (3,6) with (g,n) = (6,6): the f_1 = 3 summand has obstruction degree 4(3)+6-12-14 = -8 < 0 and vanishes identically (same mechanism as corroborated FND-0062), while the f_2 = 6 summand has degree 4(6)+6-12-14 = +4 > 0. Since Sym^6 C -> Pic^6 is surjective and generically finite for g = 6, the failure locus in the divisor model is nonempty on every geometric fibre of the unbalanced stratum and has fibre dimension >= 4 there (versus 2 for the balanced fibre |omega_C(-D)| = P^2). The omitted unbalanced part therefore enters the localization/Gysin bookkeeping at the SAME codimension 4 as Z^bal, which is precisely the exhaustiveness that corroborated FND-0086 requires before degree-26 Gysin inputs can be declared Tate or vanishing. (4) CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FINDING. Balancedness is an open condition on the Hurwitz space, so Z^bal is open in Z; but it is not dense: the closure of a 17-dimensional Z^bal whose image dominates M_6 cannot contain a 17-dimensional locus lying over the codimension-3 plane-quintic locus (a 17-dimensional irreducible set cannot properly contain another). adjudication_reason: CONFIRMED by the author of the cited theorem himself, so the evidence class rises from adversarial_review to primary_source. (1) Core clause: Broaddus (arXiv:0711.0011v3 = Duke Math. J. 161 (2012) 1943-1969), Remark 4.4, verbatim: 'A natural first guess at a single generator for St(Sigma_g^1) is the arc system coming from the standard identification of the 4g-gon which corresponds to the labelled chord diagram in Figure 6, but in fact by Proposition 4.5 below, the class of this 0-filling system is trivial in St(Sigma_g^1)'; Figure 6 is captioned 'A trivial class in St(Sigma_g^1)'. The finding's terminology matches the source exactly: 'a filling arc system k-fills Sigma_g^1 if the arc system has 2g+k arcs', so a 0-filling system has exactly 2g arcs. (2) Second clause: Main Theorem 1.1, 'The homology class [phi_0] in St(Sigma_g^1) (resp. [phi_0] in St(Sigma_g)) is nontrivial for g >= 1', and Main Theorem 1.2, 'For g >= 1 the Steinberg module St(Sigma) is a cyclic Mod(Sigma)-module generated by the single element described in Section 4' (the Figure 5 diagram phi_0, distinct from Figure 6). This confirms the finding and strengthens it: because St is nonzero while the standard class is zero, the standard system provably cannot be a cyclic generator, so the defect is not merely that a symmetry argument is uninformative. (3) Independent coinvariant-level cross-check, not requiring the unretrieved Proposition 4.5: Church-Farb-Putman (arXiv:1108.0622v3 = IMRN 2012, no. 21, 5025-5030) Theorem 2(iii), attributed to Broaddus, states that a disconnected 0-filling system maps to 0 in U_0/partial(U_1) = (St_g)_{Mod_g}, where 'U is disconnected if the set t_1 u ... u t_n in D^2 is not connected'. The standard 4g-gon diagram has chords joining sides {1,3},{2,4},{5,7},{6,8},...; the two chords of a handle cross, but distinct handles do not interleave, so the union has g components and is disconnected for every g >= 2. Its image in the coinvariants therefore vanishes independently. (4) Mechanism correction the finding does not state: CFP do not derive vanishing from a mapping class acting by -1 on the generator. They compute partial(Y) = 2X + sum_{i=3}^{2g-1} (-1)^{i-1} partial_i Y with all partial_i Y disconnected, giving 2[X] = 0, and partial(Z) = (2g+1)X, giving (2g+1)[X] = 0, whence [X] = 0 by gcd(2,2g+1) = 1. Note [X] = 0 holds only in the coinvariants; [X] is nonzero in St by Main Theorem 1.1. An adjudicator must not conflate the finding's assertion (zero in St) with CFP's conclusion (zero in (St)_G); the finding's is strictly stronger and is the one the source states for the standard system. (5) Scope, and why the obstruction is broader than stated: even repaired to use phi_0, the published route does not reach (g,n) = (6,6). Broaddus cyclicity is stated only for Sigma_g and Sigma_g^1; CFP's vanishing covers Mod_g, Mod_{g,*} (vcd 4g-3) and Mod_{g,1} with one boundary component (cd 4g-2), always with trivial coefficients. CFP do record Harer duality with coefficients, 'for nu = vcd(Mod_{g,*}) = 4g-3 we have H^{nu-k}(Mod_{g,*};M tensor Q) = H_k(Mod_{g,*}; M tensor St_g tensor Q)', but their vanishing computation is for M = Q: the relations 2[X] = 0 and (2g+1)[X] = 0 come from boundaries of 1-filling systems and become twisted by the action on M, so nothing in the published argument computes (St tensor V)_G for nontrivial V. Cyclicity alone only reduces (St tensor V)_G to a quotient of V; the stabiliser and boundary relations must still be evaluated. (6) Corroboration: Irmer (arXiv:2312.08721v1) proves Broaddus's conjectural characterisation of the unique generating orbit and that Mod_g acts on St with trivial kernel, consistent with phi_0, not the standard system, being the generator. (7) No claim contradiction: no record in data/claims.jsonl (CONJ-0001, THM-0001..THM-0007, OBS-0001, RED-0001) concerns the Steinberg module or top-degree mapping class group cohomology, so contradicts_claim_ids remains empty. statement: Component-dimension comparisons across the h^0 jump are not valid over the base generality inherited from C66-GEO-H0. statement: At (g,d)=(6,4) the non-primitive tetragonal pencil is CE-rigid and maximally unbalanced: if C is hyperelliptic of genus 6 and gamma has degree 4, then gamma=q o h necessarily, E=O(1)+O(4)+O(4), and the relations bundle is exactly F=O(2)+O(7), not merely 'not O(4)+O(5)'. Verified in the model y^2=f_14(x), z=x^2: the restriction H^0(Sym^2E(-6))->H^0(6A) is surjective onto the 7-dimensional space of degree-<=6 polynomials in x and its kernel is H^0(O(1))*(w^2-z v^2), of dimension exactly 2, forcing splitting type (2,7). Reusable because it supplies a first explicit point of the unbalanced CE stratification that FND-0091 flags as unconstructed, and because the splitting-type distance 5 shows the hyperelliptic-composed locus sits at the opposite extreme from the balanced locus rather than adjacent to it.

The 'at most two gamma-images' exceptional locus of ATT-0083 clause (F) is controlled exactly, not just bounded: Gamma <= D_a+D_b forces D_a+D_b = Gamma + R with R effective of degree 2 in the class 3D-K = 2D-L, and h^0(3D-K)<=1 on a non-hyperelliptic fibre (degree 2 with two sections would be a g^1_2) makes R unique when it exists. Rank check: expected codimension of AJ in Div^6 is g = 6, actual relative codimension is 6 - 2 = 4, so the excess rank is 2 = h^1(L), consistent with the rank-two remark in FND-0129. Every clause of FND-0133 is thereby confirmed. PRIMARY-SOURCE ANCHORS. Kleiman, 'The Picard scheme' (arXiv:math/0504020; published as chapter 9 of Fundamental Algebraic Geometry, AMS Math. Surveys and Monographs 123, 2005): subsection 3.10 defines Q by the functorial isomorphism Hom(Q, N) = f_*(F tensor f^*N); Definition 3.12 introduces LinSys_{L/X/S}; Theorem 3.13 states that L := P(Q) represents LinSys_{L/X/S}, with P(Q) = Proj Sym(Q) in the Grothendieck convention, so its points are rank-one QUOTIENTS of Q and its tautological surjection is Q_L -> O(1); Exercise 3.14 states that there is a natural relative effective divisor W on X_L/L with O_{X_L}(W) = L_L tensor f_L^*O_L(1), i.e. the twist is by +O(1), not O(-1). When pi_*L is locally free and base-change compatible, Q = (pi_*L)^dual, so Kleiman's P(Q) is precisely the space of lines in pi_*L. The convention frame is EGA II (Grothendieck, Publ. Math. IHES 8, 1961), section 4.1 and 4.2.3, and Hartshorne II.7.11 to II.7.12. The identification of the Abel tangent map with the coboundary of 0 -> O_X -> O_X(D) -> N_D -> 0 is Kleiman Remark 5.18, citing Mumford, Lectures on Curves on an Algebraic Surface (1966), p. 165; ACGH volume I chapter IV sections 2 and 4 give the classical universal-divisor and Zariski-tangent-space treatment. The excess-bundle formalism E = g^*N / N with contribution c_{d-d'}(E) cap [W] is Fulton, Intersection Theory, section 6.3 (Thom-Porteous is section 14.4, not 17.4). SHARPENINGS THAT SHOULD BE RECORDED WITH THE PROMOTION. (1) The phrase 'untwisted Hodge-bundle isomorphism' is imprecise: the bundle in question is R^1 pi_* L, which is rank two and, by relative Serre duality with M := omega tensor L^dual of degree four, is (pi_*M)^dual; it is not the Hodge bundle pi_*omega_{C/B} of rank six. The correct reading of the clause is 'no untwisted identification with a bundle pulled back from B', and that reading is what the derivation supports. (2) The disjunct 'or prove it trivial' is provably unavailable on AJ itself and the finding can be strengthened accordingly: M_univ restricts to O(1) on each P^2 fibre, so c_1(M_univ) = xi is non-torsion; writing V = R^1 pi_* L, the rank-two excess bundle E = p^*V tensor M_univ has c_2(E) = c_2(V) + c_1(V) xi + xi^2, and p_*(c_1(V) xi + xi^2) = [B] since p_* xi = 0 and p_* xi^2 = [B]. Dropping the twist therefore perturbs the pushed-forward excess class by exactly [B], a definitively nonzero error. The hedge survives only for the OPEN ordered incidence: on the complement of the discriminant inside each P^2 fibre, the restriction of xi can become torsion in CH^1 with Q coefficients, so triviality there is a distinct statement that must be argued and may not be assumed. (3) The convention hazard is real and sharper than the finding states. It is not merely a sign on M_univ: read in the Grothendieck convention, 'P_B(pi_*L)' means Proj Sym(pi_*L), which parametrizes rank-one quotients of pi_*L and is NOT the relative linear system; the correct object is Proj Sym((pi_*L)^dual), which is how FND-0127 already writes it as P((pi_*L)^dual). Downstream artifacts should disambiguate the label, not just the twist sign. (4) Generality: as with FND-0096, the twist identification transports verbatim to any (g,n) and any L with locally free base-change-compatible pushforward; only excess rank two is (6,6)-specific. (5) Existence hypotheses: writing AJ as a projective bundle at all presupposes constant h^0(L), which is the FND-0047 / FND-0107 / FND-0131 hypothesis; over nonreduced or h^0-jumping bases the FND-0107 Abel-Jacobi fibre model must be used and the twist formula then holds on the locus where the projective-bundle model is valid. On a stack base the FND-0127 smooth-atlas descent line is required. (6) 'Globally' is correct in the sense 'as an isomorphism of sheaves on all of AJ (and on its etale cover)', not 'descends to B'. DISTINCTNESS AND MERGE. Nearest sibling is FND-0129, which concerns the same excess square but fixes the typing of the zero section e: B -> Pic^0 and the coker-versus-dual choice, noting that c_2 agrees in rank two. FND-0133 supplies the global identification of that cokernel including the tautological twist that FND-0129 leaves unnamed; the two are complementary and neither subsumes the other, so they should not be merged. Distinct from FND-0122, whose cokernel is the CE evaluation cokernel of phi_5, Serre-dual to H^0 of a degree-zero line bundle and of generic rank at most one - conflating that with this rank-two excess cokernel is exactly the kind of error this finding guards against. Distinct from FND-0096 (Fitting ideal of the evaluation cokernel over Pic^0), from FND-0107 / FND-0047 / FND-0131 (representability and base change), and from FND-0127 (base scope). Merge target: none. VERDICT. Promote from candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source. The finding is mathematically correct as stated, load-bearing for C66-COMP-RANK (any excess or Chern-class computation that drops M_univ is off by a nonzero class), and should be recorded together with sharpenings (1) through (3). statement: For the universal degree-six divisor over the projective bundle AJ=P_B(pi_*L), the excess cokernel along the ordered etale incidence is globally the pullback of R1pi_*L tensored by the convention-dependent tautological line M_univ determined by O(D_univ)=L tensor pi^*M_univ. scope.generality: geometric fibres of a balanced genus-six degree-four CE family satisfying the weak relative-canonical normalization

statement: On a balanced fibre satisfying the weak CE normalization, h^0(L) = 3 (this lemma) combines with base-point-freeness of L on the balanced locus to make the general member of |L| ≅ P^2 consist of six DISTINCT points, hence the reduced-support open of the closed Abel–Jacobi incidence is nonempty and dense in every fibre of the P^2-bundle. Argument: if L had a base point p, then L(-p) would be a g^2_5 on a genus-six curve, forcing a smooth plane quintic, whose tetragonal pencil is projection from that point and is CE-unbalanced, hence excluded from the balanced locus; L base-point-free with h^0 = 3 gives a finite morphism φ_L : C → P^2 whose image spans, and in characteristic zero φ_L is separable onto its image, so a general line pulls back to a reduced divisor (Bertini), i.e. six distinct points.

adjudication_reason: Khawaja–Siksek, Theorem 14, proves the required common-factor implication over a perfect field, and the proof of their Theorem 1 explicitly records that the common-factor degree divides both original map degrees. Applying these statements to degrees 2 and 4 verifies FND-0135 exactly. No contradiction exists with CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It should therefore be promoted independently rather than merged.

scope.generality: smooth curves of genus 6 with a g^1_2 and a degree-4 map to P^1

statement: For a smooth genus-6 curve admitting maps h:C→P^1 of degree 2 and γ:C→P^1 of degree 4, Castelnuovo–Severi non-independence alone does not name the factorization; one must add that any common intermediate factor φ:C→C' has deg(φ) dividing 2 and at least 2, hence φ=h (up to automorphism of the target) and γ=q∘h with deg q=2.

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0005 (c(6)=5, so n=6 needs residual geometry) and with the C66-COMP-COMP fibrewise reduced/nonreduced cut. INDEPENDENT DERIVATION. Let C be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus 6 over a field k (Stacks 0BY7: g=dim H^1(O_C) and H^0(O_C)=k, hence χ(O_C)=1-g=-5), D an effective Cartier divisor of degree 4 with h^0(O_C(D))≥2, and L=ω_C(-D). Smooth proper curves are Gorenstein, so Stacks 0C19 gives deg(ω_C)=2g-2=10 and deg L=6. For a geometric point p (so deg(2p)=2), L(-2p) has degree 4. Stacks Lemma 53.5.2 (0BS6) supplies Riemann–Roch χ(E)=deg(E)-(1/2)rk(E)deg(ω) for locally free E on a proper Gorenstein equidimensional curve, hence χ(L(-2p))=4-g+1=-1, together with the dimension symmetry dim H^i(E)=dim H^{1-i}(E^∨⊗ω). Stacks Remark 53.4.3 (0BS4) is the invertible-sheaf form of Serre duality: h^1(L(-2p))=h^0(ω⊗L(2p)^{-1})=h^0(O_C(D+2p)). Therefore h^0(L(-2p))=h^0(O_C(D+2p))-1 identically. The inequality ≥1 is the sheaf inclusion O(D)→O(D+2p) given by a nonzero section of O(2p): on an integral curve this is injective on global sections, so h^0(O(D+2p))≥h^0(O(D))≥2. A nonzero section of L(-2p) produces an effective divisor in the complete system |L| containing 2p, hence nonreduced at p. The same RR also gives h^0(L)=1+h^0(D)≥3, so |L| is nonempty. SCOPE SHARPENING. The displayed equality uses deg(2p)=2 and therefore holds for geometric (or k-rational, k algebraically closed) points, not for a closed point of residue degree d>1, where χ(L(-2p))=1-2d and the identity becomes h^0(L(-2p))=h^0(O(D+2p))+1-2d. Read ‘every point p’ geometrically, which is the campaign’s fibrewise usage. Characteristic is unrestricted: 0BS6/0BS4 have no char-0 hypothesis, and 2p remains a nonreduced length-2 subscheme in every characteristic. The argument does not use balanced CE splitting, base-point-freeness, or constancy of h^0(L)=3. RELATION TO THE CORPUS. Complementary to corroborated FND-0134 (on balanced weakly-normalized fibres with h^0(L)=3, bpf plus char-0 Bertini make a general member reduced, so the reduced-support open is nonempty dense): a nonempty dense open in |L|≅P^2 may be all of P^2, so FND-0134 does not force a nonempty nonreduced complement and does not subsume this lemma. Complementary to FND-0083 (χ(L)=1 does not prove reduced-support nonemptiness). Distinct from FND-0073 (the identity h^0(L)=1+h^0(M)). REV-0140 correctly records that this RR identity repairs ATT-0090’s undocumented 2-jet-kernel input for the nonempty-complement half of (R2); the present finding is that repaired positive lemma, not a defect in the identity. ATT-0090 remains incomplete on other grounds (unbound h^0(L)=3 / WORKING-C66-COMP-COMP), which is FND-0058 territory and is not this lemma. Kind ‘obstruction’ is a mild misclassification: this is a positive residual-series lemma; it obstructs only proposed decompositions that assign an empty nonreduced locus to some |L|. Absence of FND-0136 from the workspace proof/findings.jsonl is the same corpus-registration discrepancy noted for FND-0134; TASK.json is controlling. Merge target: none. scope.generality: smooth genus-six curves with an effective degree-four pencil divisor

statement: If C has genus 6, D is an effective degree-four divisor with h^0(O(D))≥2, and L=ω_C(-D), then for every point p one has h^0(L(-2p))=h^0(O(D+2p))-1≥1. Hence every complete |L| contains a divisor nonreduced at p.

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001-THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0001 (stack versus space conventions) and THM-0005 (c(6)=5, so n=6 needs residual geometry). INDEPENDENT CHECKS. (1) Inertia of a scheme or algebraic space is trivial: Stacks Proposition 94.13.3 (04SZ) says an algebraic stack is an algebraic space if and only if I_X -> X is an equivalence; Stacks 04XA records that a roman-capital algebraic stack is required to have trivial inertia. If B is a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme, as ATT-0089 theorem_statement declares, then C->B is a scheme morphism, Hilb^6(C/B) and Pic^6(C/B) are algebraic spaces, and I is an algebraic space, so Aut of a geometric point of I is 1 and 1->Aut(x_tilde)->Aut(x)->S_6 degenerates to 1->1->1->S_6. (2) I is defined from Hilb^6 and Pic^6 only; gamma enters only in the construction of L, not as part of an object of I. ATT-0089 step 4 ('an ordered automorphism induces a PGL_2 transformation fixing the three images') therefore requires Aut to mean Aut(C,gamma,Gamma). Vakil Class 35 records that Aut(P^1) is three-transitive, so a PGL_2 element fixing three distinct points is the identity; that step is correct for the cover group and unavailable for Aut(C,Gamma). (3) A geometric point of M_{6,6} has automorphism group Aut(C; p_1,...,p_6)=Aut(C,Gamma) (ordered or unordered), so that is the group relevant to the forgetful map. (4) Kernel triviality is not formal. Stacks Lemma 53.12.2 (0C1D) gives 2g-2 = deg(f)(2g_Y-2)+deg(R). For the hyperelliptic involution, deg(f)=2 and g_Y=0, hence deg(R)=2g+2. Vakil Class 35 states that a hyperelliptic cover has precisely 2g+2 distinct branch points; in characteristic not 2 each branch point has a unique ramification point, so the involution fixes 2g+2=14 points on a genus-6 curve and can therefore fix six marked points. Fujimori (Ann. Scuola Norm. Sup. Pisa 1997) records the same 2g+2 upper bound for any non-identity automorphism of a curve of genus g>=2. SCOPE. The 2g+2 witness is hyperelliptic, and FND-0125 excludes hyperelliptic composed degree-4 pencils from the balanced CE locus, so this is a formal obstruction rather than a point of the campaign family. Complementary to corroborated FND-0098 (mono into M_{6,6} requires recovering gamma from L, plus a stack-level Aut argument), FND-0127 (scheme-versus-stack base scope for Grauert/H3), FND-0075 (S_6-torsor at stack level, not on coarse moduli), and FND-0060 (Hurwitz coarse dimension needs stabilizer bookkeeping). Distinct from pending FND-0138, which is the positive B_3 repair Aut(C,Gamma)=Aut(C,gamma,Gamma), not this well-posedness obstruction. Not a merge into FND-0098, FND-0101, or FND-0127: those concern monomorphism of Z, gap-marker discipline, and projective-bundle descent respectively. The finding's sole reviewer_engine (claude) is in this revision's excluded_engines; this audit is the first non-excluded verification.
statement: In C66-GEO-COMP, any inertia/stabilizer clause of the form 1→Aut(x_tilde)→Aut(x)→S_6 for a geometric point x of the Abel–Jacobi incidence I=Hilb⁶(C/B)×_{Pic⁶(C/B)}B must first name the stack and the moduli problem, because I is defined without any reference to γ. Over a scheme base every such Aut is trivial and the clause is vacuous; over a stack base the group depends on what the base classifies. Rigidity proofs that pass through 'the automorphism induces a PGL_2 transformation of P¹ fixing the marked images' prove the statement only for Aut(C,γ,Γ), automorphisms of the tetragonal cover preserving the divisor. They do not by themselves prove it for Aut(C,Γ), the group relevant to the forgetful map to M_{6,6}: an automorphism of C preserving Γ need not preserve the pencil, and triviality of the kernel is not formal, since a nontrivial automorphism of a genus-6 curve can fix as many as 2g+2=14 points and so can fix six marked points. Downstream artifacts must state which group they mean before citing such a clause.

adjudication_reason: The narrow recovery lemma is correct conditionally: O_C(Gamma)=L gives M=omega_C(-Gamma), the weak CE normalization supplies M=gamma^*O_P1(1), and Riemann-Roch gives h^0(M)=h^0(L)-1=2. The two pulled-back coordinate sections therefore form all of H^0(M), so gamma is the complete pencil |M| and is determined only up to PGL_2. This repairs the group distinction in FND-0137 in the pencil-preserving sense and implements the recovery route already identified in FND-0098. It does not identify Aut(C,Gamma) with strict deck transformations over a fixed target. The claim that rigidity applies verbatim requires the additional marked-image and etaleness open conditions and is not valid on the entire incidence as written. Its B_4 clause is not a second stratum of the cited balanced weak-normalization locus: corroborated FND-0134 makes h^0(L)=3 throughout that locus, so B_4 is empty there and must be treated as an out-of-scope warning. FND-0138 is also absent from proof/findings.jsonl and exists only as the pending candidate embedded in TASK.json. Accordingly its verified content should be merged as a scoped addendum to FND-0137, cross-referencing FND-0098, rather than promoted as an independent finding.
statement: On the stratum B_3 the tetragonal pencil is canonically recovered from the marked curve, so the two candidate automorphism groups coincide and the C66-GEO-COMP rigidity statement can be made for the M_{6,6}-relevant group. Concretely, for Γ in the incidence one has O(Γ)≅L relatively, hence M:=ω_C(-Γ)≅ω_C⊗L^{-1}=ω_C²⊗W_5^∨; under the weak CE relative-canonical normalization (FND-0105, ATT-0066/CLM-0066-2) M≅γ*O_{P¹}(1), which is base-point-free of degree 4, and on B_3 one has h⁰(L)=3 hence h⁰(M)=2, so |M| is a base-point-free PENCIL and equals the pencil defining γ; therefore γ is determined by (C,Γ) up to PGL_2. Consequently any σ∈Aut(C) with σ(Γ)=Γ satisfies σ*M≅M, preserves |M|, and induces τ∈PGL_2 with γσ=τγ, i.e. Aut(C,Γ)=Aut(C,γ,Γ) on B_3, and the deck-transformation rigidity argument (three distinct marked images plus one γ-étale marked point) applies verbatim to Aut(C,Γ). The recovery fails on B_4, where h⁰(M)=3 and |M| is a net containing many pencils.

Canning-Larson Lemma 10.3 supplies the relative-canonical identification, Lemma 10.6 supplies the relevant degree calculation, and Lemma 10.10 excludes trigonal curves and smooth plane quintics from the balanced f_1=4 stratum. Riemann-Roch and Clifford theory then give h^0(L)=3. Bertini and the discriminant theory of Lanteri-Munoz verify that the non-reduced locus is a proper closed curve in |L|, while elementary configuration-space quotient theory gives the degree-720 etale S_6-torsor. Thus the finding is mathematically sound after narrowing to characteristic zero, but its principal reduced-support result duplicates FND-0134, and its torsor clause duplicates FND-0064. The only additional content is the standard statement that the complement is a discriminant curve, so FND-0140 should be merged into FND-0134 rather than independently promoted.
statement: On every geometric fibre of a genus-6 Casnati-Ekedahl family with balanced relations bundle F=O(4)+O(5) and weak relative-canonical normalization O_X(1)|_C isomorphic to omega_{C/P1} tensor gamma^*A, the linear system |L| with L=W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} has fixed part of degree at most one, the moving part is a base-point-free g^2_5 or g^2_6, a general member is a reduced six-point divisor, the non-reduced locus is a nonempty proper closed curve in the plane |L|, and the ordered Conf_6 incidence is a nonempty smooth finite etale S_6-torsor of degree 720 over that dense non-closed surface open. The argument does not assume that L itself is base-point-free.

statement: Under (CE)+(BAL)+(N), every geometric fibre has h^0(O_C(D))=2, h^0(L)=3 and h^1(L)=2. The only Clifford-equality case that could produce h^0(D)=3 is a hyperelliptic fibre, and a hyperelliptic genus-6 degree-four cover cannot have F=O(4)+O(5). Constancy on the balanced locus therefore uses only exclusion of the hyperelliptic-composed pencil; it is not equivalent to exclusion of every non-primitive degree-four pencil through a positive-genus intermediate curve.

adjudication_reason: MATHEMATICAL VERDICT: the finding is TRUE for the campaign case but is NOT a new finding; it is a primary-source-backed proof of an assertion already carried by corroborated findings, plus a restatement of a corroborated conclusion. It is orthogonal to THM-0005 (c(6)=5, so n=6 is outside the published CKgP range) and touches no weight/Tate bookkeeping. (B) PRIMARY VERIFICATION of clause 1. Euisung Park, 'Complete Linear Series on a Hyperelliptic Curve' (arXiv:0808.0113), sets A := f^*O_{P^1}(1) for the degree-two map f, and for a line bundle L defines the factorization type (m,b) with m = max{t : H^0(L (x) A^{-t}) != 0}, B_L = L (x) A^{-m}, b = deg B_L. Thm 3.1(1): h^i(C,L) = h^i(P^1,O(m)) + h^i(P^1,O(m+b-g-1)). For g = 6, deg L = 4 = 2m + b the three admissible types give h^0 = 1 for (m,b) = (0,4); h^0 = 2 for (1,2), i.e. L = A + p + q with p,q the two base points and moving part the g^1_2; h^0 = 3 for (2,0), i.e. L = A^2 = 2 g^1_2. This is exactly the dichotomy asserted by the finding, and it also confirms 'the induced map has degree two' in the first case (the moving part is |A|). Thm 3.1(2): L is base-point-free iff b = 0, or 1 <= b <= g+1 with m + b >= g+1. Since m + b = d - m <= d, any base-point-free L of degree d <= g has d - m <= g < g+1, so b = 0 and L = A^{d/2}. For (g,d) = (6,4) this forces L = A^2. Thm 3.4(alpha): for L = A^m with 1 <= m <= g, h^0 = m+1 and phi_L is the double cover f followed by the m-uple embedding, image a rational normal curve; hence H^0(A^2) = f^*H^0(O_{P^1}(2)) is 3-dimensional and every pencil inside |A^2| is f^* of a pencil in |O_{P^1}(2)|, i.e. gamma = q o f with deg q = 2. A base-point-free pencil V has base locus containing that of |L|, so V base-point-free implies L base-point-free; the case-1 bundle A + p + q therefore supports no base-point-free subpencil. Clause 1 is thus fully established, and is an instance of the general d <= g statement. Independent cross-check by Riemann-Roch: deg 4 on g = 6 gives chi = -1, so h^0 >= 2 forces h^1 >= 3, i.e. L special, and Clifford gives h^0 <= 3 with equality only in the hyperelliptic 2 g^1_2 case - consistent with Park and with corroborated FND-0103/FND-0104. (C) SCOPE CORRECTION (mild, does not affect the campaign case): the finding states clause 1 without a genus hypothesis. It fails for d >= g+1; Park Thm 3.1(2) with (m,b) = (0,g+1) is base-point-free and non-composed, realized at (g,d) = (3,4). The correct scope is degree d <= g on a hyperelliptic curve of genus g, hence g >= 4 for degree four. Any merged record must carry this restriction. (D) VERIFICATION of clause 2. In the CE setup gamma_s is a finite degree-four morphism, so its pencil is base-point-free and clause 1 applies fibrewise: a hyperelliptic geometric fibre forces gamma_s = q o h. Corroborated FND-0125 then gives E = O(1)+O(4)+O(4) and F_s = O(2)+O(7), incompatible with the standing fibrewise-balanced hypothesis F_s = O(4)+O(5) (splitting-type distance 5). statement: On a hyperelliptic curve every base-point-free pencil of degree four factors through the hyperelliptic double cover: a degree-four divisor with h^0 >= 2 is linearly equivalent to g^1_2 + p + q, in which case the complete pencil has base points p, q and the induced map has degree two, or to 2 g^1_2, which is composed. Consequently a family satisfying the ATT-0094 hypotheses (fibrewise balanced F_s ≅ O(4)⊕O(5) together with FND-0125) has no hyperelliptic geometric fibres.

Stacks Lemma 58.11.2 (0BQL) says that a connected finite étale cover of a normal integral scheme is itself an integral normal scheme. Stacks Lemma 28.7.7 (033N) says a locally Noetherian scheme is normal if and only if it is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes. None of these tags applies to an algebraic stack. Normality of a stack is the smooth-atlas property: Stacks 100.7 (04YE) and Remark 100.7.3 (04YH) make 'normal' a smooth-local scheme property, so a stack is normal precisely when some (equivalently any) smooth atlas is a normal scheme. Étale morphisms of stacks are a separate, DM-restricted notion (Stacks 101.35/0CIK): they are not 'smooth of relative dimension 0', and the residual-gerbe examples [A^1/G_m] and [Spec k/μ_p] show that stacky finite/quasi-finite behaviour is not the scheme one. Residual gerbes exist under the Stacks 100.11 (06ML) hypotheses; their automorphism groups are the geometric inertia. Noohi (arXiv math/0201021v1, Thm 1.1) puts a homomorphism ω_x from Aut of the residue gerbe into π_1 of the stack, and identifies π_1(stack)/N with π_1 of the coarse space, N being generated by all such inertia images. Consequently inertia acts on the geometric fibre of a finite étale cover, in particular on the ordered S_6-fibre. If H_V is computed from coarse-space or atlas path monodromy without that groupoid/inertia action, the orbit count and the degrees need not match the irreducible components or representable degrees of the stack Z_V. Noohi moreover defines a covering space of a stack to be a finite étale representable morphism, so representability is an extra datum, not a formal consequence of writing 'S_6-torsor' in scheme language. The finding's rescue clauses are exactly the ones these sources license: (i) inertia-free, i.e. I_V→V an equivalence, so V is an algebraic space (Stacks Prop. 94.13.3/04SZ) and one reduces to FND-0132; or (ii) pull back to a normal scheme atlas, apply 03SF+0BQL+033N there, and descend along R=U×_V U while tracking how residual-gerbe automorphisms permute components. A third, equivalent, route is to take H_V as the image of the stacky π_1 so that inertia is already inside the monodromy; ATT-0096 does not do this. SCOPE SHARPENING. The finding is a proof-obligation obstruction, not a numerical counterexample: it does not assert that [S_6:H_V] fails when H_V is the stacky monodromy image and components/degrees are those of the stack. It asserts that the scheme-theoretic formula, as written and as used in CLM-0096-2, is not valid on a stack without one of the extra hypotheses. RELATION TO THE CORPUS. Complementary to FND-0127 (scheme-to-stack descent for Grauert/Abel–Jacobi identifications, not Galois component counts). Complementary to FND-0064 (existence of the stack-level S_6-torsor on pairwise-distinct sections) and FND-0075 (that torsor fails on coarse moduli when automorphisms permute marks; Q-coefficient cohomology descent is harmless, which does not salvage an integral/scheme-theoretic component-and-degree formula). Complementary to FND-0137 (which Aut group appears in the forgetful inertia sequence for u:Z→M_{6,6}). Distinct from all of the above: do not merge. Kind 'obstruction' is correct for CLM-0096-2. CLM-0099-3, the summary, GAP-0099-1 and the first novelty claim label the same subgroup 'geometric monodromy'. That label is correct only when k=k-bar. Independently confirmed by reading ATT-0099. (2) Component formula over k. Stacks 03SF: finite etale U-schemes are finite continuous pi_1(U,u)-sets, and connected components correspond to orbits on the geometric fibre. For a right S_6-torsor the left pi_1-action is through rho: pi_1(U,u)->S_6, the orbits are the left cosets Hg, and there are [S_6:H] of them, each of size |H|. Stacks 033N: a locally Noetherian normal scheme is a disjoint union of integral normal schemes, so connected components are irreducible. Thus Irr(Z)=H_arith\S_6 as a statement about the k-scheme Z, exactly as the theorem_statement writes it. (3) Comparison with H_geom. Restricting rho to pi_1(U_{k-bar},u) gives H_geom=rho(pi_1^geom). statement: Let U be a connected quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme over a field k, u a geometric point, and Z -> U a finite etale right S_6-torsor. The group H in Irr(Z) = H\S_6 for the k-scheme Z is the image H_arith of pi_1^{et}(U,u) -> S_6. If U is normal, integral, and locally Noetherian, connected components of Z are its irreducible components, indexed by left H_arith-cosets; each has degree |H_arith| over U and stabilizer conjugate to H_arith. If, in addition, U_{k-bar} is connected, then H_geom := image(pi_1^{et}(U_{k-bar},u) -> S_6) is normal in H_arith, [S_6:H_arith] <= [S_6:H_geom], and after base change Z has [S_6:H_geom] geometric irreducible components of degree |H_geom|. Thus irreducibility over k is weaker than geometric irreducibility. This identifies the group but does not compute either monodromy image for the balanced tetragonal family.

CLM-0101-4's justification repeats 'right multiplication is transitive on left cosets and stabilizes H_alpha g through g^{-1}H_alpha g'. REV-0150 independently re-derives the orbits as the sets H_alpha g, confirms the stabilizer g^{-1}H_alpha g, and records FC-REV0150-COSET-SIDE as a nomenclature slip that 'does not affect the truth of the clause'; strongest_attack likewise says the notation H_alpha\S_6 together with the stabilizer computation pins the correct reading. Packet FND-0148 (corroborated) uses Irr(Z)=H\S_6 and 'indexed by left H_arith-cosets' with stabilizer only 'conjugate to H_arith', so it carries the same English mislabel but not a wrong conjugate. Independent public sources agree with the group-theoretic core under elementary nomenclature: Encyclopedia of Mathematics (oldid 35336) defines the left coset as aH={ah:h in H} and the right coset as Ha; Wikipedia Coset revision 1351557349 defines gH as a left coset, Hg as a right coset, writes G/H for {gH} and H\G for {Hg}, and states that the orbit of g under the left H-action (h,g)|->hg is the right coset Hg, while the orbit under the right H-action is the left coset gH. The same page records that left and right decompositions coincide if and only if H is normal, and that the product of left cosets is the quotient-group operation only in that case. The original candidate therefore overstates that right multiplication on S_6/H={gH} is 'not well defined at all': that product is well-defined precisely when H is normal in G, hence in particular for the normal subgroups {1}, A_6, and S_6 of S_6, and fails for every non-normal monodromy image. The conjugacy bookkeeping hazard is likewise sharpest when H is non-normal: the stabilizer of Hg under the right G-action is g^{-1}Hg, whereas gHg^{-1} is the stabilizer of gH under the left G-action, and these need not be the same conjugate. No contradiction with CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001 (contradicts_claim_ids is empty). Compatible with the mathematical content of FND-0148 (H\S_6 indexing, degree |H|, stabilizer conjugate to H, arithmetic versus geometric monodromy) while correcting only the adjective 'left'. Compatible with FND-0132 (normality needed to pass from pi_0 to Irr) and with the confirmed ATT-0101 component clauses. Not a merge into FND-0148: that finding is the arithmetic/geometric monodromy distinction, not this typing discipline. Not retired as cosmetic: the English slip in ATT-0101 is harmless only because that artifact already writes Hg and g^{-1}Hg; downstream artifacts that take 'left cosets' literally as {gH} and then apply the right deck action, or that record the stabilizer as gHg^{-1} on the {Hg} indexing, are ill-typed. pre_adjudication_statement: In the component formula for a RIGHT S_6-torsor, the index set H\S_6 must be read as the set of orbits of left multiplication by H, i.e. the sets Hg, which under standard nomenclature are right cosets; the phrase 'left cosets H\S_6' used both in ATT-0101's theorem statement and in the wording of FND-0148 is a mislabel of the correct object. The distinction is typing-critical rather than cosmetic downstream: the right deck action descends to {Hg} (Hg . g' = Hgg', transitive, stabilizer of Hg equal to g^{-1}Hg), whereas on the genuine left-coset set S_6/H = {gH} right multiplication is not well defined at all, so any artifact that writes gH and then applies the deck action, or that computes a stabilizer as gHg^{-1} on that indexing, is ill-typed and will produce the wrong conjugacy bookkeeping. statement: Let G be a group and H a subgroup of G. The orbits of the left multiplication action of H on G are the sets Hg={hg : h in H}. Under standard elementary nomenclature these are the right cosets of H, and the set of such orbits is denoted H\G; the left cosets are the sets gH, and the set of left cosets is denoted G/H. The phrase 'left cosets H\S_6' in ATT-0101's theorem statement and the phrase 'left H_arith-cosets' in FND-0148 are therefore elementary mislabels of the object Hg, even though the notation H\S_6 itself is the standard symbol for that object. Now let U be a connected scheme, let Z->U be a finite etale right G-torsor, and let H be the image of etale monodromy acting by left multiplication on a geometric fibre after a choice of trivialization. The connected components of Z are indexed by the orbit set H\G={Hg}. The right deck action of G is well-defined on this set by Hg . g'=Hgg', is transitive, and the stabilizer of Hg is exactly g^{-1}Hg. Right multiplication on the genuine left-coset set G/H={gH} is well-defined if and only if H is normal in G; in particular it is well-defined when H is {1}, A_6, or S_6 inside S_6, and it fails for every non-normal monodromy image. Any artifact that writes gH and then applies the right deck action, or that computes the stabilizer of the component indexed by Hg as gHg^{-1}, is ill-typed unless H is normal, in which case both conjugates equal H. Identifying these connected components with irreducible components additionally requires U to be normal and locally Noetherian. This constraint does not refute the component, degree, dimension, or transitivity clauses of ATT-0101, which already index components by H_alpha g and compute the stabilizer as g^{-1}H_alpha g. Downstream C66-GEO-COMP and C66-TATE-* artifacts must write 'the orbit set H\G of left multiplication' (equivalently, 'the set of right cosets Hg') and must record the component stabilizer as g^{-1}Hg.

adjudication_reason: Mandatory first reads: ATT-0101 theorem_statement and Section 3 / CLM-0101-3 / CLM-0101-4, and REV-0150 checked_claims for those two clauses plus finding_candidate FC-REV0150-INDUCED-REP-ON-COMPONENTS (the exact source of FND-0152). ATT-0101 proves, and REV-0150 confirms, that Z_alpha -> U_alpha is a finite etale right S_6-torsor over a normal integral U_alpha, that Irr(Z_alpha) is the monodromy-orbit set of cardinality [S_6:H_alpha], that each component maps finite etale of degree |H_alpha| onto U_alpha, and that the right S_6-action is transitive on components with stabilizer conjugate to H_alpha. The induction formula is not stated in ATT-0101 (which explicitly records GAP-TATE and asserts no Hodge or Tate conclusion); it is a reviewer corollary. No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with packet FND-0148 (H_alpha is arithmetic monodromy; here k is algebraically closed, so the arithmetic/geometric distinction is vacuous), FND-0151 (index set is the orbit set H_alpha\S_6 of left multiplication, i.e. right cosets H_alpha g, with stabilizer g^{-1}H_alpha g), FND-0132 (normality is load-bearing for Irr=pi_0), FND-0144 (the formula is scheme-level and does not extend to stacks with inertia), FND-0053 (induction does not force Tate local systems), and FND-0075 (Q-coefficients, no integral or coarse-space descent). Independent primary checks. (1) Finite-group induction: the Q[S_6]-module attached to a transitive permutation of summands with stabilizer H_alpha and H_alpha-module V on the identity-coset summand is Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} V = Q[S_6] tensor_{Q[H_alpha]} V (Wikipedia, Induced representation, algebraic construction; Serre GTM 42). Right multiplication by g is a U_alpha-automorphism of the torsor, so all components are isomorphic as U_alpha-schemes and F(Z_alpha) is that induced object for any additive S_6-equivariant F. (2) Residual Galois: Z_alpha^1 is connected of degree |H_alpha| over U_alpha with Aut_{U_alpha}(Z_alpha^1) equal to the component stabilizer H_alpha, hence Z_alpha^1 -> U_alpha is a Galois cover with group H_alpha (Stacks Project Tag 03SF, equivalent conditions (1)-(4)). (3) Invariants: for an n-sheeted covering given by a group action, Hatcher Algebraic Topology Proposition 3G.1 states that with coefficients in a field of characteristic 0 or prime to n, pullback is injective onto the deck-invariants; equivalently, MathOverflow 57076 (Sprehn) records that if |G| is a unit in the coefficient ring then H^*(X/G) -> H^*(X)^G is an isomorphism (Milnor Characteristic Classes exercise). Thus H^*(U_alpha;Q) = H^*(Z_alpha^1;Q)^{H_alpha}, and Frobenius reciprocity gives the S_6-invariant consistency check. The same transfer applies to ordinary homology; Borel-Moore homology is included only as an additive S_6-equivariant functor (finite-sheeted lifts preserve locally finite chains), not as a separate Hatcher citation. Algebraic deck maps are morphisms of mixed Hodge structures, so the Q-linear identifications are MHS identifications. Wording corrections required before promotion: the original '=' must be an isomorphism of S_6-objects; components must be indexed by H_alpha\S_6 as in FND-0151, not by a mislabelled left-coset set; and consequence (i) overstates when it says uncomputed H_alpha is the only obstruction — H_alpha determines the induction functor and the component count, but the H_alpha-object F(Z_alpha^1) remains an independent geometric/Hodge input (GAP-TATE). Consequence (ii) is correct and is retained. Distinct from FND-0148, FND-0151, FND-0053, and FND-0075: do not merge. Promote from candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source.

Consistency check: taking S_6-invariants returns H^*(Z_alpha^1;Q)^{H_alpha} = H^*(U_alpha;Q), as it must. Two consequences for the downstream nodes. (i) The entire S_6-isotypic structure of the ordered failure locus is determined by the single subgroup H_alpha together with the H_alpha-representation on one component, so the uncomputed H_alpha of GAP-COMP-MONODROMY is the only obstruction to an exact equivariant decomposition — the component count alone is not additional information.
