statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let S be a normal finite-type k-scheme carrying a balanced+(CE)+(N) genus-six family as in ATT-0101. For each connected component S_alpha of S, let U_alpha be the reduced-support open of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle over S_alpha and let Z_alpha -> U_alpha be the finite etale right S_6-torsor Ord(U_alpha). Let H_alpha be the image of etale monodromy pi_1^{et}(U_alpha) -> S_6, acting by left multiplication on a trivialized geometric fibre. The statement is scheme-level: it assumes the confirmed ATT-0101 classification (CLM-0101-3, CLM-0101-4) and does not extend to algebraic stacks with inertia (FND-0144). Then the connected components of Z_alpha coincide with its irreducible components and are indexed by the orbit set H_alpha\S_6 of left multiplication (the right cosets H_alpha g). The right deck action is transitive on this set, and the stabilizer of the identity-coset component Z_alpha^1 is exactly H_alpha. Right multiplication by any element of S_6 is a U_alpha-automorphism of Z_alpha, so all components are isomorphic as U_alpha-schemes. The residual H_alpha-action on Z_alpha^1 is free and simply transitive on geometric fibres; Z_alpha^1 -> U_alpha is therefore a connected finite etale cover of degree |H_alpha|, hence a Galois cover with group H_alpha. For any additive functor F from finite-type k-schemes (or their Betti analytifications) to Q-vector spaces or to mixed Hodge structures over Q that is functorial for the right S_6-action — in particular ordinary Betti cohomology H^*(-;Q) and Borel-Moore homology H^{BM}_*(-;Q), each with its mixed Hodge structure — there is a canonical isomorphism of S_6-objects F(Z_alpha) isomorphic to Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} F(Z_alpha^1), where induction is Q[S_6] tensor_{Q[H_alpha]} (-) and the H_alpha-action on F(Z_alpha^1) is the residual deck action. Because |H_alpha| is invertible in Q, the finite-covering transfer identifies F(U_alpha) with F(Z_alpha^1)^{H_alpha}; Frobenius reciprocity then gives F(Z_alpha)^{S_6} isomorphic to F(Z_alpha^1)^{H_alpha} isomorphic to F(U_alpha). Two consequences, with the hypotheses above retained. (i) The S_6-isotypic decomposition of F(Z_alpha) is determined by the pair consisting of the subgroup H_alpha and the H_alpha-object F(Z_alpha^1); the component count [S_6:H_alpha] is not independent data. Computing H_alpha (GAP-COMP-MONODROMY) determines the induction functor but does not compute F(Z_alpha^1) as an H_alpha-object, which remains a separate geometric and Hodge input (GAP-TATE). (ii) The isomorphism is purely formal and upgrades nothing to Tate type: it is compatible with F(Z_alpha^1) carrying non-Tate summands (FND-0053). It is stated with Q-coefficients on schemes, so it carries none of the integral-coefficient or coarse-space content excluded by FND-0075.

adjudication_reason: MANDATORY FIRST READS. ATT-0103 (argument_markdown Sections 3-4 and 2.2, claims CLM-0103-3/4/5, gap_markers, theorem_scope) and REV-0152 (checked_claims for CLM-0103-4 and CLM-0103-5, proof_dependency_checks, strongest_attack) were read in full before the packet and the findings backlog. The contested passage is ATT-0103 Proposition 5 together with Lemma 3; REV-0152 records both as 'confirmed' and its strongest_attack is aimed at Part (E), not at the dichotomy. INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVATION ON THE PARENT (no grok worker was used: TASK.json lists 'grok' in excluded_engines and REV-0152 is grok-authored, so using the offered grok helper would have re-imported the very engine whose review is under audit). (1) deg phi_L divides 6 and nondegeneracy of the complete system forces deg X_L >= 2, so deg phi_L is in {1,2,3}; deg phi_L = 6 is degenerate. (2) deg phi_L = 3 gives an integral plane conic, which is necessarily smooth (a singular conic is reducible or non-reduced), hence isomorphic to P^1, hence L = T^{tensor 2} for a base-point-free g^1_3 T. Lemma 3 excludes this; I re-derived its two load-bearing steps. Step 1: omega_C - 2D = 4T - omega_C has degree 2, and h^0 = 1 would give D ~ 2T - A with A effective of degree two; a case analysis on t(A) yields either h^0(D) = 1 or a base point of |D|, both impossible since D = gamma^*O(1) is a base-point-free pencil with h^0(D) = 2. Hence h^0(2D) = chi(2D) = 3, so sum_i (3-a_i)_+ = 0, and with a_i >= 2 and sum a_i = 9 this forces E = O(3)^{+3}. Step 2: E(-3) = O^{+3} sits in gamma_*L with h^0 = 3 = h^0(L), so the CE generators xi_i are a basis of H^0(L) and the restriction map of the balancedness criterion IS the multiplication Sym^2 H^0(L) -> H^0(L^{tensor 2}); since H^0(L) = t^*H^0(O_{P^1}(2)) the image lies in t^*H^0(O_{P^1}(4)) of dimension five, source dimension six, so h^0(F(-6)) >= 1 and (BAL) fails. Both steps check out. (3) deg phi_L = 2 with X_L a singular cubic: normalization P^1, and C smooth lifts, giving a degree-two map C -> P^1, i.e. C hyperelliptic; this is excluded by the IMPORTED ATT-0088/CLM-0088-2 (= FND-0125, FND-0142), not by anything proved in ATT-0103. (4) deg phi_L = 2 with X_L smooth: Y := X_L is elliptic, psi is a degree-two morphism of smooth curves, char 0 makes it Galois with psi_*O_C = O_Y + M^{-1}; Riemann-Hurwitz 10 = 2(2g(Y)-2) + deg B gives deg B = 10 and deg M = 5; omega_Y = O_Y gives omega_C = psi^*(omega_Y tensor M) = psi^*M; L = psi^*N with N = O_{P^2}(1)|_Y of degree three; D = omega_C - L = psi^*(M tensor N^{-1}) = psi^*P with deg P = 2; h^0(psi^*P) = h^0(P) + h^0(P tensor M^{-1}) = 2 + 0 = 2 = h^0(D), so |D| = psi^*|P| and gamma = q o psi with q = phi_{|P|}. The splitting E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4) follows from h^0(D) = 2 (a_i >= 2) and h^0(2D) = h^0(2P) + h^0(2P - M) = 4 + 0 = 4, i.e. sum_i (3-a_i)_+ = 1, whose unique solution with sum a_i = 9 and a_i >= 2 is (2,3,4); (2,2,5) gives 2 and (3,3,3) gives 0. All verified. CORRECTIONS APPLIED TO THE CANDIDATE TEXT (the original is therefore not promoted unchanged). (a) The candidate omits the standing hypotheses that k is algebraically closed of characteristic zero and that gamma is a finite flat degree-four cover with the stated CE data; char 0 is load-bearing for psi_*O_C = O_Y + M^{-1} and for the imported hyperelliptic exclusion, so it is now explicit. (b) 'L = psi^*O_Y(1)' and 'q = phi_{|M tensor O(1)^{-1}|}' use non-intrinsic notation; corrected to L = psi^*N with N = O_{P^2}(1)|_Y in Pic^3(Y) and q = phi_{|P|} with P = M tensor N^{-1} in Pic^2(Y). (c) The candidate's list of 'excluded alternatives' conflates alternatives internal to the dichotomy (deg phi_L in {3,6}, singular cubic image) with two facts of different status: C hyperelliptic is an IMPORTED dependency (ATT-0088/CLM-0088-2), not proved by this lemma, and 'C is not a smooth plane quintic' is an antecedent used to prove base-point-freeness (ATT-0103 Lemma 2, FND-0130), not an alternative for phi_L once L is base-point-free. The adjudicated statement separates the three. (d) The candidate's one-line summary of the trigonal exclusion omits its two load-bearing steps (h^0(4T - omega_C) = 0, and that the xi_i form a basis of H^0(L) so that the restriction map is the multiplication map); both are now stated, since without them 'lands inside the five-dimensional t^*H^0(O(4))' is not justified. (e) MOST SUBSTANTIVE: the closing clause 'primitivity of gamma is not available on the whole balanced locus' does NOT follow from the dichotomy, which only fails to exclude type (ii). It is a non-emptiness assertion requiring ATT-0103 Part (E), separately adjudicated as packet finding FND-0154. The clause is retained but re-attributed rather than asserted as a consequence of the dichotomy. CROSS-CHECKS AGAINST THE PACKET. FND-0154 (corroborated) independently records, for every bielliptic-composed cover of the stated type, E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4) and F = O(4)+O(5); this corroborates the type-(ii) splitting-type clause from the opposite direction (construction rather than classification) and shows the two are consistent. FND-0155 (corroborated) is stated in terms of 'type (i)' and 'type (ii)' but the packet does not otherwise define those labels, so promoting the present finding removes a dangling reference rather than duplicating one; FND-0155 is a monodromy statement and FND-0154 an existence statement, so neither is a merge target (merge_target_id null). No conflict with FND-0130, FND-0134, FND-0139, FND-0142, FND-0125. The slip REV-0152 itself flags (connectedness of the ordering torsor equated with transitivity on six letters) lies in the monodromy claim CLM-0103-6 and was already corrected inside FND-0155; it is not load-bearing for the dichotomy. GAP-0103-3 correctly notes that composites through intermediate genus two or three, if balanced, must be type (i) by degree reasons, so the dichotomy is not weakened by that open case. INDEPENDENT PUBLIC-LITERATURE CHECKS. (i) Bopp-Hoff (arXiv:1807.05121, ar5iv HTML) defines a bundle +_j O(a_j) on P^1 to be balanced iff max_{i,j}|a_j - a_i| <= 1, records that Casnati-Ekedahl [CE96] generalized the relative canonical resolution to finite Gorenstein covers of degree k, and gives deg(N_i) = (g-k-1)(k-2-i)*binom(k-2,i-1) for the syzygy bundles in the scroll normalization. For k = 4, i = 1 this is rank two and degree g-5 = 1 at g = 6; the campaign convention differs by the twist E_scroll = E(-2), under which F = N(4) has degree 1 + 8 = 9 = g+3, matching deg E = 9 and making O(4)+O(5) exactly the balanced splitting type of a rank-two degree-nine bundle. This independently validates the rank/degree numerology on which Lemma 1(4) and both section-count exclusions rest. (ii) Castelnuovo-Severi (Theorem 14 of arXiv:2306.17772, ar5iv HTML: if g(X) > m*g(Y) + n*g(Z) + (m-1)(n-1) then both maps factor through a common cover of degree > 1) gives two consistency checks on type (ii) that the candidate does not perform. A type-(ii) curve has a degree-two map to an elliptic curve; were it also hyperelliptic, 6 > 2*1 + 2*0 + 1 = 3 would force a common degree-two factor X' with Y = X' = P^1, absurd; were it trigonal, 6 > 2*1 + 3*0 + 2 = 4 would force a common factor of degree dividing both 2 and 3, absurd. Hence type-(ii) curves are automatically neither hyperelliptic nor trigonal, so type (ii) neither collides with the imported hyperelliptic exclusion nor secretly re-enters through the excluded case L = T^{tensor 2}. No contradiction was found with any cross-checked claim; the residual defects are the scope and attribution corrections listed above, all of which are now carried in the adjudicated statement. VERDICT RATIONALE: promote (with the corrected statement). The two sibling candidates of REV-0152 are already promoted in packet C66-001-v4, the proof is complete and independently re-derived here, the exclusions are exhaustive, and the only overreach (the primitivity clause) is repaired by attribution rather than by retirement.

statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, C a smooth projective connected curve of genus six over k, and gamma : C -> P^1 a finite flat morphism of degree four with gamma_*O_C = O_{P^1} + E^vee, E locally free of rank three and degree nine, i : C -> X = P(E^vee) the relative-canonical (Casnati-Ekedahl) embedding and p : X -> P^1 with p_*O_X(1) = E. Assume (CE) the standard degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl ideal resolution 0 -> O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F -> O_X(-2) tensor p^*F -> I_C -> 0 with F locally free of rank two (necessarily of degree nine under (CE)+(N)); (N) O_X(1)|_C isomorphic to omega_C tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(2); and (BAL) F isomorphic to O_{P^1}(4) + O_{P^1}(5). Put D := gamma^*O_{P^1}(1) and L := omega_C(-D), so that deg L = 6 and h^0(L) = 3 (imported from ATT-0088/CLM-0088-1 and CLM-0088-3, FND-0139, FND-0142), and assume L is base-point-free -- an assumption that is automatic under (CE)+(N)+(BAL) by FND-0130, FND-0134 and ATT-0103 Proposition 4, whose proof needs the exclusion of the smooth plane quintic. THEN phi_L : C -> P^2 = P(H^0(L)^vee) is a finite morphism onto an integral nondegenerate plane curve X_L with deg(phi_L) * deg(X_L) = 6, and exactly one of the following two mutually exclusive cases occurs. TYPE (i): deg phi_L = 1, X_L is an integral plane sextic of geometric genus six (arithmetic genus ten, total delta invariant four), and phi_L : C -> X_L is its normalization. TYPE (ii): deg phi_L = 2 and X_L is a smooth plane cubic. Writing Y := X_L (an elliptic curve), N := O_{P^2}(1)|_Y in Pic^3(Y) and psi := phi_L : C -> Y, the morphism psi is a bielliptic double cover with psi_*O_C = O_Y + M^{-1} for M in Pic^5(Y) satisfying M^{tensor 2} isomorphic to O_Y(B), B the reduced branch divisor of degree ten; omega_C isomorphic to psi^*M; L isomorphic to psi^*N; D isomorphic to psi^*P with P := M tensor N^{-1} in Pic^2(Y); |D| = psi^*|P|, hence gamma = q o psi up to an automorphism of P^1, where q = phi_{|P|} : Y -> P^1 has degree two; and E isomorphic to O(2) + O(3) + O(4). In particular gamma is non-primitive, factoring through a curve of genus one. EXCLUDED ALTERNATIVES, WITH THEIR STATUS. (1) deg phi_L = 6 is impossible because X_L would be a line, contradicting nondegeneracy of the complete system. (2) deg phi_L = 3 is impossible: X_L would be an integral plane conic, hence smooth and isomorphic to P^1, so L would equal T^{tensor 2} for a base-point-free g^1_3 T; this is excluded by a section count, namely h^0(omega_C - 2D) = h^0(4T - omega_C) = 0 (otherwise D = 2T - A for an effective degree-two A and |D| either fails to be complete of dimension one or acquires a base point, contradicting that D = gamma^*O(1) is a base-point-free pencil with h^0(D) = 2), whence h^0(2D) = 3, sum_i (3 - a_i)_+ = 0 and E is isomorphic to O(3)^{+3}; then E(-3) = O^{+3} identifies the Casnati-Ekedahl generators with a basis of H^0(L), so the balancedness restriction map H^0(Sym^2 E(-6)) -> H^0(L^{tensor 2}) is the multiplication map Sym^2 H^0(L) -> H^0(L^{tensor 2}), whose image lies in the five-dimensional t^*H^0(O_{P^1}(4)) while its source has dimension six; hence h^0(F(-6)) >= 1 and (BAL) fails. (3) A singular cubic image is impossible because its normalization is P^1 and phi_L would lift to a degree-two morphism C -> P^1, making C hyperelliptic; this contradiction uses the IMPORTED result that no balanced (CE)+(BAL) geometric fibre is hyperelliptic (ATT-0088/CLM-0088-2, dual-confirmed by REV-0139 and REV-0142; equivalently FND-0125, which gives F isomorphic to O(2)+O(7) there, and FND-0142). It is not proved by this lemma. (4) Separately, and as an input to base-point-freeness rather than as an alternative inside the dichotomy, no balanced (CE)+(N) fibre is a smooth plane quintic (ATT-0103 Lemma 2, FND-0130): every g^1_4 on a smooth plane quintic is |H - p_0|, so L = H + p_0 has p_0 as a base point, E is isomorphic to O(2)+O(3)+O(4) and the seven-dimensional H^0(Sym^2 E(-6)) maps into the six-dimensional H^0(2H), forcing h^0(F(-6)) >= 1. SCOPE AND LIMITS. This is a statement about a single geometric fibre. It does not assert that C is non-trigonal, only that L is not the square of a base-point-free g^1_3. It does not by itself establish that type (ii) is non-empty: the dichotomy only fails to exclude type (ii), and non-emptiness -- and with it the conclusion that primitivity of gamma is not a property of the balanced locus -- is supplied separately by FND-0154 (ATT-0103 Part (E)), for intermediate genus one only. Non-primitive degree-four pencils through intermediate curves of genus two or three are not analysed; if balanced, such a cover would have to be of type (i), since its phi_L cannot factor through the intermediate curve by degree reasons. Downstream arguments that need phi_L birational -- in particular the type-(i) monodromy computation FND-0155 -- must impose type (i) explicitly. No monodromy, family, stack, Hodge, weight, purity or Tate conclusion is asserted.

adjudication_reason: The mandatory originating artifacts were checked at their contested passages. ATT-0103, CLM-0103-8 and Proposition 12 in §7 assert that the constructed elliptic double covers have E≅O(2)⊕O(3)⊕O(4) and F≅O(4)⊕O(5); its pole/trace proof assumes that the point y_0 defined by O_Y(y_0)≅M⊗P^−2 is unramified for q. REV-0152 explicitly confirms CLM-0103-8 and explains that this assumption is used to show f=nu/mu is not invariant. The review also correctly requires an independent source for the Casnati–Ekedahl embedding and normalization rather than an inference from ATT-0100. Public primary evidence strengthens and corrects the candidate: Casnati–Del Centina 2002, Theorem 1.3 and Proposition 2.1, give the degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl construction and show that a bielliptic genus-six tetragonal cover has scrollar invariants E=(2,3,4) and F=(4,5). Consequently the y_0-unramified condition is sufficient for ATT-0103's particular argument but is not necessary for the published splitting theorem. The candidate's attribution of (N) to SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 also requires correction: that lemma uses the identity O(1)|_C≅omega_C⊗gamma^*O(2) and cites Casnati–Ekedahl 1996, Theorem 2.1(2), which is the proving source. There is no contradiction with the claims backlog. FND-0125 concerns hyperelliptic-composed covers with F≅O(2)⊕O(7); FND-0142 already warns that cohomological constancy does not exclude all positive-genus factorizations; and FND-0150 is a dependency gap for a different genus-two attempt. The result answers only the remaining existence question associated with FND-0104 for a genus-one intermediate curve and does not refute FND-0104's hyperelliptic Clifford-equality statement. No existing corroborated finding states this genus-one existence and splitting result, so merger is inappropriate.

statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. Let Y/k be a smooth genus-one curve, let P∈Pic^2(Y), and let q=phi_|P|:Y→P^1 be the associated degree-two morphism. For M∈Pic^5(Y) and a reduced divisor B∈|M^⊗2|, let psi:C→Y be the double cover with psi_*O_C≅O_Y⊕M^−1 and branch divisor B, and put gamma=q∘psi. Then C is smooth and connected of genus six, gamma is finite flat Gorenstein of degree four, and its Casnati–Ekedahl bundles split as E≅O_P^1(2)⊕O_P^1(3)⊕O_P^1(4) and F≅O_P^1(4)⊕O_P^1(5). In the standard relative-canonical convention, O_P(E^∨)(1)|_C≅omega_C⊗gamma^*O_P^1(2), det F≅det E, and the ideal has the degree-four Casnati–Ekedahl resolution 0→O_X(−4)⊗p^*det E→O_X(−2)⊗p^*F→I_C→0. Thus a non-primitive tetragonal pencil factoring through a genus-one curve can lie in the balanced F-locus, so primitivity is not a property of that locus. The extra ATT-0103 condition that the unique y_0 with O_Y(y_0)≅M⊗P^−2 be unramified for q is required only by that attempt's pole/trace proof and is not a hypothesis of this adjudicated statement. This establishes existence only for intermediate genus one; it does not address intermediate genera two or three, purely composed connected components of a balanced base, or the exact monodromy image inside S_2 wr S_3.

adjudication_reason: No contradictions identified. REV-0152 confirmed all nine claims of ATT-0103 and all proof dependency checks. One non-load-bearing wording issue was identified: ATT-0103 Proposition 10 states 'Connectedness of the torsor Ord(|L|^{rs}) is equivalent to transitivity of G on the six points', which is technically incorrect (A_6 is transitive but would give two connected components of the torsor). However, since G=S_6 is already established by the 2-transitivity + transposition + Jordan argument, connectedness follows correctly from G=S_6 via the FND-0148/FND-0151 orbit-component correspondence. This slip is corrected in the adjudicated statement. Local evidence from ATT-0103 (Lemmas 6-9, Proposition 10, Proposition 13) and REV-0152 (checked_claims for CLM-0103-6 and CLM-0103-9) is fully consistent and mutually reinforcing. The Jordan step as applied (p=2, n=6) matches the fetched public statement with p < n - 2 = 4, and the biduality step matches the fetched involution statement for the dual curve.
pre_adjudication_statement: On a balanced type-(i) geometric fibre the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs})->S_6 is the full symmetric group: the point-line incidence is an irreducible P^1-bundle (transitivity); after deleting the diagonal and the finite coincidence locus over non-normal points of the sextic, the ordered-pair incidence is irreducible and dominant of degree 30 (2-transitivity, hence primitivity); a general tangent line is a simple tangency at a smooth point of the dual curve (a transposition, using characteristic-zero reflexivity of the Gauss map and nonvanishing of the Wronskian of the complete g^2_6); Jordan's theorem then gives S_6, so the ordering torsor is connected. Over any connected component S_alpha of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base that contains at least one type-(i) geometric fibre, functoriality of pi_1^{et} along U_b -> U_alpha forces H_alpha=S_6, hence Z_alpha is connected; if U_alpha is additionally normal, integral and locally Noetherian then Z_alpha is irreducible, [S_6:H_alpha]=1, and the FND-0152 induction functor is the identity. This computes the monodromy image left open by FND-0148 and FND-0152, but only on components that meet the type-(i) locus. In type (ii) the image lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6. The statement upgrades nothing to Tate type (FND-0053, FND-0152(ii)), does not apply to algebraic stacks with inertia (FND-0144), and does not determine H_alpha on a purely type-(ii) component.

statement: On a balanced type-(i) geometric fibre (satisfying (CE)+(N)+(BAL) at (g,n)=(6,6) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero), the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs}) -> S_6 is the full symmetric group S_6. The proof proceeds: (1) the point-line incidence is an irreducible P^1-bundle over C, giving transitivity; (2) after deleting the diagonal and the finite coincidence locus Sigma over non-normal points of the plane sextic X_L, the ordered-pair incidence is irreducible of dimension two and dominant of generic degree 30 over |L|^{rs}, giving 2-transitivity and hence primitivity; (3) a general tangent line is a simple tangency at a smooth point of the dual curve X_L^vee (using characteristic-zero reflexivity/biduality of the Gauss map and non-vanishing of the Wronskian of the complete base-point-free g^2_6, which has degree 48), yielding a transposition via local monodromy; (4) Jordan's theorem (in the form: a primitive subgroup of S_n containing a p-cycle for a prime p < n - 2 is S_n or A_n; applied with p = 2, where the transposition is odd, so the image is S_6, not A_6) gives G=S_6. Consequently the finite etale S_6-torsor Ord(|L|^{rs}) is connected (equivalently, the monodromy orbit set has a single element, which for a right S_6-torsor is equivalent to G=S_6, not merely to transitivity). Over any connected component S_alpha of a reduced locally Noetherian balanced+(CE)+(N) base that contains at least one type-(i) geometric fibre, functoriality of pi_1^{et} along the closed inclusion U_b -> U_alpha forces H_alpha = im(pi_1^{et}(U_alpha) -> S_6) = S_6, hence Z_alpha is connected. If U_alpha is additionally normal, integral, and locally Noetherian, then Z_alpha is irreducible, [S_6:H_alpha]=1, and the FND-0152 induction functor Ind_{H_alpha}^{S_6} is the identity. In type (ii), the monodromy image lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_3 of order 48 and is not S_6. This result computes the monodromy image left open by FND-0148 and FND-0152, but only on components meeting the type-(i) locus. It upgrades nothing to Tate type (per FND-0053, FND-0152(ii)), does not apply to algebraic stacks with inertia (FND-0144), and does not determine H_alpha on a purely type-(ii) component.

adjudication_reason: MANDATORY FIRST READS. ATT-0104 (theorem_statement, theorem_scope, argument_markdown steps 1-2, CLM-0104-1/2) and REV-0153 (checked_claims CLM-0104-1/2, strongest_attack, finding_candidates[0] key FC-C66-CE-CONVENTION-RANK-BLIND) were read in full before the packet and the findings backlog. The contested passage is the undefined referent 'the canonical filtered relations bundle' 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 in the ATT-0104 theorem_statement, together with L=W_5 tensor omega^{-1} and the rank table in clause (2). REV-0153 confirms ATT-0104: the strongest_attack tests the naive reading W=gamma^*F with HN filtration, finds that this wrong reading still satisfies clause (2) in full, and fails only in clause (1); the attack is not a refutation because the artifact is hash-bound to the packet CE convention, FND-0097, and CLM-0065-5. The observation is retained as a statement-hygiene finding, not as a refutation of ATT-0104. INDEPENDENT ARITHMETIC. Packet/CE: W=i^*(O_X(2) tensor p^*F^vee), W_f=(O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|_C. SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 (Canning-Larson arXiv:2208.02357v2, independently retrieved from ar5iv HTML, Section 10.3) defines W:=O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*F^vee and computes deg(W_{f_i}|_C)=2(2g-2+8)-4f_i=4g+12-4f_i, hence at g=6, f=4,5 one has deg W_4=20, deg W_5=16, deg W=36. Both degrees exceed 2g-2=10, so h^1(W)=0 and h^0(W)=chi(W)=36+2(1-6)=26; restriction to a reduced degree-six Gamma has rank 12; N=omega tensor W_5^vee(Gamma) has degree 10-16+6=0; d_4-n=14>10 and d_5-n=10=2g-2, so fibre rank is 11 or 12, I_j=O for j<=11, and Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e holds for this N. Naive: W'=gamma^*F with HN filtration 0->gamma^*O(5)->W'->gamma^*O(4)->0, sub degree 4*5=20, quotient degree 4*4=16. The same numerical list is obtained, with N' of degree 0 and the Fitting identity for the corresponding a_{N'}. PRIMARY-SOURCE SIGN SLIP, not a merge into the finding: Lemma 10.6's sentence 'set W_{f_i}=O(2) tensor gamma^*O(f_i)' omits the dual sign, while both the opening definition W=O(2) tensor gamma^*F^vee and the degree line use O(-f_i). The packet minus sign is the consistent convention; a literal reading of that one sentence would give entirely different degrees and is not the naive reading under audit. WORDING CORRECTION. The candidate asserts that h^0(L')=1+h^0(2K-4D) equals 3 only if 5D isomorphic to 2K. Independently: L'=O(4D-K)=L tensor O(5D-2K), so L' isomorphic to L iff 5D isomorphic to 2K; chi(L')=1 yields h^0(L')=1+h^0(2K-4D), hence h^0(L')=3 iff h^0(2K-4D)=2. The isomorphism implies the h^0 equality on balanced fibres (h^0(D)=2), but the converse is strictly weaker (2K-4D some g^1_4, not necessarily |D|). Neither 5D isomorphic to 2K nor h^0(2K-4D)=2 is supplied by (CE)+(BAL)+(N); the hyperelliptic composed case 5D isomorphic to 2K is excluded from the balanced locus by corroborated FND-0125. Fit_0=a_N^*I_e holds formally in each reading, but N and therefore V(Fit_0) differ when L is not isomorphic to L'. NO CLAIM-LEVEL CONTRADICTION: contradicts_claim_ids is empty; the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. Compatible with THM-0005 (c(6)=5, so n=6 needs residual CE geometry) and with C66-GEO-COMP. Complementary to, not a restatement of, corroborated FND-0097 (splitting versus HN filtration inside the packet convention) and FND-0105 (packet W_5 isomorphic to omega_C^2(-D) from (N) plus the Lemma 10.6 degree). Compatible with FND-0062, FND-0063, FND-0122, which assume the packet W. Merge target: none. PACKET/CE CONVENTION (SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6, with the dual sign required by W:=O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*F^vee and by the degree line of that lemma, not by the lemma's one-line 'set W_{f_i}=O(2) tensor gamma^*O(f_i)' which omits the minus): W_f=(O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(-f))|_C for f=4,5, filtered as 0->W_4->W->W_5->0 with deg W_4=20 and deg W_5=16. Then deg W=36, h^1(W)=0, h^0(W)=26, restriction to Gamma has rank 12, N:=omega_C tensor W_5^vee(Gamma) has degree 10-16+6=0, both inequalities d_4-n=14>2g-2=10 and d_5-n=10=2g-2 hold, every geometric fibre of phi has rank 11 or 12, I_j(phi)=O for j<=11, and Fit_0(coker phi)=a_N^*I_e holds for this N. NAIVE READING: W':=gamma^*F with Harder-Narasimhan filtration 0->gamma^*O(5)->W'->gamma^*O(4)->0 (sub of degree 20, quotient of degree 16) produces exactly the same numerical list, with N' of degree 0 and the same Fitting identity for the corresponding a_{N'}. Among balanced degree-four covers the degree coincidence deg(gamma^*O(5))=deg W_4=20 and deg(gamma^*O(4))=deg W_5=16 holds if and only if g=6. A pencil target arising from a g^1_4 is of the form P(V) for a rank-two vector bundle V, hence is Zariski-locally trivial (Stacks Project tag 0FMS: P(E) trivializes over affines on which E is free). statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let C be a smooth projective connected curve over k and let gamma : C -> P^1 be a finite morphism of degree four. Call gamma simply branched when every geometric fibre has at most one ramification point and that point, if present, has ramification index two; equivalently, every local monodromy permutation in S_4 is a transposition. (a) No such gamma that factors nontrivially through an intermediate smooth projective curve is simply branched. A nontrivial factorization is a pair of finite morphisms C -> Y -> P^1 each of degree at least two (necessarily both of degree two); equivalently, k(C)/k(P^1) is composite of two proper extensions and the monodromy representation of pi_1^et(P^1 minus the branch locus of gamma) in S_4 is imprimitive. Two independent reasons. First: a simply branched connected degree-four cover has all local monodromies transpositions, so its monodromy group G <= S_4 is transitive and generated by transpositions. A transitive subgroup of S_n generated by transpositions equals S_n, because the undirected graph on n letters with those transpositions as edges is connected and the transpositions of a connected graph generate S_n. Thus G = S_4, which is primitive on four letters. A nontrivial factorization supplies a G-invariant partition of a general fibre into two blocks of size two, so G lies in a conjugate of the imprimitive wreath product S_2 wr S_2 of order 8, contradicting G = S_4. (The wreath product contains the two within-block transpositions, but those generate an intransitive Klein subgroup; transitivity of an imprimitive degree-four group requires a block-swapping element, necessarily a double transposition or a 4-cycle.) Second, without invoking S_4: any degree-two morphism q : Y -> P^1 from a smooth projective connected curve Y is ramified, since Riemann-Hurwitz gives 2g_Y-2 = 2(-2)+deg R_q, hence deg R_q = 2g_Y+2 >= 2. Over each branch value of q the fibre of gamma = q o psi is of type (2,2) if psi is etale over the unique point of Y above it, or of type 4 (local monodromy a 4-cycle; locally the composition of two simple ramified double covers is z |-> z^4) if psi is ramified there; neither fibre is a transposition. (b) Specialise to the FND-0154 balanced type-(ii) family: Y a smooth genus-one curve, P in Pic^2(Y), q = phi_{|P|} : Y -> P^1 the associated finite flat degree-two morphism (four ramification points), M in Pic^5(Y), B a reduced divisor in |M^{otimes 2}| of degree ten, psi : C -> Y the double cover with psi_* O_C isomorphic to O_Y direct-sum M^{-1} branched along B, and gamma = q o psi. Assume in addition that B is disjoint from Ram(q) and that sigma(B) cap B is empty for the unique nontrivial deck involution sigma of q. Then the branch locus of gamma consists of exactly fourteen points of P^1: ten of fibre type 2+1+1 (local monodromy a transposition, over q(b) for b in B) and four of fibre type (2,2) (local monodromy a double transposition, over the four branch values of q, because psi is etale above each q-ramification point so both of its preimages acquire ramification index two). In characteristic zero the different has multiplicity d_x = e_x-1 at each ramification point, so the total ramification is 10*1 + 4*2 = 18. This agrees with Riemann-Hurwitz 2g_C-2 = 4(2g_{P^1}-2)+deg R, i.e. 10 = -8 + deg R. If B meets Ram(q), the corresponding fibre of gamma is a single point of ramification index four, with local monodromy a 4-cycle. If B contains a sigma-pair, the two would-be transposition fibres over q(b) and q(sigma(b)) coincide as a single extra (2,2) fibre. In particular the set of simply branched type-(ii) points is empty, so no deformation argument that requires eighteen distinct simple branch values, or etaleness of the fixed-target Hurwitz scheme over Conf_18 at a type-(ii) point, can apply to any point of the FND-0154 parameter space. This statement asserts neither that every type-(ii) point of the ambient fixed-target balanced Hurwitz scheme lies on a component meeting type (i), nor any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, stack-inertia, or RED-0001 conclusion.

statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let gamma : C -> P^1 be a finite morphism of degree d from a smooth geometrically connected projective k-curve C of genus g, with the target P^1 held fixed (not taken modulo Aut(P^1)). Then the differential d(gamma) : T_C -> gamma^* T_{P^1} is injective as a map of line bundles, so the Hurwitz normal sheaf N_gamma := coker(d(gamma)) is a torsion coherent sheaf supported on the ramification locus of gamma. Its length equals deg(gamma^* T_{P^1}) - deg(T_C) = 2d + 2g - 2, independently of the ramification profile, and equivalently equals sum_p (e_p - 1) by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula. A coherent sheaf of zero-dimensional support on a Noetherian curve has vanishing H^1, so H^1(C, N_gamma)=0. Consequently the deformation functor of C as a finite P^1-scheme (equivalently, of the pair (C, gamma) with varying source and fixed target, modulo automorphisms of the source over P^1) is unobstructed, with tangent space H^0(C, N_gamma) of k-dimension 2d+2g-2. Therefore the Deligne-Mumford stack of finite degree-d covers of a fixed P^1 by smooth connected genus-g curves -- equivalently the smooth-domain open of the Kontsevich stack M_{g,0}(P^1, d) -- is smooth of dimension 2d+2g-2 at every such point, independently of the ramification profile. For (d,g)=(4,6) this dimension is 18. This is a statement about the unrestricted stack of all ramification types. It is distinct from the classical Hurwitz space of covers with a fixed number r of distinct branch values (or a fixed ramification profile), which is etale over the configuration space of r points and has dimension r; that dimension equals 2d+2g-2 if and only if the cover is simply branched. In particular the unrestricted smoothness statement applies at composed or imprimitive points, which are never simply branched. Finite residual automorphisms, such as the deck involution of a composed cover, give Deligne-Mumford inertia with vanishing Lie algebra and do not change the stack dimension. The statement does not assert closedness of the composed or type-(ii) locus, irreducibility or equidimensionality of the balanced Hurwitz scheme, regularity of the coarse space at stacky points, smoothness of the Aut(P^1)-quotient (dimension 2d+2g-5), or any Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, or RED-0001 conclusion.

pre_adjudication_statement: The normality hypothesis that FND-0132, FND-0144 and FND-0148 attach to the '[S_6:H] irreducible components of degree |H|' formula can be removed on the C66-GEO-COMP model, over a base S that is reduced and locally Noetherian but possibly non-normal and reducible, by counting at the generic point of each irreducible component rather than on the whole base. Concretely: let S_beta be an irreducible component of S with its reduced structure, eta its generic point, U_beta = U x_S S_beta and U_eta the generic fibre. Because U -> S is smooth with fibres open in P^2, U_beta is integral and U_eta is an OPEN SUBSCHEME OF P^2_{kappa(eta)}, hence normal and integral, with K(U_beta) = K(U_eta). Therefore Gal(K(U_beta)) surjects onto pi_1^et(U_eta), the number of field factors of the etale S_6-algebra Z_{K(U_beta)} equals [S_6 : H_gen] for H_gen the image of Gal(K(U_beta)) in S_6, and every irreducible component of the finite etale Z|_{U_beta} dominates U_beta (finite morphism, equidimensional of dim U_beta), so field factors correspond exactly to irreducible components. H_gen is then squeezed between the geometric monodromy of the geometric generic fibre U_{eta-bar} (computable by the single-fibre theorems, since kappa(eta)-bar is algebraically closed of characteristic zero) and any globally defined structure the family carries over S_beta.

statement: Let k be a field of characteristic zero and let S be a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme, possibly reducible and non-normal, carrying a balanced (CE)+(N)+(BAL) genus-six degree-four family so that U is the distinct-support open of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle AJ=P_S(pi_*L) and Z->U is the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings. The statement is scheme-level and does not apply to algebraic stacks with inertia (FND-0144 stands). Let S_beta be an irreducible component of S with its reduced structure, eta its generic point, U_beta=U x_S S_beta, and U_eta the generic fibre of U_beta->S_beta. Then: (1) U->S is smooth of pure relative dimension two. The fibre of AJ over eta is isomorphic to P((pi_*L)_eta) isomorphic to P^2_{kappa(eta)} (Stacks 01OA, 0FCY), and U_eta is a nonempty open subscheme of that P^2, hence regular, normal, and integral, with K(U_beta)=K(U_eta). (2) Because U_eta is normal integral, Gal(K(U_beta)^sep/K(U_beta)) surjects onto pi_1^et(U_eta) (Stacks 0BQI, 0BQM, using 0BQ3). The image H_gen of Gal(K(U_beta))->S_6 therefore equals the arithmetic monodromy image of pi_1^et(U_eta)->S_6. (3) Finite etale morphisms are flat, so every generic point of Z|_{U_beta} maps to the generic point of the integral scheme U_beta (Stacks 03HV). Equivalently, Z|_{U_beta} is finite locally free over a domain, so field factors of the etale S_6-algebra Z_{K(U_beta)} biject with irreducible components of Z|_{U_beta}. The number of those field factors is [S_6:H_gen], with components indexed by the orbit set H_gen\S_6 of left multiplication (FND-0151). (4) This does not remove the normality hypotheses of FND-0132 and FND-0148 for identifying Irr(Z) with pi_0(Z), and it does not license the unmodified formula '[S_6:H] irreducible components of degree |H|' with H=im(pi_1^et(U_beta)->S_6). In general a connected finite etale cover of a connected locally Noetherian non-normal scheme need not be irreducible (Stacks 0357 and 0BQL use normality for connected implying integral). The bypass is that normality is used on U_eta, where it holds automatically because U_eta is an open in a P^2 over a field, not that U_beta itself is unibranch. (5) Write H_pi1=im(pi_1^et(U_beta)->S_6) and H_geom=im(pi_1^et(U_{eta-bar})->S_6), where kappa(eta)-bar is algebraically closed of characteristic zero so that single-fibre monodromy theorems apply to the geometric generic fibre. Functoriality gives H_geom subseteq H_gen and H_geom subseteq H_pi1. Any structure defined over all of S_beta (in particular the relative 2+2+2 block system over the closed type-(ii) locus S_ii) constrains both H_gen and H_pi1. If the geometric generic fibre is type (i), FND-0155 gives H_geom=S_6, hence H_gen=H_pi1=S_6, so Z|_{U_beta} is connected and irreducible and finite etale of degree 720 over U_beta. If the geometric generic fibre is type (ii) and, separately, its geometric monodromy image is exactly W=S_2 wr S_3, then H_geom=W together with the global block system forces H_gen=H_pi1=W, so Z|_{U_beta} has fifteen connected components, each irreducible, each finite etale of degree 48 over U_beta. The exact type-(ii) image W is not part of this lemma; without it the irreducible-component count is still [S_6:H_gen] with H_geom subseteq H_gen subseteq H_global. (6) Over a non-algebraically-closed ground field, H_gen is arithmetic monodromy of U_eta over kappa(eta) as in FND-0148 and FND-0149. Absolute dimension of each listed component is dim(S_beta)+2 when S is locally of finite type over k; without that extra hypothesis the statement is pure relative dimension two. (7) No Hodge, weight, purity, Tate, Borel-Moore, stack-inertia, or RED-0001 conclusion is asserted.

adjudication_reason: Mandatory originating artifacts were checked first. ATT-0111 Section 3 (CLM-0111-4) asserts that on a type-(ii) geometric fibre the etale monodromy image of the six-point ordering cover is exactly W=S_2 wr S_3 of order 48, via a global 2+2+2 block system, Kummer inertia along a general branch-pencil line Delta_b, surjectivity onto S_3 from the irreducible degree-three incidence plus a nonflex tangent, and conjugation generating (S_2)^3. REV-0156 recorded this as the artifact's principal novel content, attacked the discriminant decomposition, the claim that a general point of Delta_b avoids Y^vee, the Kummer computation, the S_3-surjection, and the conjugation step, and confirmed every step; the reviewer's only successful attack was on the unrelated Section 8 / CLM-0111-9 simply-branched Hurwitz deformation, which does not infect Section 3. Independent re-check of that contested passage agrees: H^0(L)=psi^*H^0(N) because deg(N tensor M^{-1})=-2, so |L| is the dual plane and the three psi-fibres over a line section give a monodromy-invariant pairing, hence G is contained in the specific wreath product stabilizing that partition; the discriminant is exactly Y^vee union the ten lines Delta_b; Plücker type (i) for a smooth plane cubic is (d,d*,delta,delta*,kappa,kappa*,g)=(3,6,0,0,0,9,1), so Y^vee is an irreducible degree-six curve (nine cusps, no nodes) and no line Delta_b is a component; local equation z^2=t at a general point of Delta_b is tame of order two in characteristic zero (Stacks tag 0BUA: wild inertia P is trivial when the residue characteristic is zero), hence a within-block transposition; the degree-three incidence is an open in a P^1-bundle over irreducible Y, so remains irreducible over |L|^{rs}; a general nonflex tangent (smooth point of Y^vee, away from B) swaps two blocks, giving a transposition in S_3 rather than a flex 3-cycle, hence image S_3; conjugates of one within-block transposition by lifts of that S_3 fill (S_2)^3, forcing G=W. No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with corroborated FND-0155, which already places type-(ii) monodromy in a conjugate of S_2 wr S_3 and explicitly declines to compute the exact image, and with FND-0154, which lists that exact-image computation among its limitations. It is also compatible with FND-0053 and FND-0152(ii): a permutation-group computation upgrades nothing to Tate type. It does not merge with FND-0155 (type-(i) image S_6 plus type-(ii) containment only). The original candidate text is narrowed: W is the stabilizer of the fibrewise 2+2+2 partition after a block-compatible trivialization, not an unspecified conjugate; Y^vee is recorded as the irreducible Plücker sextic with nine cusps; flex tangents are excluded from the S_3-transposition step; the family clause H_alpha=W is conditionalized on a purely type-(ii) connected component carrying the relative block system of CLM-0111-2; stack inertia, arithmetic monodromy, and Tate upgrades remain out of scope. Public sources independently supply the three load-bearing external ingredients: dual of a smooth cubic has degree 6 and nine inflections/cusps; |A wr_Omega H|=|A|^{|Omega|}|H|, so |S_2 wr S_3|=8*6=48 with imprimitive action on six letters; in characteristic zero the wild inertia of a DVR is trivial, so Kummer inertia of z^2=t is cyclic of order two.
pre_adjudication_statement: On a balanced type-(ii) geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero (hypotheses (CE)+(N)+(BAL) at (g,n) = (6,6), with psi : C -> Y the bielliptic double cover of the smooth plane cubic Y, reduced branch divisor B of degree ten, N = O_{P^2}(1)|_Y and L = psi^*N), the geometric monodromy image of pi_1^et(|L|^{rs}) -> S_6 is EXACTLY the wreath product W = S_2 wr S_3 of order 48, not merely contained in it. The proof is: (1) H^0(L) = psi^*H^0(N) exactly, since h^0(N) = 3 and h^0(N tensor M^{-1}) = 0 (degree -2), so |L| is the dual plane and the three fibres of psi over a line section give a global 2+2+2 block system, whence G <= W; (2) the discriminant is Y^vee union the ten lines Delta_b (b in B), Delta_b is not a component of the irreducible degree-six Y^vee, and Kummer inertia at a general point of Delta_b -- where the moving intersection point of the line with Y is a uniformizer on a transverse trait and psi is simply ramified at b -- is a within-block transposition; (3) the degree-three block cover is the restriction of the P^1-bundle over the irreducible Y, hence irreducible, giving transitivity in S_3, and a general nonflex tangent to Y away from B swaps two blocks, giving a transposition, so the image in S_3 is all of S_3; (4) conjugating the within-block transposition by lifts of the transitive S_3-image gives all three within-block transpositions, which generate the kernel (S_2)^3, and together with surjectivity onto S_3 and containment in W this forces G = W.

statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let C/k be a smooth projective connected curve of genus six, and let gamma:C->P^1 be a finite flat degree-four cover satisfying (CE), (N), and (BAL) as in FND-0153. Assume the geometric fibre is of type (ii) in the sense of FND-0153: phi_L:C->P^2 is a finite morphism of degree two onto a smooth plane cubic Y, with N=O_{P^2}(1)|_Y in Pic^3(Y), psi=phi_L:C->Y a bielliptic double cover, psi_*O_C=O_Y direct-sum M^{-1} for M in Pic^5(Y), and reduced branch divisor B of degree ten (the degree is forced by Riemann-Hurwitz: 2g_C-2=2(2g_Y-2)+deg B). Then L isomorphic to psi^*N. Moreover H^0(L)=psi^*H^0(N) exactly, because h^0(N)=3 and h^0(N tensor M^{-1})=0 (deg(N tensor M^{-1})=3-5=-2), so the complete linear system |L| is canonically identified with the dual plane (P^2)^vee. Let |L|^{rs} denote the reduced-support open in |L|, equivalently the complement of the discriminant. The three fibres of psi over the three points of a general line section of Y determine a 2+2+2 partition of the six moving points. Write W for the wreath product S_2 wr S_3=(S_2)^3 rtimes S_3 of order 2^3 * 3!=48 that stabilizes this partition in its imprimitive action on six letters. After a block-compatible trivialization of the finite etale S_6-torsor Ord(|L|^{rs})->|L|^{rs}, the geometric monodromy image G=im(pi_1^{et}(|L|^{rs})->S_6) equals this W, not merely a proper subgroup of a conjugate of W. The argument is: (1) the partition is monodromy-invariant, so G is contained in W; (2) a member psi^*(ell cap Y) is non-reduced if and only if ell is tangent to Y or ell meets B, so the discriminant is Y^vee union (union over b in B of Delta_b), where Delta_b is the line in the dual plane parametrizing lines through b; for a smooth plane cubic the Plücker characters are (d,d^*,delta,delta^*,kappa,kappa^*,g)=(3,6,0,0,0,9,1), hence Y^vee is an irreducible curve of degree six with nine cusps and no nodes, so no Delta_b is a component of Y^vee; at a general point of any Delta_b the moving line is transverse to Y at b and cuts Y at b+y_2+y_3 with y_2,y_3 distinct and off B; on a transverse strictly henselian trait the moving intersection with Y is a uniformizer through b, and since psi is simply ramified at b one may take local coordinates with psi given by u=z^2, so after adjusting the trait parameter by a unit the two corresponding sheets satisfy z^2=t while the other four remain etale; in characteristic zero the wild inertia of a discrete valuation ring is trivial, hence tame/Kummer inertia is cyclic of order two and interchanges exactly those two sheets, so G contains a within-block transposition; this transposition source is nonempty because deg B=10>0 (an etale double cover of an elliptic curve would have genus one, not six); (3) the degree-three block cover recording a point of ell cap Y is the restriction to |L|^{rs} of the P^1-bundle of lines through a point of the irreducible cubic Y, hence is geometrically irreducible, so the image of G in S_3 is transitive; a general nonflex simple tangent to Y away from B (equivalently, a general smooth point of Y^vee) coalesces two intersection points of Y while psi is etale, and a transverse trait therefore swaps two blocks, giving a transposition in S_3; thus the image in S_3 is all of S_3 (flex tangents, corresponding to the nine cusps of Y^vee, would give 3-cycles in S_3 and are excluded); (4) conjugating the within-block transposition by lifts in G of that transitive S_3-image produces the within-block transposition in each of the three blocks, which generate ker(W->S_3)=(S_2)^3; together with surjectivity onto S_3 and containment in W this forces G=W. If S_alpha is a connected component of a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme carrying a balanced+(CE)+(N) family and every geometric fibre of S_alpha is type (ii), then the relative 2+2+2 block system coming from the constant-rank cubic kernel forces H_alpha to be contained in this same W, and restriction to any geometric fibre has image W, hence H_alpha=W. This statement does not apply to algebraic stacks with inertia, does not determine H_alpha on a component that meets type (i) (there H_alpha=S_6 by FND-0155), does not assert non-emptiness of type (ii) beyond FND-0154, and upgrades nothing to Tate type.

REV-0157 (qwen) confirmed all eight claims, recorded that the strongest attack (failure of smoothness/pure dimension 18 of the unrestricted fixed-target stack at highly ramified or composed points) fails because in characteristic zero d(gamma):T_C -> gamma^* T_{P^1} is an injective map of line bundles, N_gamma is torsion of length 2g+2d-2=18, and H^1(N_gamma)=0, so the deformation complex is quasi-isomorphic to N_gamma[0] independently of ramification profile; secondary attacks on openness of H^bal, on the composed-locus bound, and on the redundant discriminant bound also failed. Packet-adjudicated inputs FND-0153, FND-0154, FND-0155, FND-0158, FND-0159, FND-0125, FND-0130, FND-0134, FND-0142, FND-0144 are corroborated and are used within their stated scopes. No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001; it is compatible with THM-0005 (c(6)=5, so n=6 lies outside the published CKgP range and residual geometry on the tetragonal Hurwitz stack remains necessary). Compatible with corroborated FND-0159 (unrestricted fixed-target stack smooth of dimension 18 at every point; that finding explicitly does not assert equidimensionality of the balanced locus or smoothness of the Aut(P^1)-quotient, both of which this finding supplies by openness of the (4,5) splitting type and finite reduced PGL_2-stabilizers). Compatible with FND-0153 (type (i)/(ii) dichotomy on a single balanced geometric fibre; type (ii) factors through a genus-one curve; non-emptiness of type (i) not asserted there). Compatible with FND-0154 (explicit balanced type-(ii) family, so H^bal is nonempty, without claiming a purely composed component). Compatible with FND-0155, whose type-(i) hypothesis this finding discharges on the universal balanced family and on smooth atlases, while FND-0155 still does not determine H_alpha on a purely type-(ii) base. Compatible with FND-0158, which explicitly does not assert ATT-0111/CLM-0111-9 (every type-(ii) point lies on a component meeting type (i)); the present finding proves that conclusion by a pure-dimension comparison (18 versus at most 14), not by a simply-branched deformation. Compatible with FND-0060 (the count b-3=15 is the PGL_2-quotient dimension, matching 18-3). Compatible with FND-0144: automaticity of the type-(i) hypothesis is a statement about geometric points and scheme atlases, not a stack-inertia component formula. Public sources independently support the geometric core and do not contain the campaign-specific FND-0155 packaging. Canning-Larson arXiv:2110.01059 Section 2.3 defines the parametrized Hurwitz scheme H^dagger_{k,g} of finite flat degree-k genus-g covers of a fixed P^1 with no simple-branching hypothesis, and the unparametrized stack as the PGL_2 (equivalently SL_2) quotient; for k=4 it isolates the open non-factoring substack H^{nf}_{4,g} and treats factoring covers (intermediate double covers; monodromy in a conjugate of D_4) as a proper locus. That independently licenses comparing the full unrestricted stack to a proper composed locus and the 18-versus-15 bookkeeping. The same paper's splitting-locus formula (codimension of the (e1,e2) stratum with e1<=e2 is max{0,e2-e1-1}) implies that a rank-two degree-nine bundle of type (4,5) has expected codimension 0, so the balanced type is open, confirming ATT-0112 Lemma 2.2 (h^0(F(-5))=5-a equals 1 iff a=4, and {h^0<=1} is open by upper semicontinuity). Canning-Larson arXiv:2208.02357v2 Lemma 10.6, as excerpted in the packet at SRC-0004, supplies deg(W_f|_C)=4g+12-4f and the relative-canonical convention used to identify L, but is not load-bearing for the dimension comparison. Classical Hurwitz geometry (configuration-space description of simply branched G-covers; Wikipedia Hurwitz space) gives dimension equal to the number of distinct simple branch values, which is 2g+2d-2=18 only for simple branching; ATT-0112 and FND-0159 correctly refuse to infer unrestricted dimension from that count, using instead the ramification-profile-independent normal sheaf. Two wording defects in the candidate text are corrected rather than promoted unchanged: (1) 'equivalently' conflates 'no component of H^bal lies in H^ii' with the quantitative bound dim(H^bal cap H^comp)<=14; the latter implies the former via purity of dimension 18, but the converse fails and the weaker discriminant bound dim<=17 already yields the qualitative conclusion; (2) type (ii) is strictly smaller than the non-primitive locus, since FND-0153 records that a balanced cover factoring through genus two or three, if it exists, must be type (i). Residual limitations are scope, not contradictions: the type-(i) hypothesis remains non-automatic on a base swallowed by the dimension-at-most-14 type-(ii) locus; irreducibility of H^bal is not claimed; FND-0152 induction and S_6 monodromy are consequences of FND-0155 once type (i) is present, not part of this finding's geometric core.

statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let H=H_{4,6}(P^1) be the Deligne-Mumford stack of pairs (C,gamma) with C a smooth projective connected genus-six curve and gamma:C->P^1 a finite morphism of degree four onto a fixed P^1 (equivalently, the smooth-source open of Mbar_{6,0}(P^1,4)). By FND-0159, H is smooth over k of pure dimension 18 at every point, independently of the ramification profile. Let F be the Casnati-Ekedahl relations bundle in the packet orientation F=ker(Sym^2 E -> gamma_*(omega_{C/P^1}^{otimes 2}))=p_*(I_C(2)), locally free of rank two and degree +9. Let H^bal be the locus where F is isomorphic to O_{P^1}(4) direct-sum O_{P^1}(5). Then H^bal is open in H: on geometric fibres F_t=O(a)+O(9-a) with a<=4, one has h^0(F_t(-5))=5-a, which equals 1 if and only if a=4, so H^bal coincides with the open {h^0<=1} cut out by upper semicontinuity. Hence H^bal is itself smooth of pure dimension 18, reduced and normal; every nonempty connected component has dimension exactly 18. Nonemptiness of H^bal is FND-0154. For h in {0,1,2,3} let H^{comp,h} be the constructible locus of covers admitting a factorization gamma=q o psi through a smooth projective connected curve of genus h with both maps of degree two, and let H^comp be their union. Relative Kontsevich/normal-sheaf dimension plus quasi-finiteness of composition (Steinitz finiteness of intermediate fields of a separable degree-four extension) gives dim H^{comp,h}<=16-2h, in particular dim H^{comp,1}<=14. The hyperelliptic-composed locus H^{comp,0} is disjoint from H^bal (ATT-0088/CLM-0088-2; independently FND-0125, F=O(2)+O(7)). The type-(ii) locus H^ii of FND-0153 inside H^bal is contained in H^{comp,1}, hence dim H^ii<=14. The non-primitive locus H^bal cap H^comp is contained in the union of H^{comp,1}, H^{comp,2}, and H^{comp,3} and therefore has dimension at most 14, i.e. codimension at least four in H^bal. This quantitative bound implies, but is not equivalent to, the following: no connected component of H^bal is contained in H^ii or in the closure of H^ii in H^bal, because every nonempty connected component has dimension 18>14. Thus every such component contains a type-(i) point, the closure of H^ii in H^bal has dimension at most 14, and H^i=H^bal minus H^ii contains a dense open of complement dimension at most 14. In particular balanced type-(i) covers exist and are dense in every connected component of H^bal. The type of a point is PGL_2-invariant; PGL_2 acts with finite reduced stabilizers (subgroups of the finite group Aut(C)), so Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2] is a smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of pure dimension 15; PGL_2 is connected, so pi_0(Hbar^bal)=pi_0(H^bal), and the non-primitive locus there has dimension at most 11, again of codimension at least four. Consequently the type-(i) hypothesis of FND-0155 is automatic on the universal balanced family and on every connected component of every smooth atlas of H^bal: each connected component of a locally finite-type smooth atlas is a smooth (hence normal integral reduced) k-scheme mapping openly into H^bal with image of dimension 18, therefore not contained in H^ii. A redundant independent bound dim H^comp<=17 follows from quasi-finiteness of the discriminant morphism br:H->P^{18} together with FND-0158(a), and already prevents a component of H^bal from lying in H^comp, but does not yield codimension four. statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let H = H_{4,6}(P^1) denote the Deligne-Mumford stack over k of pairs (C, gamma) with C a smooth projective connected curve of genus six and gamma : C -> P^1 a finite morphism of degree four onto a fixed P^1 (equivalently, the smooth-source open of the Kontsevich stack Mbar_{6,0}(P^1,4)). Every such gamma is finite flat Gorenstein, hence carries Casnati-Ekedahl data: gamma_* O_C = O direct-sum E^vee with E locally free of rank three and degree nine, and, in the packet orientation, a rank-two relations bundle F := ker(Sym^2 E -> gamma_*(omega_{C/P^1}^{tensor 2})) = p_*(I_C(2)) of degree +9, whose formation on H commutes with arbitrary base change. Let H^bal be the locus of points at which F is isomorphic to O_{P^1}(4) direct-sum O_{P^1}(5). Then H^bal is an open substack of H. Precisely: on a geometric fibre one has F_t isomorphic to O(a) direct-sum O(9-a) with a <= 4 by the Birkhoff-Grothendieck splitting theorem, and h^0(F_t(-5)) = 5-a, which equals 1 if and only if a = 4; the locus {t : h^0(F_t(-5)) <= 1} is open by upper semicontinuity of cohomology for the proper flat morphism P^1_T -> T, using that O(-5) is the pullback of O_{P^1}(-5) along the trivial P^1-bundle P^1_T -> P^1. Combined with the corroborated statement that H is smooth of dimension 18 at every point, independently of ramification profile (FND-0159), every nonempty connected component of H^bal is smooth of dimension 18, and H^bal is reduced and normal. This dimension is inherited from the ramification-profile-independent normal-sheaf count on the unrestricted stack, not from a count of distinct branch values. statement: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero. Let B be a separated finite-type k-scheme, and let V be a constructible mixed Hodge module on B, or an admissible variation of mixed Hodge structure viewed in D^b MHM(B), of weights at most w in Saito's convention (Gr_k^W H^i(V)=0 for all k>i+w). Compactly supported hypercohomology H_c^p(B;V) then has weights at most p+w, so the ceiling permits a possibly nonzero Gr^W_{p+w} rather than excluding it. Vanishing of Gr^W_p H_c^p(B;Q), including the vanishing obtained by compact-support localization of B as a dense open in a smooth affine d-fold when p<d, does not imply Gr^W_{p+w} H_c^p(B;V)=0 unless V is a constant mixed Hodge structure, in particular a constant Tate twist Q(-m). For a polarizable variation of Hodge structure of weight w, the lowest weight of ordinary H^p(B;V) is the image of intersection cohomology of the intermediate extension, pure of weight p+w; dually Gr^W_{p+w} H_c^p(B;V) is that top-weight piece and is not a functor of H_c^p(B;Q). A weight-w summand of V supported on a p-dimensional stratum likewise contributes in weight p+w. Consequently, in a compact-support Leray spectral sequence E_2^{p,q}=H_c^p(B; R^q f_! Q) of mixed Hodge structures, the estimate weights<=p+q does not kill Gr^W_{p+q}; additional control of the constructible coefficient object (constancy, lisseness, strata, or a weight-controlled extension across an affine ambient) or of the weight-(p+q) differentials is required. Exception: if R^q f_! Q is a constant Tate object, the identification H_c^p(B;Q(-m)) isomorphic to H_c^p(B;Q)(-m) does transfer the constant-coefficient top-weight vanishing. In the ATT-0113 setting this obstruction applies to the affine relative-dimension-2 morphism f:U->X^bal, with B=X^bal a dense open in a smooth affine 15-fold and with total degree p+q=16 for p<=14; the parenthetical alternative of running localization for a bounded complex of sheaves equally requires an unsupplied extension of R^q f_! Q across Y=X\X^bal, and dual Artin vanishing on the affine ambient does not apply to j_! of a local system from a proper open nor to general constructible sheaves.

adjudication_reason: The exact contested passage in ATT-0114, Lemma 1.1/CLM-0114-1, derives the injection from the compact-support localization sequence, the bound wt H_c^{m-1}(Y) <= m-1, and strictness of the weight filtration; it then dualizes using H_m^{BM}=H_c^m dual with no Tate twist. REV-0161's strongest attack concerned a possible hidden identification of discriminant-complement cohomology with projective-bundle cohomology. The attack does not contradict the lemma: localization proves only that the kernel of H_c^m(V) -> H_c^m(X) has weights at most m-1, hence gives an injection after Gr_m^W; it gives neither an isomorphism of the full groups nor a Leray statement with nonconstant coefficients. The audit does, however, reject the originating attempt's unqualified Deligne-Mumford-stack scope. Deligne's simplicial construction supports ordinary stack cohomology but is not, by itself, a cited construction of compactly supported cohomology or Borel-Moore homology for stacks. Tubach's later six-functor theory supplies a possible modern stack-level repair, but that is additional infrastructure not established in ATT-0114. No independently retrieved primary source explicitly verified the proposed rational compact-support comparison with coarse spaces in the exact Betti mixed-Hodge conventions used there. The promoted statement is therefore narrowed to schemes; this still covers the load-bearing applications U subset A and Z^(1) subset D identified in ATT-0114 and REV-0161. Reduced structure on Y is harmless for rational Betti cohomology. With H_m^{BM}(Z;Q) defined as H_c^m(Z;Q)^vee, no Tate twist occurs; because H_c^m has weights at most m, its dual has weights at least -m, so W_{-m}H_m^{BM} is the dual of Gr_m^W H_c^m. This also fixes the direction: dualizing the corner injection gives T_m(X) -> T_m(V) surjective. The finding is distinct from FND-0164 because it uses a degree drop from m to m-1 on the fixed closed complement, not a transfer of a constant-coefficient weight bound to a nonconstant Leray coefficient object.

statement: Let X be a separated scheme of finite type over C, let j: V -> X be an open immersion, and let Y=X\V with its reduced structure. Work with Q-coefficients. For every integer m, compact-support localization is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures containing H_c^{m-1}(Y;Q) -> H_c^m(V;Q) -> H_c^m(X;Q). All weights of H_c^{m-1}(Y;Q) are at most m-1, and morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for the weight filtration; hence Gr_m^W is exact and Gr_m^W H_c^m(V;Q) -> Gr_m^W H_c^m(X;Q) is injective. Define H_m^{BM}(Z;Q):=H_c^m(Z;Q)^vee, with no Tate twist, and T_m(Z):=W_{-m}H_m^{BM}(Z;Q). Then the induced restriction T_m(X) -> T_m(V) is surjective. Equivalently, classes in the kernel created by removing Y are subquotients of H_c^{m-1}(Y;Q), have weights at most m-1, and cannot occupy the weight-equals-degree corner. This statement does not identify H_c^m(V;Q) with H_c^m(X;Q) or with the cohomology of a projective bundle or other compactification, and it makes no claim for Deligne-Mumford stacks without an independently established compact-support mixed-Hodge formalism.

statement: Let S be a reduced locally Noetherian scheme carrying a proper smooth genus-six degree-four family satisfying (CE), (N), and (BAL), with associated fibre-degree-six line bundle L such that h^0(C_s,L_s)=3 for every geometric fibre s and L_s is base-point-free. Write Delta_script-C for the diagonal in script-C x_S script-C and pr_1,pr_2 for its projections. Then script-G:=pr_{2*}(pr_1^*L(-Delta_script-C)) is locally free of rank two on script-C and is compatible with arbitrary base change. Using the line convention for projectivization, the incidence morphism (p,Gamma)↦p identifies script-D canonically with P_script-C(script-G), hence with a Zariski-locally trivial P^1-bundle over script-C. Let U⊂A be the reduced-support locus, let Z→U be the finite étale right S_6-torsor of orderings, and put Z^(1):=script-D x_A U. Then Z^(1) is open in script-D, is finite étale of degree six over U, and is canonically Z/S_5 for the stabilizer S_5 of the first letter. If F is a Q-linear cohomological theory with transfer for free finite étale quotients, then F(Z^(1))≅F(Z)^{S_5}≅Hom_{S_6}(Ind_{S_5}^{S_6}(1),F(Z))≅M_[6](F(Z)) direct-sum M_[5,1](F(Z)), because Ind_{S_5}^{S_6}(1)≅[6] direct-sum [5,1]. Thus Z^(1) recovers the multiplicity spaces of the [6] and [5,1] isotypic summands; it is not itself their direct sum as S_6-subrepresentations. This applies, where defined, to rational ordinary, compactly supported, or Borel–Moore cohomology and their mixed Hodge structures and weight-graded pieces. It asserts neither Tate type nor control of other S_6-isotypics and does not extend to integral coefficients or functors without finite-quotient transfer.

adjudication_reason:
Mandatory local reads first. ATT-0116 (proof/attempts/ATT-0116.json): the contested passages are Step 5 of argument_markdown ('Therefore K (and hence the contribution supported on Z) is Tate ... if and only if K is spanned by Hodge (8,8)-classes'), claim CL-05 (status 'proved'), and theorem_statement clause (b) ('the contribution supported on Z is Tate of the exact target type if and only if K is spanned by Hodge (8,8)-classes, equivalently by algebraic fundamental classes of codimension-8 cycles supported on the closure of Z'). REV-0163 (proof/reviews/REV-0163.json): marks CL-05 and the synthetic claim THM-B-IFF 'failed', with strongest_attack asserting that K is the entire lowest-weight compact-support corner and that 'Z-Tate is neither necessary nor sufficient for spanning of K'. FND-0168 is the reviewer's novel_candidate_from_this_review with key 'global-K-not-Z-supported-tate-iff'.

Independent verification of the uncontested chain. ATT-0116 CL-01 to CL-04 are correct and are not touched by this finding: d = 3*6-3+6 = 21, 2d-16 = 26, Q(-13)(21) = Q(8) with weight 26-42 = -16, H^{BM}_{16} dual to H^{16}_c with no extra twist and Q(-8)^vee = Q(8). CL-04 I re-derived rather than imported: in H^{15}(D;Q) -> H^{16}_c(M_{6,6};Q) -> H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q) -> H^{16}(D;Q), D proper gives weights <= 15 on H^{15}(D), M_{6,6} smooth gives weights <= 16 on H^{16}_c, and strictness makes the image of H^{16}_c in the pure weight-16 group H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6}) equal to Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(M_{6,6};Q); that image is exactly K. So the finding's first sentence is confirmed: K is the whole degree-16 compact-support corner, a global invariant of M_{6,6} carrying no support condition, and Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c is the TOP weight piece of H^{16}_c (dual to the LOWEST weight piece W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}), consistent with FND-0032's corner orientation.

Three wording corrections applied to the candidate. (i) 'the Poincare dual of the RED-0001 open input' is loose: K is the Q-linear Hodge-structure DUAL of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) under Borel-Moore/compact-support duality; Poincare duality is the separate twisted identification W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16} = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) of FND-0001. The adjudicated statement separates the two maps. (ii) The candidate attributes the tautology to semisimplicity. Semisimplicity is not needed: for a pure weight-16 Q-Hodge structure V, 'V is a direct sum of Q(-8)' and 'V is spanned by its Hodge (8,8)-classes' are the same condition V_C = V^{8,8} by definition of Hodge type. Semisimplicity (packet FND-0033) is what rules out extension gaps at this corner; it is not what makes the (8,8)-spanning restatement contentless. (iii) 'is not equivalent to' overreaches as a mathematical assertion. Non-equivalence of two statements cannot be established here, because if the RED-0001 target is Tate both sides are true and the biconditional holds vacuously. The defensible content is that the biconditional is unproved and is a non-sequitur in the load-bearing direction, and that the missing input is a support-exhaustion statement. The adjudicated statement says exactly that.

One substantive correction to REV-0163, carried into the adjudicated statement. The review's 'neither necessary nor sufficient' is only half right, and which half depends on a reading the attempt never fixes. Fix a closed support Y in M_{6,6} carrying Z. Gr^W is exact on mixed Hodge structures, so the Borel-Moore localization sequence H^{BM}_{16}(Y) -> H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}) -> H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6} minus Y) stays exact after applying Gr^W_{-16} = W_{-16} at the lowest weight. Under reading (i), 'the contribution supported on Z' = the image of the first map, a SUB-object of the RED-0001 group: then K Tate implies that contribution Tate (sub-objects of a type-(8,8) structure are type (8,8)), so Z-Tate is necessary, and only sufficiency fails, requiring Tate-ness or vanishing of the piece injecting into the complement's group. Under reading (ii), 'the contribution' = Gr^W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y) itself, an upstairs group of which only the image is constrained: then neither direction follows. So the review is right that the reduction collapses, but its blanket 'neither necessary nor sufficient' holds only under reading (ii); the ambiguity between the two readings is itself part of the defect and is now recorded.

Two places where REV-0163 overreads, corrected so the promoted finding does not inherit them. (a) The review's degree check (clause iv) says a codimension-4, 17-dimensional support has fundamental class in H^8 'not H^{16}', treating the attempt's phrase as a degree error. The phrase 'codimension-8 cycles supported on the closure of Z' is in fact degree-consistent: codimension 8 in the 21-dimensional Mbar_{6,6} equals codimension 4 on the 17-dimensional support, and such a cycle does have class in H^{16}. The real defect is that the Gysin shift H^{16-8}(Z-tilde;Q)(-4) -> H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q) is never written and no smooth model or closed embedding is supplied. (b) The review states that no morphism Z -> M_{6,6} is constructed. That is accurate about the cited dependency ATT-0112, but the packet's adjudicated FND-0147 does supply a representable unramified quasi-finite monomorphism from the balanced ordered model to M_{6,6}. The finding must therefore not rest on the absence of any morphism; the correct obstruction is that a monomorphism with locally closed constructible image is not a closed immersion of a pure-codimension-4 closed substack, which is what a Gysin map needs (packet FND-0052, and the working-context hard stop quoted in REV-0163's dependency check).

Relation to existing packet findings; no merge. FND-0031 (circularity of rewriting the corner as ker(H^{16}(Mbar) -> H^{16}(D))), FND-0052 (no closed embedding / no Gysin for (M_{6,6},Z)), FND-0071 (kernel-Tate does not make H^{2r}(Mbar) Tate: the reverse containment issue), FND-0152 (the S_6-induction isomorphism upgrades nothing to Tate) and FND-0167 (Tate conclusions for Z-side corners are conditional on (H-C)/(H-S) and explicitly exclude M_{6,6}) each cover a neighbouring defect, but none states this one: that the localization kernel is the global corner, that the semisimplicity/(8,8) restatement is contentless, and that the missing hypothesis is support exhaustion in the Borel-Moore localization sequence. FND-0168 is distinct and non-redundant, so it is promoted in its own equivalence group rather than merged; merge_target_id is null. It contradicts no adjudicated claim: it refutes only ATT-0116's proposed CL-05/theorem-(b) equivalence, which is a rejected attempt claim, not packet content, hence contradicts_claim_ids stays empty.

Public-source cross-check. The weight-graded compact-support machinery invoked above (Deligne weight spectral sequence for H^*_c(M_{g,n};Q), E_2-degeneration, and the duality gr_k H^*_c(M_{g,n}) = gr_{6g-8+2n}H^{6g-6+2n-*}(M_{g,n})^vee displayed as equation (9) in section 2.7) is standard and publicly documented in arXiv:2110.05711v2, which supports the corner bookkeeping but contains no support-exhaustion or algebraicity theorem for the (6,6) degree-16 corner. arXiv:1805.10186 (Chan-Galatius-Payne, JAMS 34 (2021) 565-594) fixes the opposite, top-weight corner and so cannot supply the missing input, consistent with FND-0032. Payne's survey arXiv:2605.20453 frames Hodge/Tate-conjecture statements for moduli of curves as verified in a range of cases via the boundary stratification with open problems remaining, i.e. no general algebraicity theorem is available to license the Hodge-to-algebraic upgrade. The Hodge conjecture itself is proved only in the (1,1) case and low-dimensional or special situations and is open for higher codimension in general, so the codimension-8 upgrade on the 21-dimensional Mbar_{6,6} is an assumption, not an equivalence.
pre_adjudication_statement: For (g,n)=(6,6), the group K=ker(H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q)->H^{16}(D;Q)) is the entire pure weight-16 compact-support corner Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(M_{6,6};Q), equivalently the Poincare dual of the RED-0001 open input. Tate type of a contribution supported on the balanced Casnati-Ekedahl locus Z is not equivalent to K being spanned by Hodge (8,8)-classes, nor to K being spanned by algebraic codimension-8 cycles on a closure of Z. Semisimplicity of pure polarizable weight-16 Hodge structures makes 'spanned by Hodge (8,8)-classes' tautological for K itself and supplies neither a support restriction nor an algebraicity statement.
