statement: Scope: (g,n)=(6,6) over C with Q-coefficients; Mbar_{6,6} the smooth proper Deligne-Mumford stack of dimension d=21, D = Mbar_{6,6} minus M_{6,6} its proper boundary, Z the balanced Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure locus. (1) K := ker(H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q) -> H^{16}(D;Q)) is canonically isomorphic, as a pure polarizable Hodge structure of weight 16, to Gr^W_{16}H^{16}_c(M_{6,6};Q) -- the top weight graded piece of H^{16}_c and the entire degree-16 compact-support corner of M_{6,6} -- and is canonically the Hodge-structure dual of the RED-0001 open input W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), with Q(-8) dual to Q(8). This uses only smoothness of M_{6,6} (weights of H^{16}_c are <= 16), properness of D (weights of H^{15}(D) are <= 15) and strictness. It is a global invariant of M_{6,6} and carries no support condition. The separate Poincare identification W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) = W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) (FND-0001) is a different map and must not be conflated with this duality. (2) For any pure Q-Hodge structure V of weight 16, 'V is a finite direct sum of Q(-8)' and 'V is spanned by its Hodge (8,8)-classes' are the same condition (V_C = V^{8,8}) by the definition of Hodge type; neither polarizability nor semisimplicity of the category of pure polarizable weight-16 Q-Hodge structures is needed for this equivalence, and neither adds information to it. Applied to K, the equivalence is a restatement of the target, not a reduction: it imposes no support condition and produces no cycle class. (Semisimplicity, per FND-0033, only excludes extension gaps at this corner.) (3) Give 'the contribution supported on Z' its only standard meaning by first fixing a closed support Y in M_{6,6} containing the image of Z. Since Gr^W is exact on mixed Hodge structures, the Borel-Moore localization sequence yields an exact sequence W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) -> W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q). Consequently: (3a) if the Z-supported contribution means the image of the first map, then K Tate of type Q(-8) implies that contribution is Tate (a sub-object of a type-(8,8) structure is of type (8,8)), so Z-Tate is necessary; but the converse -- the direction the reduction needs -- does not follow, since it additionally requires a support-exhaustion input, namely vanishing or Tate-ness of the quotient injecting into W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16} of the complement of Y. No such input is established for (6,6). (3b) if it means W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) itself, then neither direction follows, since only the image of that group is constrained by K. ATT-0116 fixes neither reading. Hence the asserted equivalence 'the contribution supported on Z is Tate of the exact target type if and only if K is spanned by Hodge (8,8)-classes' is unproved and is a non-sequitur in its load-bearing direction. This is a statement about a missing hypothesis, not a demonstration that the two sides have different truth values: if the RED-0001 target is Tate, both sides hold, so the biconditional cannot be refuted by exhibiting differing truth values. (4) 'K is spanned by algebraic fundamental classes of codimension-8 cycles of Mbar_{6,6} supported on a closure of Z' implies 'K is spanned by Hodge (8,8)-classes', but the converse is the Hodge conjecture in codimension 8 on the 21-dimensional Mbar_{6,6}, which is unproved in general beyond the (1,1) case; writing 'equivalently' between the two silently assumes it. (5) Independently of (3) and (4), the support clause carries two further undischarged obligations: (5a) a closed (stratified) embedding of the balanced reduced-support model into M_{6,6}/Mbar_{6,6} together with a Gysin map -- that model is an open piece of the failure locus (FND-0052), and FND-0147 supplies only a representable unramified quasi-finite monomorphism to M_{6,6}, which is not a closed immersion of a pure-codimension-4 closed substack; (5b) the Gysin degree shift H^{8}(Z-tilde;Q)(-4) -> H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q) for a 17-dimensional codimension-4 support with a suitable smooth model Z-tilde. The phrase 'codimension-8 cycles supported on the closure of Z' is itself degree-consistent (codimension 8 in Mbar_{6,6} equals codimension 4 on the 17-dimensional support), so the defect is the unwritten shift and the missing closed embedding, not the codimension label; the fundamental class of the support itself lies in H^{8}, not H^{16}. Not asserted: that K fails to be Tate; that the Z-supported contribution fails to be Tate; that Z-supported classes do not in fact span K; any computation of H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6};Q); any claim for (g,n) other than (6,6), although the logical structure of (2)-(4) is general. Confirmed and untouched: ATT-0116 clause (a) and claims CL-01 through CL-04.

adjudication_reason: Mandatory first reads: ATT-0118 sections 1-4 and claims CLM-0118-1 through CLM-0118-5; REV-0165 confirmation of all five claims, dependency checks, and strongest_attack. The contested construction is the mu_3-Kummer cover y^3=x(x-1) of M_{0,4}, the Kunneth class of type (15,1) in Gr^W_16 H_c^16 of its 15-fold power over M_{0,18}, and finite-etale transport to a balanced simply-branched Hurwitz chart. Independently recomputed: Riemann-Hurwitz 2g(Cbar)-2=3(-2)+6=0 gives genus one; H_c^0(C)=0 forces compact-support Kunneth in degree 16 on C^15 to be exactly one H_c^2=Q(-1) and fourteen H_c^1, so the top-weight summand is Q(-1) tensor H^1(Cbar)^{tensor 14} of weight 16 and Hodge type (15,1); pairwise diagonals have dimension at most 14. Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, Theorem 8.2.4(ii) (Publ. Math. IHES 44 (1974), pp. 38-39, doi 10.1007/BF02685881) states that Hodge numbers of H^n(X) vanish unless (p,q) lies in [n-N,N] x [n-N,N] when dim X=N, hence F^{15} H_c^{16} vanishes in dimension at most 14; morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for W (Hodge II, and FND-0165), so the class survives both localizations. Finite-etale transfer over Q is injective on the corner. Existence of a nonempty simply-branched balanced open does not rest on CLM-0112-4 nor on the packet's composed elliptic witness FND-0154, which FND-0158 proves is never simply branched. Load-bearing existence is the Bujokas-Patel Main Theorem (arXiv:1504.03756v1): if g>=(d-3)(d-1) then the Casnati-Ekedahl bundle F of a general cover in the classical simply-branched Hurwitz space H_{d,g} is balanced; for (d,g)=(4,6) one has 6>=3, and a balanced rank-2 degree-9 bundle is O(4)+O(5). Combined with FND-0159 (classical Hurwitz space etale over the configuration space of r=18 points) and Clebsch irreducibility of H_{4,6}, a Zariski-open of simply-branched tetragonal covers is balanced, so a connected etale chart V of Hbar^bal with Gr^{15,1} Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(V;C) nonzero exists. Adjoining V to any allowed atlas U yields U disjoint-union V, and H_c is additive. No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty; FND-0167 states (H-S) as a hypothesis and explicitly makes no assertion about its truth, so the present statement supplies new information rather than opposing FND-0167. Distinct from corroborated FND-0085 (finite branch maps do not imply mixed-Tate cohomology) and FND-0054 (a predicted Tate motive may not be used unconditionally): those leave Tate-ness open, whereas this exhibits an allowed base on which the j=8 corner is provably non-Tate. Compatible with CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, and RED-0001: the argument never touches Z, K, or M_{6,6}. REV-0165 already recorded that FND-0167's corner injections run from U into a sum of corners of S, so non-Tateness of S does not transport to Z=Ord(U); Delta has dimension 16, so the F^{15} vanishing used on the base does not apply to the discriminant. FND-0165 withholds compact-support mixed Hodge theory for Deligne-Mumford stacks, which is why the campaign's scheme-atlas quantification is the vulnerable one. Wording corrections relative to the candidate: (i) existence is attached to Bujokas-Patel rather than CLM-0112-4; (ii) (H-S) is FND-0167's hypothesis on any reduced separated finite-type C-scheme carrying the balanced setup, not merely on atlases; (iii) the Z-corner is excluded; (iv) FND-0167 itself is not described as asserting (H-S). Promote the narrowed statement; do not merge.

statement: Over C with Q-coefficients, at (g,n)=(6,6). Let Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2] be the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of pure dimension 15 of balanced genus-six degree-four covers (FND-0162). Let S range over reduced separated finite-type C-schemes carrying a (CE)+(N)+(BAL) family in the sense of FND-0167, including connected components of reduced separated finite-type etale scheme atlases of Hbar^bal. The constant-coefficient corner Gr^W_16 H_c^16(S;Q) is not an invariant of the stack Hbar^bal: it depends on S. Explicitly, the mu_3-Kummer cover C->M_{0,4} cut out by y^3=x(x-1), with smooth projective model Cbar of genus one, yields a nonempty irreducible finite-etale cover Mtilde of M_{0,18} whose Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Mtilde;Q) contains a nonzero Hodge type (15,1), obtained as the compact-support Kunneth summand Q(-1) tensor H^{1,0}(Cbar)^{tensor 14} and surviving removal of the pairwise-diagonal locus of dimension at most 14 because Hodge numbers of compactly supported cohomology vanish in filtration degree strictly larger than dimension (Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, Theorem 8.2.4(ii)). By the Bujokas-Patel theorem that the Casnati-Ekedahl bundle F of a general cover in the classical simply-branched Hurwitz space H_{d,g} is balanced whenever g>=(d-3)(d-1) (hence for (d,g)=(4,6)), together with FND-0159 (the classical Hurwitz space is etale over the configuration space of r=2g+2d-2=18 points), there is a connected finite-etale Hurwitz chart X over M_{0,18} whose balanced open is nonempty. Finite-etale pullback/trace of the type-(15,1) class along a connected component Xtilde of X times_{M_{0,18}} Mtilde, followed by compact-support localization onto the balanced open V of Xtilde (FND-0165), produces a connected smooth 15-fold V, etale over Hbar^bal, with Gr^{15,1} Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(V;C) nonzero. Thus Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(V;Q) is not a finite direct sum of Q(-8). For any allowed atlas U, the disjoint union U sqcup V is again an allowed atlas and compactly supported cohomology is additive, so the same non-Tate summand appears in Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U sqcup V;Q). Consequently the j=8 instance of hypothesis (H-S) of FND-0167, namely that Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8), is false for some allowed S. FND-0167 itself does not assert (H-S). Any campaign statement that asserts or requires (H-S) while universally quantifying over a reduced locally Noetherian scheme atlas of Hbar^bal, or over all reduced separated finite-type C-schemes carrying the balanced setup, is therefore false as stated rather than merely unproved. (H-S) may be asserted only for a specifically named atlas, or replaced by a stack-level statement, which requires a compact-support mixed-Hodge formalism for Deligne-Mumford stacks that FND-0165 explicitly withholds. This does not address Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q) for Z=Ord(U): the FND-0167 corner map injects Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U) into a sum of Tate twists of corners of S, so it cannot transport non-Tateness from S to Z, and the discriminant in the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle has dimension 16 so F^{15} H_c^{16} need not vanish there.

The contested parenthetical 'dominant (in particular finite etale)' is false as written: finite etale implies dominant, not conversely, and the transfer identity Tr f^*=deg requires a finite etale morphism of smooth d-folds (or an open immersion, via FND-0165 localization), so the merely-dominant case is excluded from the promoted statement. No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty; CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, and RED-0001 concern Mbar_{g,n} / the open Borel-Moore corner of M_{g,n}, not etale covers of M_{0,n} or Hurwitz charts. Distinct from FND-0167, which states (H-S) only as an undischarged hypothesis, and from the sibling atlas-dependence candidate in REV-0165: this finding is the dimension-independent production mechanism, not the (H-S) quantification claim. statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let d≥2 be an integer. Let B=M_{0,4}≅P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. Let Cbar be the smooth projective connected curve with function field C(x,y) and equation y^3=x(x-1): the degree-three map Cbar→P^1 given by x is totally ramified over exactly 0,1,∞ (valuations of x(x-1) equal 1,1,−2, none divisible by 3), and Riemann-Hurwitz gives 2g(Cbar)−2=3(−2)+3(2)=0, so Cbar has genus one. Let C be Cbar minus those three ramification points, so C→B is connected finite etale of degree three. Compact-support localization yields Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C;Q)≅H^1(Cbar;Q) of Hodge types (1,0) and (0,1), and H_c^2(C;Q)≅Q(−1); also H_c^0(C)=0. Identifying M_{0,d+3} with the complement of the pairwise diagonals in B^d, set Mtilde:=C^d ×_{B^d} M_{0,d+3}. This is a nonempty Zariski-open in the irreducible d-fold C^d, hence irreducible, and Mtilde→M_{0,d+3} is connected finite etale. Compact-support Kunneth of mixed Hodge structures places, for each of the d choices of factor, a direct summand Q(−1)⊗(Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C;Q))^{⊗(d−1)} inside Gr^W_{d+1} H_c^{d+1}(C^d;Q); the Hodge component (1,1)+(d−1)·(1,0)=(d,1) is one-dimensional and nonzero. The inverse image Y of the pairwise diagonals has dimension ≤d−1, so the Hodge numbers of H_c^{d+1}(Y) vanish for p>dim Y and therefore F^d H_c^{d+1}(Y;C)=0. Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for W and F; weights of H_c^d(Y;Q) are at most d; hence Gr^W_{d+1} of the compact-support localization sequence H_c^{d+1}(Mtilde)→H_c^{d+1}(C^d)→H_c^{d+1}(Y) is exact (FND-0165), the type-(d,1) class dies in H_c^{d+1}(Y), and it lifts to a nonzero class of Hodge type (d,1) in Gr^W_{d+1} H_c^{d+1}(Mtilde;Q). In particular F^d Gr^W_{d+1} H_c^{d+1}(Mtilde;C)≠0. For d≥2 one has d>(d+1)/2, so this weight-equals-degree corner is non-Tate. Now let W be a smooth connected complex algebraic d-fold equipped with a finite etale morphism f:W→M_{0,d+3}, and let W' be any connected component of W×_{M_{0,d+3}} Mtilde. Then W'→W is finite etale of positive degree, W'→Mtilde is finite etale of positive degree, and finite-etale pullback/trace over Q injects the type-(d,1) class into Gr^W_{d+1} H_c^{d+1}(W';Q). The same non-Tate class is obtained if instead f is a dense open immersion, by a second application of FND-0165 to the complement of dimension ≤d−1. Consequently the property that Gr^W_{d+1} H_c^{d+1}(−;Q) is Tate is not invariant under finite etale refinement of any such base, and no Tate assertion for that corner can be proved by an argument that is invariant under finite etale pullback, transfer, averaging, monodromy-orbit counting, or descent along an etale scheme atlas. This applies in particular to every simply-branched Hurwitz chart whose branch map is finite etale over M_{0,r} with r=d+3. The statement does not apply to a merely dominant morphism that is neither finite etale nor an open immersion; it does not assert anything about compactly supported cohomology of a Deligne-Mumford stack in the absence of a scheme atlas; and it does not transport non-Tateness to Gr^W_{16} H_c^{16}(Z;Q) of a Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure model, nor to RED-0001.

statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients in the FND-0167 setup for (g,n)=(6,6). Let S be a reduced separated finite-type C-scheme of pure dimension 15 carrying a (CE)+(N)+(BAL) genus-six degree-four family whose relative degree-six line bundle L is fibrewise base-point-free with h^0=3, so that formation of pi_*L commutes with base change. Put A=P_S(pi_*L), a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle of dimension 17; let Delta be the non-reduced-divisor locus; put U=A minus Delta; and let Z=Ord(U)->U be the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings. FND-0167 supplies an injection of pure polarizable weight-16 Hodge structures Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)^{S_6}=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U;Q) into Gr^W_16 H_c^16(S;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H_c^14(S;Q)(-1) direct-sum Gr^W_12 H_c^12(S;Q)(-2), obtained by composing the FND-0165 corner injection for the open immersion U subset A with the projective-bundle formula for A->S. Independently, fibrewise Bertini (the general member of |L| consists of six distinct points) together with the classical discriminant and dual-curve description of a spanned g^2_6 in |L| isomorphic to P^2 imply that Delta->S is nonempty of pure relative dimension one, hence dim Delta=16. Consequently ATT-0118's refutation of (H-S) at j=8 on an allowed atlas component does not refute Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q) or Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q), both of which remain open. statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let H=H_{4,6}(P^1) be the Deligne-Mumford stack of finite degree-four covers of a fixed P^1 by smooth connected genus-six curves, and let H^bal be the open locus where the Casnati-Ekedahl relations bundle in the packet orientation F=ker(Sym^2 E -> gamma_*(omega_{C/P^1}^{otimes 2})) is isomorphic to O_{P^1}(4)+O_{P^1}(5) (rank two, degree +9). Write Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2]. Call gamma simply branched when every geometric fibre has partition type 2+1+1+1, equivalently when every local monodromy permutation in S_4 is a transposition, equivalently when gamma has eighteen distinct simple branch values. (1) The packet's self-contained nonemptiness witness for H^bal (FND-0154: gamma=q o psi through a smooth genus-one curve) is never simply branched. This is FND-0158: a nontrivial factorization C->Y->P^1 of degrees (2,2) has a fibre of type (2,2) or 4 over each branch value of q, since every degree-two map Y->P^1 is ramified (Riemann-Hurwitz: deg R_q=2g_Y+2>=2); equivalently, a simply-branched connected degree-four cover has monodromy group S_4, which is primitive, while a nontrivial factorization is imprimitive. Under the extra reducedness and disjointness hypotheses of FND-0158(b), the FND-0154 family has fourteen branch values (ten of type 2+1+1 and four of type (2,2)), and the set of simply-branched type-(ii) points is empty. Consequently FND-0154 may not be cited as a simply-branched balanced cover. (2) Existence of a simply-branched point of H^bal, equivalently of Hbar^bal, is not supplied by FND-0154, nor by the type-(i) density statement of FND-0162 (type (i) means not FND-0153 type (ii), which excludes only the bielliptic-through-a-plane-cubic case and still permits primitive non-simple ramification). Any construction that needs a simply-branched balanced cover — in particular any argument that places a Hurwitz chart etale over M_{0,18} or Conf_18 inside the balanced locus — must discharge existence by one of the following routes. Route A (packet-internal dimension comparison): H is smooth of pure dimension 18 at every point, independently of ramification profile (FND-0159). The classical Hurwitz space of a fixed ramification profile with r distinct branch values is etale over the configuration space of those r points and has dimension r, which equals 18 if and only if the cover is simply branched (FND-0159; Kanev, arXiv:math/0509154, Introduction: the discriminant map of the simply-branched Hurwitz space is etale onto Y^{(n)}-Delta, with Delta the codimension-one locus of non-simple divisors). Hence the non-simply-branched locus in H has dimension at most 17. Combined with nonemptiness of H^bal (FND-0154) and the fact that H^bal is open of pure dimension 18 (FND-0162, FND-0163), every nonempty connected component of H^bal, and of the quotient Hbar^bal of pure dimension 15, meets the simply-branched locus. Equivalently, after the PGL_2 quotient, the same comparison is the dual-confirmed bound dim(non-simply-branched)<=14 in Hbar^bal of pure dimension 15 recorded as CLM-0112-4. Route B (Bujokas-Patel genericity): for a general point of the classical irreducible simply-branched Hurwitz space H_{d,g}, the Casnati-Ekedahl bundle of quadrics F is balanced whenever g>=(d-3)(d-1) (Bujokas-Patel, arXiv:1504.03756v1, IMRN 2021, Main Theorem; algebraically closed field of characteristic zero). Here F is defined by 0->F->Sym^2 E->alpha_*(omega_alpha^{otimes 2})->0, with rk F=d(d-3)/2 and deg F=(d-3)(g+d-1), and balanced means h^1(End F)=0. At (d,g)=(4,6) one has g=6>=3, rk F=2, deg F=9, hence F isomorphic to O(4)+O(5), matching the packet orientation. This route does not use FND-0154. FND-0163 records it only inside a NOT ASSERTED clause, so a proof that invokes it must cite the theorem independently. (3) This existence hinge is inherited by every argument that realises an etale chart of Hbar^bal over M_{0,18} or Conf_18. It does not by itself control Gr^W_16 H_c^{16} of the evaluation-failure model Z, nor the campaign target RED-0001.

The FND-0167 arrow has source Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U;Q), identified by transfer with Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)^{S_6}, and target the direct sum of three constant-coefficient corners of S. Hence Tate-ness of the target propagates to the source, by strictness and semisimplicity of pure polarizable Hodge structures, but a non-Tate target does not force a non-Tate subobject. Moreover, placing the ATT-0118 class in the fibre-degree-zero summand of H_c^16(A) does not establish that it survives restriction to U: because dim Delta=16, Deligne's dimension bound permits Hodge index p=15 in H_c^16(Delta), so it supplies no F^15-vanishing. This is a failure of the proposed lifting argument, not proof that the class dies. The candidate's unqualified sentence that Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q) remains open is contradicted as a global campaign statement by FND-0176 and FND-0178, which use a different product-family and fibre-degree-two route to produce a non-Tate invariant Z-corner. The defensible observation is therefore limited to the ATT-0118 first-summand route. It duplicates the already corroborated FND-0171, with related coverage in FND-0169 and the route distinction recorded in FND-0177, so FND-0175 should be merged into FND-0171 rather than promoted independently.

statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients, at (g,n)=(6,6). Let (C_0,gamma_0) be a geometric type-(i) fibre of H^bal in the sense of FND-0153, for instance any simply-branched balanced fibre (existence: FND-0172). Let B be a reduced separated finite-type C-scheme. The constant (CE)+(N)+(BAL) family over B with fibre (C_0,gamma_0) is an allowed ATT-0112 clause-(E) base, because its classifying image is a single type-(i) point. For this family, A=P_B(pi_*L) is isomorphic to B times |L_0| isomorphic to B times P^2, the reduced-support open U_0 of |L_0| is a nonempty smooth connected affine surface (the complement of the discriminant curve of the spanned g^2_6), U is isomorphic to B times U_0, and Z=Ord(U) isomorphic to B times Z_0 is the finite etale right S_6-torsor of orderings. Poincare duality on the smooth connected surface U_0, equivalently compact-support localization of U_0 subset P^2 against the discriminant curve Delta_0 of dimension 1, yields H_c^4(U_0;Q) isomorphic to Q(-2), pure of type (2,2). Compact-support Kunneth of mixed Hodge structures for products of separated finite-type C-schemes (the compact-support form of Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, Proposition 8.2.10) therefore realises H_c^m(B;Q)(-2) as a direct mixed-Hodge-structure summand of H_c^{m+4}(U;Q) for every integer m, and, Q(-2) being pure of weight 4 with Gr^W exact, realises Gr^W_m H_c^m(B;Q)(-2) as a direct summand of Gr^W_{m+4} H_c^{m+4}(U;Q). Finite-etale transfer over Q identifies Gr^W_{m+4} H_c^{m+4}(U;Q) with the S_6-invariants inside Gr^W_{m+4} H_c^{m+4}(Z;Q). Consequently any theorem asserting that Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8) for every allowed clause-(E) base forces Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(B;Q) to be a finite direct sum of Q(-6) for every reduced separated finite-type C-scheme B. This last assertion is false: if C is the affine Kummer curve of FND-0170 (the smooth projective model of y^3=x(x-1) minus the three ramification points of x), then for B=C^8 compact-support Kunneth supplies a nonzero Hodge component of type (8,4) in Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(B;Q), namely Q(-1)^{tensor 4} tensor (Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C;Q))^{tensor 4} with the type-(1,0) line of H^1(Cbar) in each of the four H_c^1 factors, and tensoring with Q(-2) produces a nonzero type-(10,6) class in Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q) and hence in Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q). Type (10,6) satisfies Deligne's Hodge-number bound (Theorie de Hodge III, Theorem 8.2.4(ii)) for dim U=10 and is not of type (8,8), so Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q) is not a finite direct sum of Q(-8) and T_16(Z) is not a finite direct sum of Q(8). The exact C66-TATE-SUPPORT theorem of campaign revision 4, universally quantified over every reduced locally Noetherian C-scheme carrying a (CE)+(N)+(BAL) family with no connected-component image contained in the type-(ii) locus, is therefore false. A repaired C66-TATE-SUPPORT must either name a specific base or atlas, or retain the FND-0167 hypotheses (H-S) including the j=6 corner Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q). The exhibited class is the third FND-0167 summand Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S)(-2), realised as a Kunneth summand of H_c^{16}(U) itself on a product family, not a lift of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S); FND-0171, which blocks transport of the j=8 first summand through the corner injection on a pure-dimension-15 atlas, does not apply. Not asserted: any computation of the global kernel K, any conclusion about a fixed 15-dimensional atlas of Hbar^bal, or any statement about RED-0001.

REV-0167 confirms CLM-0119-4, CLM-0119-5, and CLM-0119-6, and strongest-attack (ii) records that an initial suspicion that H_c^4 of the discriminant curve might be nonzero confused it with H_c^2. Packet FND-0167 supplies the corner injection Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U) into Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S) + Gr^W_14 H_c^{14}(S)(-1) + Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S)(-2) and does not assert surjectivity. Packet FND-0171 records that this injection cannot transport non-Tateness from S to U and that, on a pure-dimension-15 base, dim Delta=16 so Deligne's F^{15} vanishing used for dimension-at-most-14 complements fails; it leaves Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U) and Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z) open. Primary checks: Deligne, Theorie de Hodge III, Theorem 8.2.4, states that nonzero Hodge numbers h^{p,q} of H^n(X) satisfy (i) p,q>=0 and (ii) if dim X=N then (p,q) lies in [n-N,N] x [n-N,N], hence F^p vanishes for p>dim X; (iii) proper implies p+q<=n; (iv) smooth implies p+q>=n. Proposition 8.2.10 gives Kunneth as mixed Hodge structures for ordinary cohomology of products of separated finite-type C-schemes, and Corollary 8.2.8 / Wikipedia Mixed Hodge structure records the compact-support localization sequence H_c^m(U)->H^m(X)->H^m(Y). Topological cohomological dimension gives H_c^k(X;Q)=0 for k>2 dim_C X, so H_c^4 of a curve vanishes. Stacks tag 0FMG Lemma 50.11.4 gives H^{2i}_{dR}(P^n)=A c_1(O(1))^i for 0<=i<=n and zero otherwise, matching H_c^{2j}(P^2)=Q(-j) for j=0,1,2. The original candidate overstated two points, which the adjudicated statement corrects: (1) fibrewise restriction H_c^{2j}(P^2)->H_c^{2j}(Delta_0) rigorously controls the three FND-0167 summands only for product families via Kunneth, not for general relative P^2-bundles without a Leray argument withheld by FND-0164; (2) vanishing of H_c^{2j}(Delta_0) is sufficient for the restriction to vanish and, among fibre degrees j=0,1,2 with dim Delta_0<=1, is equivalent to 2j>2 dim Delta_0, but is not a general iff. The 16-dimensional discriminant clause is the non-product dim-S=15 geometry of FND-0171, not the product-family fibrewise picture. With those hypotheses restored, the explanation of why FND-0171 blocks ATT-0118 but not ATT-0119 is correct.

The fibre-degree-2j summand survives removal of the discriminant precisely when H_c^{2j}(Delta_0)=0, i.e. when 2j > 2 dim Delta_0. Thus the j=2 summand Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S)(-2) always survives in product families (H_c^4 of a curve vanishes), while the j=0 and j=1 summands can be killed or altered by restriction to the 16-dimensional discriminant. statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let S be a reduced separated finite-type C-scheme, let Delta_0 subset P^2 be a closed subscheme of dimension at most 1, and set U_0=P^2 minus Delta_0. For a product (equivalently, constant (CE)+(N)+(BAL)) family with U isomorphic to S times U_0, compact-support Kunneth of mixed Hodge structures and the projective-bundle formula identify Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S times P^2;Q) with the direct sum of three pure weight-16 summands Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S;Q) direct-sum Gr^W_14 H_c^{14}(S;Q)(-1) direct-sum Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q)(-2), corresponding to fibre degrees 2j for j=0,1,2. Compact-support localization along U_0 subset P^2 is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures; at the weight-equals-degree corner Gr^W is exact, so the fibre-degree-2j projective-bundle summand of A=S times P^2 lies in the image of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q) if and only if the restriction Gr^W_{2j} H_c^{2j}(P^2;Q) -> Gr^W_{2j} H_c^{2j}(Delta_0;Q) vanishes. Vanishing of H_c^{2j}(Delta_0;Q) is sufficient for that restriction to vanish, and holds whenever 2j>2 dim Delta_0. Thus the fibre-degree-2 summand Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q)(-2) always survives in such product families as a direct Kunneth summand of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q), equivalently H_c^4(U_0;Q)=Q(-2), because H_c^4 of a curve vanishes; this is the class used by ATT-0119. If Delta_0 is nonempty and proper then H_c^0(U_0;Q)=0, so the fibre-degree-0 summand Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S;Q) does not appear in H_c^{16}(U;Q); the restriction H_c^2(P^2)->H_c^2(Delta_0) is typically nonzero for a positive-degree plane curve, so the fibre-degree-1 projective-bundle summand need not arise from U. Independently, on a non-product FND-0167 family with S of pure dimension 15, the discriminant Delta subset A has dimension 16, so Deligne's Hodge-number bound (Theorie de Hodge III, Theorem 8.2.4(ii)) does not force F^{15} H_c^{16}(Delta;C)=0. This is why FND-0171 blocks transporting the (H-S) j=8 / fibre-degree-0 first summand of ATT-0118 to U, while it does not block the ATT-0119 fibre-fundamental-class class, which is already a Kunneth summand of H_c^{16}(U) itself. The FND-0167 corner map injects Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U) into the three summands and cannot by itself transport non-Tateness from any ambient summand to U; survival of the third summand in product families is a kernel/Kunneth statement, not a reverse of that injection. Fibrewise restriction on Delta_0 does not by itself control non-product families at fibre degrees j=0,1 without a compact-support Leray argument, which FND-0164 withholds for nonconstant coefficients. No assertion is made about RED-0001, about T_16 of a dimension-17 model over a dimension-15 atlas of Hbar^bal, or about S_6-isotypics other than the S_6-invariants of the product model.

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. Independent inspection of ATT-0119 sections 1-7 and of REV-0167 (CLM-0119-1 through CLM-0119-6, ATT-0119-scope-compliance, and strongest_attack) confirms the contested passage: the TASK-C66-M-004 theorem_statement quoted identically in both artifacts is universally quantified over every reduced locally Noetherian C-scheme carrying a (CE)+(N)+(BAL) family with no connected-component image in the type-(ii) locus, imposes no dimension, dominance, or non-isotriviality condition, and declares a surviving non-Tate summand in Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q) itself to be a disproof. The constant simply-branched type-(i) family over S=C_aff^8 meets every written hypothesis of that quantification. Hodge recomputation: for Cbar given by y^3=x(x-1), valuations of x(x-1) at 0,1,infinity are 1,1,-2, none divisible by 3, so the x-map is totally ramified at three points; Riemann-Hurwitz gives 2g-2=3(-2)+3(2)=0, g(Cbar)=1. Compact-support localization against the three-point complement (H_c^k=0 for k>=1) yields H_c^2(C_aff;Q)=Q(-1) and Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C_aff;Q) isomorphic to H^1(Cbar;Q) of types (1,0) and (0,1), matching FND-0170 and the localization sequences on the fetched Wikipedia Mixed Hodge structure page (H^2 of a smooth proper curve is Q(-1); H_c of a complement is mixed of the expected weights). Compact-support Kunneth on S=C_aff^8 forces the degree-12 corner to be four H_c^2 factors and four H_c^1 factors (2a+b=12 and a+b=8), so Gr^W_12 contains Q(-1)^{tensor 4} tensor (Gr^W_1 H_c^1)^{tensor 4} with a nonzero type-(8,4) component. For the constant family, U isomorphic to S times U_0 with U_0 a smooth connected surface (reduced-support open in |L_0| isomorphic to P^2), so Poincare duality gives H_c^4(U_0;Q)=Q(-2); equivalently localization against the discriminant curve of dimension 1 kills H_c^{>=3} of the complement and identifies H_c^4(U_0) with H^4(P^2)=Q(-2). Kunneth therefore realises Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S)(-2) as a direct MHS summand of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U), of type (10,6). Deligne Hodge III (numdam PMIHES 1974, DOI 10.1007/BF02685881; FND-0169 already records Theorem 8.2.4(ii)) permits h^{p,q} of H_c^{16} on a 10-fold for 0<=p,q<=10, so (10,6) is allowed and is not killed by p>dim vanishing. Finite-etale transfer over Q injects the S_6-invariants, and the class is pulled back from U, hence occupies the trivial ([6]) isotypic. A finite direct sum of Q(-8) is pure of type (8,8), so this is a surviving non-Tate summand in the exact H_alpha-object of the quantified lemma. FND-0171 does not apply: that obstruction blocks transport of non-Tateness from the first FND-0167 summand Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S) through a dimension-16 discriminant, whereas the present class is already a Kunneth summand of H_c^{16}(U) (the third FND-0167 summand), and on the product family H_c^4 of the discriminant curve vanishes. Existence of a simply-branched balanced fibre is FND-0172; independently, the fetched Bujokas-Patel Main Theorem (arXiv:1504.03756v1) states that the Casnati-Ekedahl bundle of quadrics F of a general cover in H_{d,g} is balanced whenever g>=(d-3)(d-1), which holds at (d,g)=(4,6) since 6>=3, and balanced rank-two degree-nine F is O(4)+O(5). Compatible with, and not a duplicate of, corroborated FND-0167 (conditional Tate-transfer under (H-S)/(H-C)), FND-0169 (universal (H-S) at j=8 fails on some atlas components), FND-0170 (Kummer-curve Kunneth, explicitly not transporting non-Tateness to Z), and FND-0171 (Z remained open after the j=8 attack). The original candidate text is dangerously ambiguous: S=C^8 could be misread as affine 8-space, for which H_c^{12} vanishes and the (8,4) class does not exist; the adjudicated statement therefore names C_aff. The original (H-S) clause is retained after check: on this S, j=6 gives type (8,4) and j=7 gives type (8,6) from six H_c^2 and two H_c^1 factors, so (H-S) fails at j=6 and j=7, while j=8 is eight copies of H_c^2 and is Tate Q(-8). Thus FND-0167's implication is not touched. The witness has dim Z=10, so it does not address a 15-dimensional atlas or RED-0001. Distinct from FND-0169/FND-0171: do not merge. Merge target: none. Promote candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source on independent verification of the localization, Kunneth bookkeeping, Poincare duality on a surface, Hodge-number bound, finite-etale transfer, and Bujokas-Patel existence input.

statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let C_aff be the smooth connected affine curve obtained from the smooth projective model Cbar of y^3=x(x-1) by deleting the three ramification points of the degree-three x-map: Cbar has genus one by Riemann-Hurwitz, H_c^2(C_aff;Q)=Q(-1) of type (1,1), and Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C_aff;Q) is isomorphic to H^1(Cbar;Q) of types (1,0) and (0,1). Let S=C_aff^8, a smooth connected affine C-scheme of dimension 8, in particular reduced, locally Noetherian, separated, and of finite type. Compact-support Kunneth of mixed Hodge structures places a nonzero Hodge type-(8,4) class in Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q), arising from the summand Q(-1)^{tensor 4} tensor (Gr^W_1 H_c^1(C_aff;Q))^{tensor 4}. Let (C_0,gamma_0) be a simply-branched balanced type-(i) geometric fibre of H^bal (existence by FND-0172, equivalently Bujokas-Patel: the Casnati-Ekedahl bundle of a general cover in H_{d,g} is balanced for g>=(d-3)(d-1), hence at (d,g)=(4,6)). The constant (CE)+(N)+(BAL) family over S with this fibre is an allowed ATT-0112 clause-(E) base: its classifying image is a single type-(i) point, hence not contained in the type-(ii) locus. For this family, U isomorphic to S times U_0 and Z isomorphic to S times Z_0, where U_0 is the reduced-support open in |L_0| isomorphic to P^2, a smooth connected surface, so H_c^4(U_0;Q)=Q(-2) of type (2,2). Compact-support Kunneth therefore realises Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S;Q)(-2) as a direct mixed-Hodge-structure summand of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(U;Q), carrying a nonzero Hodge type-(10,6) class (permitted by Deligne's Hodge-number bound on the 10-fold U). Finite-etale transfer over Q injects this S_6-invariant class into Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q). A finite direct sum of Q(-8) is pure of type (8,8), so Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(Z;Q) is not a finite direct sum of Q(-8) and T_16(Z):=W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(Z;Q), dual with no extra Tate twist, is not a finite direct sum of Q(8). Consequently the exact TASK-C66-M-004/C66-TATE-SUPPORT theorem, as universally quantified over every reduced locally Noetherian C-scheme carrying a (CE)+(N)+(BAL) genus-six degree-four family with no connected-component image contained in the type-(ii) locus and with no dimension, dominance, or non-isotriviality hypothesis, is false. The witness lies entirely in the simply-branched locus and already in the S_6-invariant ([6]) isotypic component. The class is a Kunneth summand of H_c^{16}(U) itself, namely the third FND-0167 corner Gr^W_12 H_c^{12}(S)(-2), not a lift of Gr^W_16 H_c^{16}(S), so FND-0171 does not block it. This does not resolve RED-0001, does not address T_16 of a dimension-17 model over a named 15-dimensional etale atlas of Hbar^bal, and does not refute the conditional implication of FND-0167, because the witness base violates (H-S) at j=6 and at j=7 (while the j=8 instance of (H-S) holds for this particular S).

statement: The universally quantified C66-TATE-SUPPORT lemma is false. Let C be the affine elliptic Kummer curve obtained from y^3=x(x-1) by removing its three ramification points, take S=C^8, and equip S with the constant family of a simply-branched balanced type-(i) tetragonal fibre. Then U=S×U_0 and Z=S×Z_0 are allowed clause-(E) models, and Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q) contains in its S_6-invariant part a nonzero Hodge component of type (10,6), arising from Gr^W_12 H_c^12(C^8;Q) tensor H_c^4(U_0;Q). Consequently T_16(Z) is not a direct sum of Q(8). This concerns the model Z itself and does not imply anything about the global kernel K or RED-0001.

adjudication_reason: The candidate does not contradict CONJ-0001, THM-0001, RED-0001, FND-0001, FND-0052, FND-0147, FND-0165, or FND-0168. FND-0168(3) requires a closed support Y containing the image of Z before a Z-supported contribution in T has a referent, and records in (5a)/(5b) that a closed embedding of the balanced reduced-support model together with a Gysin degree shift remain undischarged; it does not assert that those inputs are needed merely to name the image of the supports map. ATT-0120 constructs that Y as the reduced Zariski closure of the classifying image of the dual-confirmed ATT-0112 ordered reduced-support model, and names T_Z as the kernel of ordinary restriction on the smooth pair (M_{6,6}, M_{6,6} minus Y). REV-0169 independently confirmed all seven claims CLM-0120-1 through CLM-0120-7. The contested ATT-0120 section 5 parenthetical equating T_Z with the supports group rather than its image is exactly the FND-0168(3a)-versus-(3b) hazard; REV-0169 already recorded it as non-adverse because the kernel definition and both certificate fields use the image form, and this audit retains only that image form. FND-0052 (the reduced-support model is an open piece of the failure locus, not a closed pure-codimension-4 subvariety of M_{6,6}) obstructs Gysin for the pair (M_{6,6}, Z), not restriction of ordinary cohomology along the complement of a closure Y. FND-0147 supplies a representable unramified quasi-finite monomorphism, which ATT-0120 correctly does not use: existence of the classifying morphism is the universal property of M_{6,6}. FND-0165 withholds compact-support mixed Hodge theory of Deligne-Mumford stacks as a standalone input; the load-bearing maps are ordinary restriction on the smooth stacks M_{6,6} and U_Y, already licensed by FND-0001, together with cohomology with supports computed on that smooth ambient. Public sources confirm the mixed-Hodge facts: morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for the weight filtration (Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971); Elzein-Le arXiv:1302.5811, section 3); Borel-Moore homology carries a mixed Hodge structure dual to compactly supported cohomology, and for a smooth ambient the closed-open pair yields an exact sequence from Borel-Moore of the closed subset through ordinary cohomology of the ambient to ordinary cohomology of the open (Arapura arXiv:2103.05038v2, Lemma 1.2; Wikipedia Mixed Hodge structure, distinguished triangle i_* i! Q -> Q -> R j_* Q, using smoothness of the ambient only). The Gysin shift by twice the codimension appears only when the closed subset is regularly immersed, which is not used. Chevalley's theorem (Stacks tag 054K) makes the classifying image constructible, but only the Zariski closure is load-bearing. No merge is appropriate: FND-0168 records missing hypotheses for a different attempt (ATT-0116), whereas this finding is the positive kernel-form interface. The original campaign-status sentence that the C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE obligation is dischargeable is replaced by the mathematical construction, and the degeneracy Y = M_{6,6} left open by ATT-0120 is closed by the already dual-confirmed dimension count dim Z = 20 < 21.
pre_adjudication_statement: For (g,n)=(6,6) the C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE obligation is dischargeable using only (i) the universal property of M_{6,6} applied to the ordered reduced-support CE model over a smooth scheme atlas of H^bal, and (ii) the open-closed localization of the smooth stack M_{6,6} along the reduced Zariski closure Y of the resulting classifying image: setting T_Z := ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q)(21)) realises FND-0168(3a)'s image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> T, by exactness of W_{-16} on the Borel-Moore localization sequence together with compatibility of Poincare duality with open restriction on the smooth pair. statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let X denote the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack M_{6,6} of dimension 21, and let T := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), identified by FND-0001 with W_{26} H^{26}(X;Q)(21). Let Z be the ordered reduced-support Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure scheme over a smooth finite-type scheme atlas of the balanced tetragonal stack H^bal, as supplied by the dual-confirmed ATT-0112 clause (E). The tautological smooth genus-six curve with six pairwise-disjoint sections on Z is an object of X(Z), so the universal property of X supplies a morphism f: Z -> X of locally finite-type Deligne-Mumford stacks; no monomorphism, unramifiedness, or closed-immersion claim is used. Let Y be the unique reduced closed substack of X whose underlying space is the Zariski closure of the geometric image of f; Y is independent of the choice of smooth finite-type atlas of H^bal. The source Z has dimension 20 (atlas dimension 18 plus relative dimension two of the reduced-support open of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle), so the image of f has dimension at most 20 and Y is a proper closed substack of X; the complement U_Y := X minus Y is a nonempty dense smooth open of dimension 21. Restriction r: H^{26}(X;Q) -> H^{26}(U_Y;Q) is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures. Both groups have weights at least 26, morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for the weight filtration, and W_{26} equals Gr^W_{26} on each. Define T_Z := ker(T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U_Y;Q)(21)). Then T_Z is a pure polarizable weight -16 subobject of T, equal to the image of the degree-26 cohomology-with-supports map W_{26} H^{26}_Y(X;Q)(21) -> T, and not in general isomorphic to the supports group W_{26} H^{26}_Y(X;Q)(21) itself (the FND-0168(3a)-versus-(3b) distinction). Poincare-Verdier duality on the smooth ambient X identifies cohomology with supports along Y with Borel-Moore homology of Y and intertwines ordinary open restriction with Borel-Moore corestriction on the smooth pair (X, U_Y); consequently T_Z coincides with the image of W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> T in the sense of FND-0168(3a). This naming uses only the closed-open pair (Y, U_Y) inside the smooth stack X. It does not require a closed embedding of Z, a regular immersion or lci hypothesis on Y, purity of any codimension, or a Gysin shift by twice a codimension. Coverage is one-sided: every class in T supported on a closed subset of X contained in Y, in particular every class supported on the image of Z or on its closure, lies in T_Z; extra components of Y are not excluded. The construction asserts neither T_Z = T, nor any Tate type of T or T_Z, nor a map from the cohomology of Z. Therefore FND-0052 and FND-0168(5a)/(5b) are not obstructions to forming this C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum; they remain binding wherever T_Z must be computed or shown Tate.

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the geometric properness of Y does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. Local originating artifacts were checked first. ATT-0120 Section 8 explicitly disclaims dimension of Y, equidimensionality of Y, and dim Y=17, while constructing Y as the reduced Zariski closure of the finite-type classifying image of the ordered reduced-support model; the degenerate reading Y=M_{6,6} is therefore unaddressed in the attempt, which is the gap REV-0169 records. That last clause overstates. Geometric properness of Y rules out only the unnoticed degeneration in which U_Y is empty and r_T=0 identically, which would force T_Z=T with no cohomological content. FND-0168(3a), already corroborated, records that T_Z=T can still hold for a proper closed Y, because restriction T->W_{26}H^{26}(U_Y;Q)(21) may vanish on a nonempty dense open; support-exhaustion remains a separate C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY input. The dimension count itself is independently confirmed. Hacking, Algebra Number Theory 2 (2008), 809-818, and arXiv math/0509567v2 Section 2: the stack of stable n-pointed genus-g curves is a smooth proper Deligne-Mumford stack of dimension 3g-3+n, so dim Mbar_{6,6}=21 and the open smooth locus M_{6,6} has the same dimension; Wikipedia Moduli space, section Moduli of curves, records the same formula for M_{g,n}. FND-0159/FND-0162/FND-0163 give H and H^bal smooth of pure dimension 18 (normal-sheaf length 2d+2g-2=18 at (d,g)=(4,6)), matching CLM-0112-2. A Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle is smooth of relative dimension two, so Stacks tag 0AFE yields dimension 20 for the Abel-Jacobi bundle; FND-0134 makes the reduced-support open dense in every fibre, and the S_6-ordering torsor is finite etale, so the stack-level ordered model over H^bal has dimension 20. Compatible with FND-0052 (the reduced-support model is an open piece of the failure locus, not itself a closed pure-codimension-4 subvariety of M_{6,6}: Y is a closure, still proper). Compatible with FND-0168(5b), which names a 17-dimensional Gysin source as an undischarged closed-embedding obligation rather than a proved upper bound on the classifying image. Compatible with FND-0147 (representable unramified quasi-finite monomorphism after pencil reconstruction), which would make dim of image equal dim of the PGL_2-quotiented 17-dimensional model and is not used here, matching ATT-0120's refusal of the monomorphism route. Distinct from FND-0168: do not merge. Promote from candidate to corroborated on independent primary-source verification of dim M_{6,6}=21, of dim(image)<=dim(source) for quasi-DM finite-type morphisms, and of the 18+2 source dimension; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source. pre_adjudication_statement: The stack-level ordered reduced-support CE model over H^bal has dimension 18 + 2 = 20 (H^bal smooth of pure dimension 18 by CLM-0112-2, plus the relative dimension two of the reduced-support open of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle), so the set-theoretic image of its classifying morphism to M_{6,6} has dimension at most 20 and its reduced Zariski closure Y satisfies dim Y <= 20 < 21 = dim M_{6,6}. Hence Y is a proper closed substack and M_{6,6} minus Y is a nonempty dense open. Any kernel-form CE support datum is therefore a genuine proper-support term and cannot degenerate into an unnoticed support-exhaustion statement T_Z = T.

statement: Work over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let H=H_{4,6}(P^1) be the Deligne-Mumford stack of finite degree-four covers of a fixed P^1 by smooth connected genus-six curves, and let H^bal be the open locus where the Casnati-Ekedahl relations bundle is isomorphic to O(4)+O(5). Then H^bal is smooth of pure dimension 18 (FND-0159, FND-0162, FND-0163). Let Z be the stack-level ordered reduced-support Casnati-Ekedahl model over H^bal: the finite etale S_6-torsor of orderings of the reduced-support open U of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle P(pi_*L). That bundle is smooth of relative dimension two, U is nonempty and dense in every fibre (FND-0134), and the ordering torsor is finite etale, so Z is smooth of pure dimension 18+2=20. Let f:Z->M_{6,6} be the classifying morphism of the tautological six-pointed smooth genus-six curve constructed in ATT-0120/CLM-0120-1, and let Y be the reduced closed substack of M_{6,6} whose underlying space is the Zariski closure of the geometric image of f (equivalently, of any smooth finite-type scheme atlas of Z; atlas independence as in CLM-0120-2). Then f is locally of finite type and quasi-DM, hence dim Y<=dim Z=20. Independently, M_{6,6} is a smooth Deligne-Mumford stack of dimension 3*6-3+6=21. Therefore dim Y<=20<21, Y is a proper closed substack, and U_Y:=M_{6,6} minus Y is a nonempty dense open. In particular the kernel-form CE support term T_Z:=ker(T->W_{26}H^{26}(U_Y;Q)(21)) of ATT-0120 is not forced to equal T by emptiness of the complement: the geometric degeneration Y=M_{6,6} does not occur. This does not assert the cohomological support-exhaustion T_Z=T, nor that restriction to U_Y is nonzero on T; those remain separate inputs as in FND-0168(3a). The bound dim Y<=20 is not asserted to be sharp: the classifying image is PGL_2-invariant, Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2] has dimension 15, and the corresponding model has dimension 17. No closed embedding of Z, regular immersion, Gysin map, or Tate type is asserted.

adjudication_reason: Mandatory first reads were ATT-0120 and REV-0169. ATT-0120 Sections 4-6 construct the kernel-form datum T_Z := ker(T -> W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q)(21)) from ordinary restriction along the open complement of the reduced classifying-image closure Y, identify it with FND-0168(3a)'s image of the supports map, and explicitly declare coverage one-sided: the kernel contains every class supported on a closed subset of Y (hence every Z-supported class in the only sense available before a regular embedding) but may also contain classes on extra components of the closure. ATT-0120 does not compare two different closed supports and does not claim uniqueness of a minimal kernel. REV-0169 confirms ATT-0120 and extracts the candidate as a reusable comparison rule, distinct from FND-0168(3a) which fixes one Y. That distinction is correct: corroborated FND-0168(3) records the exact sequence W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> T -> W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q) for a single closed support containing the image of Z, and therefore already implies that the kernel-form term equals the image of Borel-Moore homology of Y, but it does not record monotonicity in Y or minimality of the reduced closure. No claim-level contradiction arises: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and the statement does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, RED-0001, FND-0001, FND-0052, or FND-0168. Primary-source checks confirm the two load-bearing lemmas. Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II (Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971), doi 10.1007/BF02684692), Theorem 2.3.5: the category of mixed Hodge structures is abelian, every morphism is strictly compatible with the weight filtration W, and Gr^W_n is an exact functor. The same paper, Theorem 3.2.5(iii) and 3.2.11.B: the mixed Hodge structure on H^*(X) of a smooth complex algebraic variety is functorial in X, so restriction along an open immersion (in particular U' subset U subset M_{6,6}) is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures; kernels of composed restrictions therefore enlarge as the open shrinks. The same functoriality of restriction is the input that makes the Borel-Moore localization sequence of FND-0168(3) and the right-exact sequence (6.1) of Canning-Larson-Payne, arXiv:2307.08830v3, compatible with open-closed pairs other than the compactification boundary. Stacks Project Tag 0508 / Lemma 100.10.1 (Tag 0509): a closed subset T of |X| for an algebraic stack X carries a unique reduced closed substack Z with |Z|=T, so the reduced Zariski closure of the classifying image is the unique smallest closed substack containing that image and therefore yields the unique smallest kernel-form term in this family. Two wording defects in the candidate are corrected rather than promoted unchanged. First, 'met exactly by that minimal choice' overstates coverage: no-omission holds for every closed Y containing the image, and even the minimal kernel may contain non-CE support on the closure minus the constructible image (ATT-0120 Section 6). Second, 'imports non-CE support that must then be separately shown Tate' is a remaining C66-TATE-SUPPORT obligation inside the kernel-form family, not a theorem that extra support is non-Tate, and Y proper subset Y' need not strictly enlarge the kernel. Merge with FND-0168 is refused. Promote the corrected statement.
pre_adjudication_statement: For closed substacks Y contained in Y' of M_{6,6}, both containing the image of the CE model, the kernel-form terms satisfy ker(T -> W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q)) contained in ker(T -> W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6} minus Y';Q)). Taking Y to be the reduced closure of the classifying image therefore yields the unique minimal such term. Two consequences: the 'no omitted Z-supported term' obligation is intrinsically one-sided and is met exactly by that minimal choice; and the only way to enlarge the support term toward exhaustion is to enlarge Y beyond the CE geometry, which imports non-CE support that must then be separately shown Tate.

statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let T := W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6}; Q), identified by Poincare duality with W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6}; Q)(21) (FND-0001). Let Im subset |M_{6,6}| be the set-theoretic image of the classifying morphism to M_{6,6} of the ordered reduced-support Casnati-Ekedahl evaluation-failure model of ATT-0112 clause (E). Let Y subseteq Y' be closed substacks of M_{6,6} with Im subset |Y|. Write U := M_{6,6} minus Y and U' := M_{6,6} minus Y', so U' subseteq U are smooth open substacks of dimension 21. Restriction H^{26}(M_{6,6}; Q) -> H^{26}(U'; Q) factors through H^{26}(U; Q) as a morphism of mixed Hodge structures. Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strictly compatible with the weight filtration, so W_{26} is an exact functor. Poincare duality on the smooth opens identifies W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(U; Q) with W_{26} H^{26}(U; Q)(21) and likewise for U'. Therefore ker(T -> W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(U; Q)) is contained in ker(T -> W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(U'; Q)), equivalently ker(T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U; Q)(21)) is contained in ker(T -> W_{26} H^{26}(U'; Q)(21)). A closed subset of |M_{6,6}| carries a unique reduced closed substack structure, so the reduced closed substack Y_0 whose underlying space is the Zariski closure of Im is the unique smallest closed substack containing Im, and the associated kernel T_{Z,Y_0} is the unique smallest kernel-form term among those indexed by closed substacks of M_{6,6} containing Im. This comparison is internal to that kernel-form family and does not constrain other constructions of subobjects of T. Two consequences: (i) the obligation that no class in T supported on a closed subset contained in the image of Z, or in its closure, be omitted is one-sided (the kernel may contain classes supported on extra components of Y, including points of the Zariski closure of Im that do not lie in Im) and is already met by every such Y, in particular by Y_0; (ii) a strictly larger kernel-form term cannot be obtained from a closed support contained in Y_0, so enlarging the kernel-form term toward exhaustion T_{Z,Y}=T requires a closed support not contained in Y_0 and therefore not equal to the reduced CE classifying-image closure. That extra support is not identified with the CE geometry by the kernel-form interface and is not shown Tate by that construction; showing any enlarged term Tate remains a separate C66-TATE-SUPPORT obligation. Support-exhaustion T_{Z,Y}=T is not asserted for any Y, and vanishing of restriction from T to a nonempty complement is not asserted.

statement: Let X be a smooth d-dimensional Deligne-Mumford stack over C and f: Z -> X a finite-type morphism. Let Y be the reduced closed substack whose underlying space is the Zariski closure of the geometric image of f. For any degree i and twist (n), the kernel of the restricted localization map W_m H^i(X;Q)(n) -> W_m H^i(X minus Y;Q)(n) is a sub-mixed-Hodge structure equal to the image of W_m H^i_Y(X;Q)(n) in W_m H^i(X;Q)(n), by strictness and exactness of Gr^W_m. It contains every class supported on any closed subset of X contained in Y, requires no Gysin map, no regularity or lci hypothesis on Y, and no closed immersion of Z. It may strictly contain the span of Z-supported classes; equality or exhaustion is a separate assertion not supplied by this pattern.

statement: Let H and X be algebraic stacks. Suppose a subset S of the geometric points |X| is defined as the image of a classifying morphism attached functorially, in the 2-Yoneda sense, to smooth surjective finite-type atlases of H: for every such atlas V->H from an algebraic space there is a finite-type morphism f_V:Z_V->X, and these morphisms are compatible with pullback along morphisms of atlases. Then for any two such atlases V->H and V'->H, the 2-fibre product W=V x_H V' exists as an algebraic space (Stacks Project Tag 04T2); the projections W->V and W->V' are smooth and surjective, hence surjective on geometric points (Tags 04XH, 04XI); and W->H is again a smooth surjective atlas. If Z_(-) is constructed only for scheme bases, one must pass to a scheme presentation of W. The tautological family on Z_W is then the pullback of the families on Z_V and Z_{V'}, so the geometric images of f_V, f_{V'}, and f_W in |X| coincide. Consequently S is independent of the atlas, and the unique reduced closed substack Y of X with |Y| equal to the Zariski closure of S (Tag 0509) is independent of the atlas. Common refinement of atlases of H does not by itself produce a morphism [H/G]->X or identify S with the image arising from an atlas of the quotient: a morphism [H/G]->X exists if and only if the classifying morphism from H is G-equivariant, equivalently the X-valued moduli point is G-invariant on geometric points (Tag 04WM). This lemma does not assert that a scheme-level tautological model constructed on atlases of H transfers to etale atlases of [H/G], and it does not assert atlas-independence of compactly supported cohomology of the atlas. In the campaign case (g,n)=(6,6), with H=H^bal the balanced tetragonal stack, X=M_{6,6}, and G=PGL_2, the extra invariance is ATT-0112/CLM-0112-7; the failure of ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 to transfer to atlases of Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2] is the separate finding FND-0187.

pre_adjudication_statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients at (g,n)=(6,6). Let Y be any closed substack of M_{6,6} and T_Z := ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6} minus Y;Q)(21)) the associated kernel-form term. Exactness of W_{-16} on the Borel-Moore localization sequence makes W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> T have image exactly T_Z, so T_Z is a QUOTIENT of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q). That source group is pure polarizable of weight -16: H^{BM}_k of any finite-type object is Q-dual to H_c^k, whose weights are at most k, so Borel-Moore weights in degree k are at least -k and the bottom filtration step W_{-k}H^{BM}_k is pure of weight -k with polarizable graded piece. Since pure polarizable weight -16 Q-Hodge structures form a semisimple abelian category, a quotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is a finite direct sum of Q(8). Hence, for the ATT-0120 support Y, 'W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8)' is a SUFFICIENT condition for the exact C66-TATE-SUPPORT theorem, and it requires no closed regular embedding, no lci or purity hypothesis, no Gysin map, and no degree shift by twice a codimension -- only Poincare-Verdier duality on the smooth ambient, which FND-0180 already supplies. It remains sufficient, not necessary, and it says nothing about support-exhaustion T_Z = T.

statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients at (g,n)=(6,6). Let X denote the smooth Deligne-Mumford stack M_{6,6} of dimension 21, and let T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), identified by FND-0001 with W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21). Let Y be any closed substack of X, write U:=X minus Y, and let T_Z:=ker(T->W_{26}H^{26}(U;Q)(21)) be the associated kernel-form term (the ATT-0120/FND-0180 interface when Y is the reduced classifying-image closure). Poincare-Verdier duality on the smooth ambient identifies cohomology with supports along Y with Borel-Moore homology of Y: topologically H^{BM}_k(Y) isomorphic to H^{2d-k}(X,U) for the closed embedding of Y into the oriented real 2d-manifold underlying X (Iversen IX.4.7), and algebraically H^{26}_Y(X;Q) isomorphic to H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)(21). This identification requires no closed regular embedding of Y, no lci or purity-of-codimension hypothesis, no Gysin map, and no degree shift by twice a codimension. FND-0180 already records that the same duality intertwines ordinary open restriction with Borel-Moore corestriction, so T_Z equals the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)->T in the sense of FND-0168(3a). Morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict, hence W_{-16} is exact on the Borel-Moore localization sequence, and T_Z is a quotient of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q). Duality convention as in FND-0165: H^{BM}_k(-;Q):=Hom(H_c^k(-;Q),Q) with no extra Tate twist. Deligne's weight bound, recorded for Borel-Moore homology by Hanamura-Saito, gives that H_c^k has weights at most k and therefore H^{BM}_k has weights at least -k, so the bottom step W_{-k}H^{BM}_k is pure of weight -k. Over C this piece is polarizable (graded-polarizable Deligne mixed Hodge structures, including the simplicial-scheme formalism of Hodge III 8.3 applied to an etale atlas of the finite-type stack Y). Thus W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight -16. Polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of a fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category (FND-0033), so a quotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is a finite direct sum of Q(8). Hence, for any such Y and in particular for the ATT-0120 support, the condition that W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8) is sufficient for T_Z to be a finite direct sum of Q(8), which is the C66-TATE-SUPPORT conclusion. The condition is sufficient, not necessary: non-Tate summands of the source may die in the map to T. The statement does not assert that the source is Tate, does not prove T_Z Tate, and says nothing about support-exhaustion T_Z=T. Stack-level compactly supported cohomology of Y is used only through the Poincare-Verdier mixed Hodge structure already granted by FND-0180 on the smooth pair (X,U); this does not reopen the FND-0165 exclusion of an independent stack-level H_c formalism. FND-0052 and FND-0168(5a)/(5b) remain binding for any Gysin-style computation that would identify the supports group with a codimension shift of ordinary cohomology of Y, but they are not required for this sufficiency.

pre_adjudication_statement: For any closed substack Y' of M_{6,6} with dim Y' < 8, the kernel-form term ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6} minus Y';Q)(21)) is zero, since H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q)=0 whenever 16 > 2 dim Y'. Combined with monotonicity of kernel-form terms in the support, this yields a dimension floor for the whole campaign: a closed support can contribute a nonzero subspace to the ATT-0120 term T_Z only if it has dimension at least 8, hence only in the range 8 <= dim <= 17 given dim Y <= 17. In particular every constant or product clause-(E) model, whose classifying image in M_{6,6} is contained in the at-most-two-dimensional set of ordered reduced members of a single linear system on a single fixed curve, contributes exactly zero to T_Z. Such models are therefore inert in BOTH directions: they can neither disprove nor support the exact C66-TATE-SUPPORT theorem, whatever their standalone Hodge types, and their exclusion needs no pushforward on compactly supported cohomology.

statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let X=M_{6,6}, let T=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), identified with W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21), and for a closed finite-type separated Deligne-Mumford substack Y' of X define K(Y'):=ker(T->W_{26}H^{26}(X\Y';Q)(21)). Assume the rational compactly supported cohomology of Y' agrees with that of its coarse moduli space, and use the Borel-Moore convention H^{BM}_k(Y';Q)=Hom_Q(H_c^k(Y';Q),Q). Poincare-Verdier localization identifies K(Y') with the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q) in T. If dim(Y')<8, then H_c^{16}(Y';Q)=H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q)=0 because 16>2dim(Y'), and therefore K(Y')=0. If Y' is contained in another closed support Y, factorization of open restriction gives K(Y') contained in K(Y). Consequently, a nonzero subspace of the ATT-0120 kernel T_Z supported on a closed Y' contained in its classifying-image closure Y requires dim(Y')>=8. The verified general ceiling is dim(Y)<=20; when the repaired PGL_2-quotient factorization of FND-0187 is included, dim(Y)<=17 and such supports can occur only in the range 8<=dim(Y')<=17. For a constant or product clause-(E) model Z_B=B times Z_0 whose classifying map factors through the fixed-fibre model Z_0 and whose classifying-image closure Y_0 has dim(Y_0)<=2, one has K(Y_0)=0 and K(Y_0) contained in T_Z. This conclusion concerns only target classes supported on Y_0; it asserts no compact-support pushforward from Z_B to T or T_Z, does not determine the Tate type of T_Z, and does not claim that such models are logically useless in proving the theorem.

adjudication_reason: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty and the finding does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001 through THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. Local contested passage, checked first in ATT-0121 and REV-0171: ATT-0121 Section 3 and CLM-0121-2 apply ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 over a connected component of a smooth finite-type etale scheme atlas of Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2] to obtain a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle and dim Z=15+2=17. REV-0171 marks CLM-0121-2 unresolved precisely because CLM-0112-8 is confirmed only over smooth finite-type atlases of H^bal, and records the odd-twist/Brauer obstruction as the concrete reason. That citation-range defect is real and independent of whether dim Y<=17 can later be repaired. Compatible with CLM-0112-8 on its actual H^bal-atlas scope; with CLM-0112-2 and CLM-0112-7 (dimensions 18 and 15, PGL_2-invariance of the M_{6,6} point); with FND-0181, whose proved bound is dim Y<=20 from the H^bal-level 18+2 model and which explicitly does not cover equality dim Y=17; and with FND-0171, which takes Zariski-local triviality of A=P_S(pi_*L) as a hypothesis on a dimension-15 base rather than as a consequence of CLM-0112-8. Distinct from FND-0157, which warns that a general etale P^1-bundle or Severi-Brauer conic need not arise as a g^1_4 target: the present finding is only that the tautological target over an Hbar^bal atlas is the associated P^1-bundle of a PGL_2-torsor, whose class can obstruct ordinary O(5). Compatible with FND-0169, which includes etale atlases of Hbar^bal among bases carrying a geometric (CE)+(N)+(BAL) family without discharging ordinary O(5) or Zariski-local triviality of the Abel-Jacobi P^2. Independent primary checks. (1) Encyclopedia of Mathematics: a Brauer-Severi scheme over X is etale-locally P^n_X, equivalently a finitely presented proper flat morphism with geometric fibres projective spaces, classified by H^1(X,PGL_{n+1}). (2) Kollár arXiv:1606.04368v2, Baby Example 3 and Main Example 5 / Corollary 14: a conic with no rational point has no degree-1 line bundle; O_P(1) exists as an ordinary line bundle on a Severi-Brauer variety P iff P is isomorphic to projective space; in the non-split case the ordinary Picard group is generated by multiples of the canonical class, which on P^1 is O(-2). Section 6 and Definition 47: the complete linear system of a twisted line bundle is itself a Severi-Brauer variety, so projectivization of the twisted sheaf of sections is a PGL-form of projective space rather than a Zariski-locally trivial projective bundle. Theorem 81 records the same Euler sequence and Azumaya algebra for Severi-Brauer schemes over a base. (3) Wikipedia (Lichtenbaum): 0->Pic(X)->Z -delta-> Br(K)->Br(K)/(X)->0 with delta(1) the Brauer class of X, so if the class has order d then the least ordinary divisor degree is a multiple of d; for a relative P^1 this order divides 2, hence ordinary O(5) exists iff the class vanishes. These sources confirm the mechanism and the two repair routes (twisted linear system as a relative Severi-Brauer scheme of dimension two; PGL_2-quotient of the already-constructed 20-dimensional H^bal-level model) as standard, not as theorems already written in ATT-0121. Do not merge with FND-0181 or FND-0157. Promote from candidate; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source.
pre_adjudication_statement: ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 (Grauert, pi_*L locally free of rank three, Zariski-locally trivial Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle, reduced-support open, S_6-ordering torsor) is established over smooth finite-type atlases of H^bal and does not transfer verbatim to etale atlases of Hbar^bal = [H^bal/PGL_2]. The packet convention W_5 = (O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*F^vee)|_C involves gamma^*O_{P^1}(-5); over the PGL_2-quotient the target P^1 descends only as a Severi-Brauer/P^1-bundle whose Brauer class can obstruct the odd twist O(5), so W_5, L = W_5 tensor omega^{-1} and pi_*L need not exist as sheaves on such an atlas, and Zariski-local triviality of the P^2-bundle is not available there. Projectivization is insensitive to the twist, so the Abel-Jacobi fibration still exists as a Severi-Brauer scheme of relative dimension two and the dimension count 15+2 = 17 survives; alternatively one obtains dim(image) <= 20 - 3 = 17 directly from three-dimensional PGL_2-orbits with finite stabilizers, consistent with dim Hbar^bal = 18 - 3 = 15. Attempts that need the 17-dimensional model must supply one of these two repairs rather than cite CLM-0112-8 unchanged.

statement: Work over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero (or C) at (g,n)=(6,6). ATT-0112/CLM-0112-8 (Grauert; formation of pi_*L commuting with base change so that pi_*L is locally free of rank three; Zariski-locally trivial Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle A=P_S(pi_*L); reduced-support open U; finite etale S_6-ordering torsor Z=Ord(U)) is established over smooth finite-type scheme atlases of the fixed-target stack H^bal and does not transfer verbatim to a general etale scheme atlas S of Hbar^bal=[H^bal/PGL_2]. The packet convention is W_5:=(O_{P(E^vee)}(2) tensor gamma^*O_{P^1}(-5))|_C, the f_2=5 summand of (O(2) tensor gamma^*F^vee)|_C; the construction therefore uses the odd twist O(5) on the target. Over such an S the tautological target is the P^1-bundle associated to the classifying PGL_2-torsor, i.e. a Severi-Brauer scheme of relative dimension one. Ordinary O_P(d) exists on that target if and only if d is even or the image of the torsor in Br(S)[2] vanishes (Lichtenbaum sequence; Kollár: O_P(1) exists as an ordinary line bundle iff the Severi-Brauer variety is isomorphic to projective space; on a non-split conic the ordinary Picard group is generated by O(2)). Hence W_5, L:=W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1}, and pi_*L need not exist as ordinary (untwisted) sheaves on S, and Zariski-local triviality of the Abel-Jacobi P^2-bundle is not licensed by citing CLM-0112-8 unchanged. This does not assert that the Brauer class is nonzero on every atlas of Hbar^bal, and does not assert that a general Severi-Brauer conic arises as a g^1_4 target. The relative complete linear system of the corresponding twisted invertible sheaf is a Severi-Brauer scheme of relative dimension two, so a dimension count 15+2=17 can be repaired at that level; alternatively, the classifying morphism to M_{6,6} is PGL_2-invariant (CLM-0112-7), so the image of the H^bal-level ordered reduced-support model of dimension 18+2=20 (FND-0181) factors through a stack quotient of dimension 20-3=17, consistent with dim Hbar^bal=18-3=15. Neither repair is supplied by citing CLM-0112-8, and neither proves equality dim Y=17. Attempts that need a 17-dimensional model must write one of these repairs (or an SL_2/GL_2 lift on which O(1) exists) rather than cite CLM-0112-8 unchanged. Compatible with FND-0181's proved bound dim Y<=20 and with CLM-0112-8 on its H^bal-atlas scope.

adjudication_reason: Mandatory inspection of ATT-0123 and REV-0175 confirms that the contested passage is REV-0175's proposed biconditional, not ATT-0123's already acknowledged gap CLM-0123-3. ATT-0123 proves only that a Tate source A has Tate quotient T_Z; it neither proves A Tate nor computes T_Z. The candidate's categorical core is correct after correction. Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Lemma 4.2.3, states semisimplicity and proves that a polarized homogeneous Hodge structure splits off any subobject by its orthogonal complement; specialized to a point, every epimorphism of polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures splits. The source record's SHA-256 is over the 20,222 UTF-8 bytes of the live fetched textual extraction of the public PDF, not a purported digest of the server's raw PDF binary. Cross-checking FND-0180, FND-0185, and FND-0033 supplies the geometric quotient, purity, and polarizability hypotheses. Several corrections are required: q should be attributed to FND-0180 and FND-0185, with FND-0168(3) providing localization, rather than to the interpretive clause FND-0168(3a); polarizability of A comes from FND-0185, not the narrower geometric scope of FND-0033; a splitting of q exists but is noncanonical and is unnecessary for the biconditional; only the decomposition into simple isotypic components is canonical. Because morphisms between nonisomorphic simple objects in a semisimple category vanish, q carries the Q(8)-isotypic and complementary parts to the corresponding parts of T_Z, and surjectivity gives q(A_nonTate)=(T_Z)_nonTate. Thus the biconditional is valid. It does not contradict FND-0168, FND-0185, or FND-0188, and the atlas, family-base, and product-model examples do not compute q(A_nonTate). However, the candidate's proof-lane wording overclaims: A_nonTate contained in ker(q) is equivalent to the desired conclusion that T_Z is Tate, not an independently checkable sufficient hypothesis that discharges it. The result is a categorical sharpening and exact reformulation of FND-0185, not a separate obstruction or new geometric input, so it should be merged into FND-0185 rather than promoted independently.
statement: Let Y be a closed substack of X=M_{6,6}, A:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q), T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), and let q:A->T_Z be the surjection of FND-0180/FND-0168(3a) onto the kernel-form term. By FND-0185, A is a pure polarizable Q-Hodge structure of weight -16, and polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of fixed weight form a semisimple abelian category (FND-0033). Hence q splits, A is isomorphic to ker(q) direct-sum T_Z, and morphisms preserve canonical isotypic components, so writing A = A_Tate direct-sum A_nonTate for the canonical splitting into the Q(8)-isotypic part and its complement one gets (T_Z)_nonTate = q(A_nonTate). Therefore T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8) if and only if A_nonTate is contained in ker(q). Two lane consequences: a C66-TATE-SUPPORT proof routed through the verified interface source may replace the FND-0185 hypothesis 'A is Tate' by the strictly weaker and canonical 'A_nonTate is contained in ker(q)', and a C66-CEX-LOCAL / C66-CEX-SURVIVE disproof through the same interface must exhibit a non-Tate isotypic summand of A with nonzero image in T, which is the theorem's survival clause in checkable form. Exhibiting a non-Tate class anywhere in A, in an atlas, in a family base, or in a standalone product model settles neither lane.
