statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let X be a smooth complex scheme or Deligne-Mumford stack of pure dimension d, and let Y be a closed finite-type subscheme or closed substack. Mixed Hodge structures on Borel-Moore homology are those of Deligne, and morphisms are strict for the weight filtration. For smooth X the lowest-weight piece W_{-k}H^{BM}_k(X;Q) is pure of weight -k: geometric Poincare duality identifies H^{BM}_k(X) with H_c^{2d-k}(X)(d), whose weights are at most -k, equivalently under the Hom convention H^{BM}_k:=Hom(H_c^k,Q) used by Canning-Larson-Payne. Purity of this piece, the numerical coincidence of Borel-Moore degree k with weight -k, and the mere existence of a closed support Y do not force the image of W_{-k}H^{BM}_k(Y;Q) -> W_{-k}H^{BM}_k(X;Q) to be a Tate Hodge structure. In particular, matching the C66-001 ledger (d,k)=(21,16): let A be a complex abelian variety of dimension 9, let X=A x P^{12} (smooth projective of dimension 21), and let Y=A x {pt} (closed embedding of codimension 12). Then H^*(A;Q) is the exterior algebra on H^1(A;Q) as Hodge structures, H^1(A) is pure of weight 1 with types (1,0) and (0,1) of dimension 9, and H^2(A) is therefore pure of weight 2 with types (2,0), (1,1), (0,2) and h^{2,0}=binomial(9,2)=36 nonzero. Kunneth together with the Gysin map of a point {pt} subset P^{12}, whose class generates H^{24}(P^{12};Q) isomorphic to Q(-12), realises H^2(A)(-12) as a direct summand of H^{26}(X;Q). Geometric Poincare duality with twist (21) identifies this summand with H^2(A)(9) inside W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), and the Borel-Moore pushforward H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) -> H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q) is an isomorphism onto that summand. The Tate-twist convention V(m)^{p,q}=V^{p+m,q+m} (weight decreased by 2m) sends the types of H^2(A) to (-7,-9), (-8,-8), and (-9,-7) on H^2(A)(9), which is polarizable, pure of weight -16, and not a finite direct sum of Q(8). Consequently any argument for the C66-TATE-SUPPORT theorem at (g,n)=(6,6), that the named kernel-form subobject T_Z=im(W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q)->T) of T:=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8), cannot conclude from purity, Borel-Moore degree 16, weight -16, and closed support in a smooth 21-fold alone. Additional geometric input is required, such as: (i) dim Y<=8, which forces W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) itself to vanish if dim Y<8 or to be a finite direct sum of Q(8) if Y has dimension 8 (top Borel-Moore); (ii) Tate type of the relevant lowest-weight groups on residual strata of dimensions 9 through 16; or (iii) vanishing of every non-Tate summand of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y;Q) in the map to T. This statement does not assert that the named T_Z of M_{6,6} is non-Tate, does not refute RED-0001, and does not supply a Gysin computation on the Casnati-Ekedahl classifying-image closure.

Since the coarse space of X is quasi-projective, each (O cap C_a)^c is quasi-projective and irreducible, hence contains a dense affine open A_a; a finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine, so S_j (the substack over A) is smooth of pure dimension d_j with affine coarse space. S_j is open in Y^(j), so Y^(j+1) := (Y^(j) minus S_j)_red is closed in Y^(j) hence in X, and S_j = Y^(j) cap (X minus Y^(j+1)) is closed in X minus Y^(j+1). Y^(j+1) is the union of the lower-dimensional components with the proper closed subsets C_a minus S_j, so dim Y^(j+1) <= d_j - 1; strict decrease of a nonnegative integer forces termination. Confirmed, and confirmed to use no dimension bound for Y and no 'open of an affine stack is affine' step (affineness is asserted of the coarse space only, which is exactly the archive constraint at issue).
(ii) Lemma 2: V_{j+1} minus S_j = V_j holds because Y^(j) = Y^(j+1) disjoint-union S_j as sets, so (S2) applies to the smooth pair (V_{j+1}, S_j) of pure codimension c_j = 21 - n_j. Arithmetic re-checked: 26 - 2(21 - n_j) = 2n_j - 16; the twist (-c_j) raises the weight floor of H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) from 2n_j-16 to (2n_j-16) + 2(21-n_j) = 26, so W_{26} of the twisted group equals (W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q))(-c_j); and (-c_j) + 21 = n_j with final weight (2n_j-16) - 2n_j = -16. W_{26} is exact by (S5), so it carries ker(H^{26}(V_{j+1}) -> H^{26}(V_j)) = im(H^{2n_j-16}(S_j)(-c_j) -> H^{26}(V_{j+1})) to the corresponding kernel and preserves the surjection onto the image. A_{j+1} subset A_j because the opens enlarge and restriction is functorial; ker(A_j -> W_{26}H^{26}(V_{j+1})(21)) = A_j cap A_{j+1} = A_{j+1}; so A_j/A_{j+1} embeds in a quotient of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j) and is a subquotient of it. A_0 = T_Z by CLM-0120-4 (V_0 = U_Y) and A_N = 0 (V_N = X). Confirmed. Crucially the artifact claims only a subquotient, never an identification with a supports group, so REV-0180's first attack prong and the FND-0168(3a)/(3b) hazard are genuinely avoided; I independently confirm that the connecting map from H^{25}(V_j) can be nonzero in weight 26 and that the weaker subquotient claim is what the argument actually needs.
(iii) n_j <= 7 gives 2n_j - 16 <= -2 < 0. n_j >= 17 gives 2n_j - 16 - n_j = n_j - 16 >= 1, so the degree strictly exceeds dim S_j = dim S_j^c; (S3) reduces to the affine coarse space and (S4) kills it. n_j = 8 gives degree 0, H^0 pure of weight 0 and a finite direct sum of Q, so the graded piece is a subquotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) and hence such a sum by (S6). Confirmed, including that these are degree comparisons, not appeals to smallness of dimension, so the archive constraint 'positive-codimension strata cannot contribute solely because they have smaller dimension' is not walked.
(iv) Strict decrease gives at most one stratum per dimension; {8,...,16} has nine elements and {9,...,16} has eight, so the counts 'at most nine surviving pieces, at most eight residual' are correct. (S6) supplies a noncanonical splitting of the finite filtration inside a semisimple abelian category, an honest Hodge-structure isomorphism per FND-0033, not a semisimplification. Confirmed.
(v) Sufficiency confirmed, including the twist identity Q(8-n_j)(n_j) = Q(8).

(A) 'the only substantive antecedent ... is Tate control of residual strata of dimensions 9 through 16' conflates two different conditions. pre_adjudication_statement: For the ATT-0120 kernel T_Z inside T = W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), the reduced closed support Y can be peeled into finitely many smooth affine-coarse strata with strictly decreasing dimensions, producing a decreasing kernel filtration A_j whose graded pieces are subquotients of W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j). Strata with n_j <= 7 or n_j >= 17 contribute zero, strata with n_j = 8 contribute only finite direct sums of Q(8), and semisimplicity splits T_Z noncanonically as the direct sum of the surviving pieces with 8 <= n_j <= 16. Thus the only substantive antecedent for T_Z to be a finite direct sum of Q(8) is Tate control of residual strata of dimensions 9 through 16; no dimension bound on Y, no Gysin map for Y or Z, and no closed embedding of Z is required.

The recorded case d = 21, m = 26 gives the thresholds n_j <= 7, n_j >= 17 and the Q(8) endpoint at n_j = 8.

statement:
SCOPE. Work over C with Q-coefficients at (g,n) = (6,6). Let X := M_{6,6}, the smooth separated Deligne-Mumford stack of smooth genus-six curves with six ordered marked points, of pure dimension d = 21, with finite inertia and quasi-projective coarse space. Let T := W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), identified by Poincare duality (FND-0001) with W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21), pure polarizable of weight -16. Let Y be the atlas-independent reduced closed substack of X named by the verified C66-SUPPORT-INTERFACE datum (ATT-0120/CLM-0120-2), and let T_Z := ker(r_T) be its named subobject of T, where r_T : T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y;Q)(21) is W_{26} of ordinary open restriction twisted by (21) (ATT-0120/CLM-0120-3, CLM-0120-4). No dimension, purity, irreducibility, regular-immersion, or lci property of Y is assumed or used. Call a chain Y = Y^(0) superset Y^(1) superset ... superset Y^(N) = empty of reduced closed substacks of X admissible if the dimensions n_j := dim Y^(j) strictly decrease and, for every j, S_j := Y^(j) minus Y^(j+1) is smooth of pure dimension n_j, has affine coarse space, and is closed in X minus Y^(j+1).

LOAD-BEARING IMPORTED INPUTS, to be carried by every downstream citation. (S1) Ordinary Q-cohomology of smooth separated finite-type DM stacks over C carries functorial mixed Hodge structures with H^m of weights at least m. (S2) The purity (Gysin) long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures for a smooth closed substack of pure codimension c in a smooth DM stack. (S1) and (S2) are stack-level statements imported from V-manifold/orbifold Hodge theory via an etale atlas and Q-descent; they are not proved in the originating artifact. (S3) Rational coarse comparison H^*(S;Q) = H^*(S^c;Q) for separated finite-inertia DM stacks over C (Behrend, Cohomology of Stacks, Proposition 36). (S4) Artin vanishing H^k(A;Q) = 0 for k > dim A for a possibly singular complex affine variety A (Esnault, Variation on Artin's vanishing theorem, Theorem 2.1). (S5) Strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures for W, hence exactness of W_m. (S6) Semisimplicity of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures of a fixed weight (FND-0033).

CLAIMS. (1) An admissible chain for Y exists. It is constructed by removing, at each stage, the components of Y^(j) of dimension below n_j, the pairwise intersections of the top-dimensional components, and Sing(Y^(j)), then taking the substack lying over a dense affine open of the coarse space of each remaining top-dimensional component; Y^(j+1) is the reduced complement. The construction uses no dimension bound for Y (in particular FND-0181 and FND-0187 are not load-bearing here) and asserts affineness only of stratum coarse spaces, never of a stratum stack or of an open of an affine stack.

(2) For every admissible chain, A_j := ker(T -> W_{26}H^{26}(X minus Y^(j);Q)(21)) is a finite decreasing filtration of T by sub-Hodge structures with A_0 = T_Z and A_N = 0, and each graded piece A_j/A_{j+1} is a subquotient of the pure polarizable weight -16 Hodge structure W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q)(n_j). This follows from (S2) applied to the smooth pair (X minus Y^(j+1), S_j) in degree 26 and codimension 21 - n_j, exactness of W_{26} by (S5), and the weight bound of (S1), using 26 - 2(21-n_j) = 2n_j - 16 and (-(21-n_j)) + 21 = n_j. Only a subquotient is claimed; no supports group is named, and no supports group is identified with its image in T, so the FND-0168(3a)/(3b) hazard is not incurred.

(3) For every admissible chain, A_j/A_{j+1} = 0 when n_j <= 7, because the ordinary degree 2n_j - 16 is negative; A_j/A_{j+1} = 0 when n_j >= 17, because then 2n_j - 16 > n_j = dim S_j = dim S_j^c and (S3) followed by (S4) on the affine coarse space kills H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q); and A_j/A_{j+1} is a finite direct sum of Q(8), possibly zero, when n_j = 8, being a subquotient of H^0(S_j;Q)(8) and hence such a sum by (S6). Both vanishings are degree comparisons, not inferences from smallness of stratum dimension.

(4) For every admissible chain, T_Z is isomorphic, not necessarily canonically, to the direct sum of the graded pieces A_j/A_{j+1} indexed by those j with n_j in {8, ..., 16}, the splitting being supplied by (S6). Strict decrease of the n_j means at most one stratum occurs per dimension, so at most nine pieces survive, of which at most eight lie in the range 9 <= n_j <= 16. T_Z depends only on the pair (X, Y) (ATT-0120/CLM-0120-6), but the individual residual strata S_j with 9 <= n_j <= 16 depend on the chosen chain; no chain is canonical and none is needed.

(5) T_Z is a finite direct sum of Q(8) if and only if, for one admissible chain -- equivalently, by (4), for every admissible chain -- every graded piece A_j/A_{j+1} with 9 <= n_j <= 16 is a finite direct sum of Q(8). The 'if' direction is the sufficiency implication proved in the originating artifact. The 'only if' direction holds because A_j is contained in A_0 = T_Z for every j, so each graded piece is a subquotient of T_Z, and by (S6) every subquotient of a finite direct sum of Q(8) is again one.

(6) A strictly stronger, merely sufficient antecedent. If W_{2n_j-16}H^{2n_j-16}(S_j;Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(8-n_j) for every residual stratum, then by the twist identity Q(8-n_j)(n_j) = Q(8), clause (2) and (S6), each residual graded piece is a finite direct sum of Q(8) and clause (5) applies. This stratum-level condition is NOT necessary: the graded piece is only a subquotient of that group, so a non-Tate stratum group is compatible with Tate graded pieces. The residual obligation isolated by this result is therefore Tate control of the graded pieces A_j/A_{j+1} for 9 <= n_j <= 16, which is the assigned obligation of C66-TATE-SUPPORT; stratum-level Tate control is one sufficient route to it.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT AVOIDED. The argument does use the purity (Gysin) long exact sequence for the constructed smooth pairs (X minus Y^(j+1), S_j), as the assigned theorem expressly permits. What it avoids is any Gysin map, fundamental class, regular immersion, closed embedding, expected-codimension bookkeeping, or codimension shift for Y itself or for any model of Z inside X (FND-0052, FND-0168(5)), and any Borel-Moore or compact-support mixed Hodge formalism on the singular stack Y (FND-0165), replaced throughout by ordinary cohomology of smooth stacks.

NOT ASSERTED. No Tate type for T_Z or for T; clause (5) is an equivalence between two open conditions, not a determination of either. No lower bound on T_Z: T_Z = 0 is compatible with clauses (1) through (6), all direct sums then being empty. No support exhaustion T_Z = T. No preferred admissible chain and no chain-independence of the residual strata. No realization of an adjudicated proper non-Tate model as a single admissible stratum, a proper support being inadmissible because it is not affine. No assembly of complementary target terms, and nothing about RED-0001.

GENERALITY. Nothing above is specific to (6,6). For any reduced closed substack Y of a smooth separated finite-type DM stack X over C of pure dimension d with finite inertia and quasi-projective coarse space, and any even ordinary degree m, the same construction and argument give a filtration whose graded pieces are subquotients of W_{m-2(d-n_j)}H^{m-2(d-n_j)}(S_j;Q)(n_j - d + m/2), vanishing for n_j < d - m/2 and for n_j > 2d - m, and of type a finite direct sum of Q(d - m/2) at n_j = d - m/2. The recorded case d = 21, m = 26 yields the thresholds n_j <= 7 and n_j >= 17 and the Q(8) endpoint at n_j = 8.

Math. 35 (1968), for E_2-degeneration of the smooth proper map C^n -> M_g (CLP bibliography [12], Proposition 2.16), relative Kunneth, and the pi_2 projectors of Petersen-Tavakol-Yin, Ann. Sci. Ec. Norm. Super. 54 (2021), Sections 5.1 and 5.2.2, to identify Psi with i_s=2 summands modulo Phi; it does not use Deninger-Murre abelian-scheme projectors. statement: Let g>=2, n>=1, and work with rational coefficients on Deligne-Mumford stacks. Write C^n for the n-fold fibre product of the closed universal curve pi:C->M_g, and set k=vcd(M_{g,n})=4g-4+n. The open immersion M_{g,n} subset C^n induces a surjection W_k H^k(C^n;Q) ->> W_k H^k(M_{g,n};Q) by Deligne's identification of the lowest-weight piece in degree k. Canning-Larson-Payne Lemma 3.1(a) then supplies an isomorphism of pure weight-k Hodge structures W_k H^k(M_{g,n};Q)/(Phi_{g,n}^k+Psi_{g,n}^k) congruent to the direct sum over |lambda|=n of W_k H^{k-n}(M_g;V_lambda) tensor V_{lambda^T}, where Phi_{g,n}^k=sum_i pi_i^* W_k H^k(M_{g,n-1};Q) and Psi_{g,n}^k=sum_i psi_i Phi_{g,n}^{k-2}; the identification of Psi with the Kunneth summands having some i_s=2, modulo Phi, is the published pi_2-projector statement of that lemma (Petersen-Tavakol-Yin), not a fibrewise canonical-class slogan. Harer's virtual cohomological dimension gives H^p(M_g;L)=0 for every Q-local system L and every p>vcd(M_g)=4g-5 (equivalently: cohomological dimension of a torsion-free finite-index subgroup, transferred by rational Hochschild-Serre). Hence every multi-index i in {0,1,2}^n with |i|<=n has base degree k-|i|>=4g-4>4g-5 and the primitive quotient vanishes. Independently k=vcd(M_{g,n-1})+1, so Phi_{g,n}^k=0. Therefore W_{vcd} H^{vcd}(M_{g,n};Q)=Psi_{g,n}^{vcd}=sum_i psi_i sum_j pi_j^* W_{vcd-2} H^{vcd-2}(M_{g,n-1};Q). The comparison vcd(M_{g,n})-n=4g-4=vcd(M_g)+1 is independent of n>=1. Each psi_i is algebraic of type Q(-1). Whenever n-1<=c(g) in the published CKgP table c(3)=c(4)=11, c(5)=7, c(6)=5, c(7)=3, Canning-Larson-Payne Proposition 4.5 implies that W_{vcd-2} H^{vcd-2}(M_{g,n-1};Q) is algebraic of Tate type, and semisimplicity of polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of a single weight realises W_{vcd} H^{vcd}(M_{g,n};Q) as a finite direct sum of Q(-vcd/2). In particular, at the campaign pair (g,n)=(6,6) one has k=26, n-1=5=c(6), and W_26 H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-13). The same peel does not kill the primitive term in degree vcd-1 and does not apply where no published c(g) is available.

pre_adjudication_statement: On the n-fold fibre product C^n of the universal curve over M_g, the class omega_s=pr_s^* c_1(omega_{C/M_g}) is not homogeneous for the Kunneth multi-index: it decomposes as a_s+b_s+c_s with a_s in H^2(M_g) (slot value 0), b_s in H^1(M_g;V) (slot value 1) and c_s the R^2 component (slot value 2, coefficient 2g-2). Only c_s carries the i_s=0 to i_s=2 isomorphism, so any argument of the form 'multiplication by psi_s spans the i_s=2 summands modulo the summands with some slot 0' must dispose of the slot-1 cross term b_s. Two disposals are valid: H^1(Mod_g;H_1(Sigma_g;Q))=0 for g>=2 (Morita: the integral group is Z/(2g-2)), which makes b_s=0 identically; or a downward induction on |i| using A_i=c_s B_{i'} inside omega_s B_{i'}+A_{i'}+A_{i''} with |i''|=|i|-1 and the base case A_j=0 for k-|j|>vcd(M_g).

scope.object: n-fold fibre product of the closed universal curve over M_g

statement: Work over Q with g>=2. Let pi:C->M_g be the universal closed curve and C^n its n-fold fibre product. Write omega_s=pr_s^* c_1(omega_{C/M_g}); on C this is the class psi_1 of Petersen-Tavakol-Yin, and its restriction to the open configuration space M_{g,n} subset C^n is the tautological psi class. The Leray-Kunneth decomposition of the smooth proper map C^n->M_g splits H^*(C^n) into summands H^{k-|i|}(M_g; tensor_s R^{i_s} pi_* Q) indexed by i in {0,1,2}^n. The class omega_s is not homogeneous for this multi-index: it decomposes as a_s+b_s+c_s with a_s in H^2(M_g) (slot value 0), b_s in H^1(M_g; R^1 pi_* Q) (slot value 1), and c_s in H^0(M_g; R^2 pi_* Q) (slot value 2). The fibre restriction of omega_s is the canonical class of degree 2g-2, so c_s equals 2g-2 times the generator of R^2 pi_* Q isomorphic to Q(-1). Only c_s induces the isomorphism from the i_s=0 summand onto the i_s=2 summand; cup-product with a_s preserves the multi-index while raising base degree by 2, and cup-product with b_s raises the s-th slot by 1. Consequently any argument of the form 'modulo summands with some slot 0, multiplication by psi_s (or omega_s) spans the i_s=2 summands because the class restricts to a nonzero multiple of the fibre canonical class' must dispose of the slot-1 cross term b_s. Three disposals are valid over Q. (1) The slot-1 summand vanishes: H^1(M_g; R^1 pi_* Q) isomorphic to H^1(Mod_g; H^1(Sigma_g; Q))=0 for g>=2. This is the rational form of Morita's theorem H_1(Mod_g; H_1(Sigma_g; Z)) isomorphic to Z/(2g-2) for g>=2, recorded as H^1(Gamma_g, H_Q)=0 by Hain-Reed; equivalently H^2(C; Q) has basis {lambda, omega}, so the H^1(M_g; V) summand of H^2(C) is zero, hence b_s=0 identically and modulo slot-0 summands multiplication by omega_s coincides with multiplication by c_s. (2) The relative Chow-Kunneth projector of Petersen-Tavakol-Yin, pi_2 = psi_2/(2g-2) - kappa_1/(2(2g-2)^2), already lies in the Q-span of a psi class and a pullback from M_g, so it realises the i_s=0 to i_s=2 isomorphism inside Psi+Phi; Canning-Larson-Payne Lemma 3.1 invokes these projectors. (3) Downward induction on |i|: writing A_i for the multi-index summand of W_k H^k(C^n) and B_{i'} for the class with slot s reset to 0, one has A_i = c_s B_{i'} inside omega_s B_{i'} + A_{i'} + A_{i''} with |i''|=|i|-1, using the base case A_j=0 whenever k-|j| exceeds vcd(M_g)=4g-5. Disposal (3) applies in particular at the campaign point (g,n,k)=(6,6,26), where every multi-index with |i|<=6 has base degree at least 20>19. Thus the containment of i_s=2 summands in Phi+Psi holds over Q, but a fibre-restriction sentence does not by itself justify it.

statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let g>=2 and n>=2. Let pi:C->M_g be the universal closed curve of genus g, and let C^n be its n-fold fibre product over M_g, a smooth separated finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack. Identify M_{g,n} with the open complement in C^n of the union of pairwise diagonals. Then, for every integer k, restriction along this open immersion is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures inducing a surjection W_k H^k(C^n;Q) ->> W_k H^k(M_{g,n};Q). The surjection follows from Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Corollaire 3.2.17: for a smooth separated scheme (and, with Q-coefficients, a smooth finite-type Deligne-Mumford stack via a scheme atlas), W_k H^k equals the image of H^k of any smooth proper compactification; a smooth proper compactification of C^n is simultaneously a compactification of the open M_{g,n}, so both lowest-weight groups equal the image of the same compactification cohomology and restriction factors that image. Consequently W_k H^k(M_{g,n};Q) is a quotient of W_k H^k(C^n;Q), and any generation, vanishing, or Tate-type upper bound on the source yields the same upper bound on the target. Identifying the kernel of restriction on W_k, including Gysin exactness for the diagonal divisors and the symplectic Schur-Weyl or traceless decomposition of (R^1 pi_* Q)^{tensor n}, is needed only to upgrade the surjection to an isomorphism (Canning-Larson-Payne Lemma 3.1(a)). This surjection does not assert that Kunneth summands of H^*(C^n) are summands of R^* f_* Q for the non-proper map f:M_{g,n}->M_g; that identification remains invalid, because the fibres are configuration spaces of distinct points and R^1 of the punctured curve is mixed of weights 1 and 2. In particular the statement applies at the campaign case (g,n,k)=(6,6,26).

adjudication_reason: The mandatory origin check found that ATT-0135, CLM-0135-1 and CLM-0135-2 use the published primitive-quotient formula, while REV-0185 identifies three possible attacks: applicability of vcd to nontrivial symplectic coefficients, the W_26 indexing on degree-20 local-system cohomology, and the informal psi-versus-R^2 projector sketch. The final published Canning-Larson-Payne article resolves the latter two directly: Lemma 3.1(a) states the quotient is the direct sum of W_k H^{k-n}(M_g;mathbb V_lambda) tensor V_{lambda^T}, and its proof uses the closed universal curve, smooth-proper Leray degeneration, the all-R^1 Kunneth term, Petersen-Tavakol-Yin projectors, and symplectic contractions. Thus (g,n,k)=(6,6,26) gives ordinary degree 20 and weight index 26; it does not involve the mixed R^1 of the punctured forgetful map discussed in FND-0037. Church-Farb-Putman explicitly record Harer's result vcd(Mod_g)=4g-5 and the consequent vanishing H^i(Mod_g;V tensor Q)=0 for i>4g-5 and arbitrary Mod_g-modules V. Formally, choose a torsion-free normal finite-index subgroup Gamma of Mod_6 with cd(Gamma)=19. Then H^20(Gamma;mathbb V_lambda)=0, and Hochschild-Serre for the finite quotient Mod_6/Gamma collapses over Q because finite-group invariants are exact, giving H^20(Mod_6;mathbb V_lambda)=0. Hence W_26 of that zero group is zero. This is compatible with FND-0035: FND-0035 only blocks an above-vcd argument at the target degree 26 on Mod_{6,6}, whereas the present application is degree 20>19 on Mod_6. It also does not contradict RED-0001, THM-0005, or any claim listed in contradicts_claim_ids. No equivalent adjudicated finding was found, so merging is unwarranted. The finding is promoted only for the primitive quotient; ATT-0135's later conclusions still require its separate Phi-vanishing and CKgP/Tate inputs.

scope.object: primitive quotient of the lowest-weight ordinary cohomology of the complex Deligne-Mumford stack M_{6,6}

statement: Work over C with rational singular cohomology and its mixed Hodge structure. For g>=2, let pi_i:M_{g,n}->M_{g,n-1} forget the ith marking, define Phi_{g,n}^k=sum_i pi_i^*W_k H^k(M_{g,n-1};Q), and define Psi_{g,n}^k=sum_i psi_i Phi_{g,n}^{k-2}. Canning-Larson-Payne Lemma 3.1(a) gives an isomorphism of pure rational Hodge structures W_k H^k(M_{g,n};Q)/(Phi_{g,n}^k+Psi_{g,n}^k) isomorphic to the direct sum over partitions lambda with |lambda|=n and length(lambda)<=g of W_k H^{k-n}(M_g;mathbb V_lambda) tensor V_{lambda^T}, where mathbb V_lambda is the weight-|lambda| rational symplectic local system and V_{lambda^T} is the corresponding rational S_n-module with trivial Hodge structure. At (g,n,k)=(6,6,26), every underlying group H^20(M_6;mathbb V_lambda) vanishes: stack cohomology identifies it with H^20(Mod_6;mathbb V_lambda), and a torsion-free normal finite-index subgroup of Mod_6 has cohomological dimension vcd(Mod_6)=4*6-5=19; Hochschild-Serre for the finite quotient is exact over Q. Consequently W_26 H^26(M_{6,6};Q)/(Phi_{6,6}^26+Psi_{6,6}^26)=0 as a pure rational Hodge structure. This conclusion concerns only the primitive quotient and does not infer vanishing at degree 26 from vcd(Mod_{6,6})=26.
